children.text: māṣaparṇabhṛtīyasaṃbandho'pi pūrvavat ayaṃ gṛṣṭim ca ekavāraprarāūtām
children.translated_text: The connection with the Māṣaparṇabhṛtīya section is as before; here too a gṛṣṭi cow is one that has calved once.

children.text: rasadoṣaprabhāvadvārā dravyavikāraprabhāvaniścayo na sartara dravye vikāre cetyāhan a tvevaṃ rkhlu savraīreti
children.translated_text: The determination of the effect of a modification of a substance is made through the effects of <s>rasa</s> and <s>doṣa</s>; but not in every case, whether of substance or of modification. Therefore he says, 'Not indeed in this way in all cases ...'.
Here, by the expression 'having four teats,' he states and shows the cause as one with the complete set of four teats.
This extends from the word 'for' and so on up to 'it can be ascertained.'
In 'vikṛti, rohiṇī,' the phrase refers to things that are unevenly combined, and 'rohiṇī' means red in color.
The expression 'those combined by alteration and unequal combination' means both those combined by alteration and those combined unequally.

children.text: samavetānāmiti lardhvaśṛṅgatvaṃ militānāṃ viśuddha rasānāṃ bahukṣīrāyā doṣāṇāṃ eva ca
children.translated_text: 'Of those combined' should be understood as referring to the joined pure rasas, to their upward prominence in the corrupt reading, and also to the doṣas of a cow rich in milk.
This is to be known from the wording 'there is.'

children.text: tatra ikṣvādeti rasasya ikṣudaṇḍa vikṛtisamavāyo bhakṣā
children.translated_text: There, in the example beginning with sugarcane, the altered combination of <s>rasa</s> belongs to the sugarcane stalk as something eaten.

children.text: yathā madhure taṇḍauīyake madhuro hi prakṛtyā snehavṛṣyatvaāikaraḥ taṇḍulīyake tu vikṛtisamavetatvena tanna kearoi
children.translated_text: For example, in sweet taṇḍulīyaka: by nature the sweet taste produces unctuousness and virility, but in taṇḍulīyaka, because it is present through altered combination, it does not do that.
Unequally combined rasas, however, are illustrated in cases such as sesame connected with arjuna, where leaves of the arjuna tree have been eaten.

children.text: kaṣāyakaṭutiktamadhurāḥ yadi hīme rasāḥ samayā mātrayā sama etāḥ syustatastilo'pi pitta9ślṣmaharast ridoṣaharo vā syāt pittakaphakarastvayaṃ tenātra rasānāṃ kvacit kartṛtbvma kartṛtvaṃ cy kvaciditi vaiṣabmamu jnnyate
children.translated_text: Astringent, pungent, bitter, and sweet: if these rasas were present together in equal measure, then sesame too would remove pitta and kapha, or would remove all three doṣas. But this sesame increases pitta and kapha; therefore here an inequality is known, since rasas sometimes act and sometimes do not act.

children.text: nānātmadkāāmi ikṣvādā htydihetutrayaṃ vā tu arjunādā vi vā ṛtisamavāyavieamasamavāyayore māṣaparṇabhṛtā vopamlabhakam
children.translated_text: The three causes beginning with diversity, seen in examples such as sugarcane, or again in examples such as arjuna, are illustrative of altered combination and unequal combination, as in the Māṣaparṇabhṛtīya context.
Thus there are three alternative interpretations.

children.text: tena payaḥ nānātmaka śṛtamaśṛtaṃ ptādi veti tyādibhirv dvī ikṛtisamavāyaviṣamasamavāyau yogau
children.translated_text: Accordingly, milk as diverse, boiled or unboiled, and so on, together with the other examples, gives the two conjunctions called altered combination and unequal combination.
These two are present.

children.text: nānātma śarkarākṣaudrasarpirbhiryuktaṃ ānāmiti taditi nānārūpahetujāaeiānāṃḥtena tṛtīyaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Diverse' means joined with sugar, honey, and ghee; by the phrase 'of those,' namely those produced from causes of many forms, the third cause is indicated.

children.text: hetubhedabalādeva rasado ṣayorvikṛto viṣamo vā melako bhavatītyarthaḥ
children.translated_text: The meaning is that, by the force of difference in causes, the mixture of <s>rasa</s> and <s>doṣa</s> becomes either altered or unequal.

children.text: kivā etatprayogo'pi nānātma jatkarṇe kānāmiti tasyāḥ nānāpramāṇānām
children.translated_text: Or this application too concerns diversity; in the phrase referring to things of various measures, it denotes their differing proportions.

children.text: kṣīraṃ śarkarākṣaudrayuttṃ vā kevalaṃ śṛtama śṛtaṃ bā iita ||
children.translated_text: Milk may be mixed with sugar and honey, or be plain; it may be boiled or unboiled, and so forth.

children.text: evaṃ ca nānāpramāṇatvaṃ viṣamasama vāye hetuḥ
children.translated_text: Thus difference of measure is a cause of unequal combination.
'And impaired by one another' means whose qualities have been mutually harmed.

children.text: parasparaguāāopaghātastu yadyapi doṣāṇā prāyo nāseva tathā'pyadṛṣṭavaśāt kvācedbhavatātie jñeyaṃ rasānāṃ tu pravalenā yopaghāto bhavatyeva
children.translated_text: Although mutual impairment of qualities generally does not occur among the doṣas, still it should be understood that it sometimes occurs through an unseen cause; among rasas, however, impairment by the stronger one certainly occurs.

children.text: anyaiśca vikalpanairiti anyaiśca bhedakaiḥ tatra rasasya bhedakāḥ svararakalkādayaḥḥ ekasthaīva hi dravyasya ka tpanāāvaśaṣeṇa guṇāntarāṇi bhavānīta
children.translated_text: 'And by other differentiations' means by other distinguishing factors. Among rasas the differentiators are fresh juice, paste, and the like; for the very same substance has other qualities depending on a particular mode of preparation.

children.text: doṣasya tu dūṣyāntarā ṇyeva guṇāntarayogādbhedakāni bhavānta
children.translated_text: For a doṣa, however, other dūṣyas themselves become differentiators because of conjunction with other qualities.
As it has been said: 'The very same aggravated doṣa, because of a particular difference in its arising,
and also when it has gone to another site, produces diseases.'

children.text: asminvyākhyāne rasānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ ca ya utkarṣāpakarṣakṛto viṣamasamavāyaḥ pṛthagucyate sa na yutvateḥ yato viṣamasamavāye'pyutkṛṣṭasya rasasya tathā doṣasya co tkṛṣṭā guṇā apakṛṣṭastha cāpakṛṣṭā guṇā bhavantīti kṛtvā'vayavapra bhāvānanumānenaiva samudāyaprabhāvānumānaṃ śakyam
children.translated_text: In this explanation, the unequal combination of rasas and doṣas caused by increase and decrease is stated separately; that is not appropriate. For even in unequal combination, the superior qualities belong to the superior rasa or doṣa, and the inferior qualities to the inferior one, so the effect of the aggregate can be inferred from the effects of its components.

children.text: athocyeta viṣamamelake rasasya doṣasya ca na ta eva guṇā utkṛṣṭā apakṛṣṭā vā bhavānita kitu guṇāntarameva bhavati hanta tarhi vikṛta evāyaṃ samavāyo visadṛśakāryakārāātvāt
children.translated_text: If it is said that in an unequal mixture the very same qualities of the rasa or doṣa are not superior or inferior, but that an entirely different quality arises, then indeed this is altered combination, because it produces an unlike effect.

children.text: tadevaṃ ṇadarśāādanyathā vyākhyāyateyatdvividho melako bhavati rasānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ ca prakṛtyanuguāḥ prakṛtyananuguṇaśca tatra yo militānāṃ prākṛta guṇānupamardena melako bhatratī sa prakṛtisamasamavāyaśabdeno cyate yastu prākṛtaguṇopamardena bhavati sa vikṛtiviṣamasama vāyo'bhidhīyate vikutyā hetubhūtayā viṣamaḥ prakṛtyananuguāāḥ samavāyo vikṛtiviṣamasamavāya ityarthaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, since that interpretation has a fault, it is explained otherwise: the mixture of rasas and doṣas is of two kinds, conforming to nature and not conforming to nature. The mixture that occurs without suppressing the natural qualities of the things combined is called natural equal combination. But that which occurs through suppression of the natural qualities is called altered unequal combination; that is, because alteration is the cause, the combination is unequal, not conforming to nature.

children.text: atreva vihmativiṣama samavo nānātmakatvādihetutrayaṃ yathāvivṛtameva yojanīyam
children.translated_text: Here too the three causes of altered unequal combination, beginning with diversity, should be applied just as already explained.

children.text: ye tu bikutiviṣamasamavāyau pṛthageva kurvanti viṣamasamavāyastha vaiṣamyatāratamyenātibahuprapañcitatvād viṣamāvayavaguṇānumānaṃ ||
children.translated_text: Those who make altered combination and unequal combination entirely separate have over-elaborated the gradations of inequality in unequal combination; the inference of the qualities of unequal components is thereby left as the point at issue.
Homage to him who has assumed three forms through the division of the three guṇas,
to the source of the three Vedas, the three-eyed one, the lord of the three worlds.
Homage to <s>Sarasvatī</s>, through whose grace, for people of meritorious action,
the overseer of the world is seen reflected in the mirror of the intellect.
Repeated homage to <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Deveśa</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Hutāśa</s>, <s>Veśa</s>, <s>Caraka</s>, and the others.
Homage to the lord of serpents, who through the recension of the Pātañjala work, the Mahābhāṣya, and Caraka
removes the defects of mind, speech, and body.
Following the meanings of <s>Caraka</s> taught by the teacher <s>Naradatta</s>,
the commentary <s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> is composed by <s>Cakradatta</s>.

children.text: sabhyāḥ sadguruvāksudhāsrutiparisphītaśrutīn asmi vo nālaṃ toṣayituṃ payodapayasā nāmbhonidhis tṛpyati
children.translated_text: O worthy ones, whose learning has swelled through hearing the nectar of a true teacher's words, I am not able to satisfy you with the water of a rain-cloud; the ocean is not filled by rain-water.

children.text: vyākhyābhāsarasaprakāśanam idaṃ tv asmin yadi prāpyate kvāpi kvāpi kaṇo guṇasya tadasau karṇe kṣaṇaṃ dhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: Yet if, in this illumination of the flavor of a semblance of commentary, some particle of merit is found here and there, let it be placed in the ear for a moment.

children.text: iha hi dharmārthakāmamokṣaparipanthirogopaśamāya brahmaprabhṛtibhiḥ praṇītāyurvedatantreṣvativistaratvena samprati vartamānālpāyurmedhasāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ na samyagarthādhigamaḥ tadanadhigamācca tadvihitārthānāmananuṣṭhāne tathaivopaplavo rujāmiti manvānaḥ paramakāruṇiko 'trabhavān agniveśo'lpāyurmedhasāmapi suropalambhārthaṃ nātisaṃkṣepavistaraṃ kāyacikitsāpradhānam āyurvedatantraṃ praṇetum ārabdhavān ||
children.translated_text: Here, indeed, in the treatises of <s>Ayurveda</s> composed by <s>Brahma</s> and the others for the pacification of diseases that obstruct <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire, and liberation, because they are excessively extensive, men of the present time, with short life and limited intellect, do not properly understand the meaning. And because they do not understand it, the matters enjoined there are not put into practice, and so the affliction of diseases continues. Thinking thus, the most compassionate venerable <s>Agnivesa</s> began to compose a treatise of <s>Ayurveda</s>, not too brief and not too extensive, chiefly concerned with bodily therapeutics, for easy comprehension even by those of short life and limited intellect.

And when that treatise, consisting of the sections on verses, causes of disease, measurement, body, senses, treatment, pharmaceutics, and success, was to be stated, its statement of the principal meaning of the whole treatise
is to be understood as shown by the sentence beginning with the damaged word "kta" and so on, which expresses that point.

children.text: nanu prayojanābhidhānaṃ śāstrapravṛttyarthamiti yaduktaṃ tanna yuktaṃ yato na prayojanābhidhānamātreṇa prayojanavattāvadhāraṇaṃ vipralambhakasaṃsāramocanapratipādakādiśāstreṣu prayojanābhidhāne'pi niṣprayojanatvadarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: But it may be objected: what was said, that the statement of the purpose is for engaging one in the treatise, is not correct, because merely stating a purpose does not establish that there really is a purpose. Even when a purpose is stated in treatises that teach, for example, liberation from the deceiving cycle of existence, they are seen to be without practical purpose.

children.text: atha manyase āptaprayojanābhidhānametadato'tra yathārthatvaṃ nanu bho kathamayaṃ prayojanābhidhāyī āptaḥ tadabhihitaśāstrasya yathārthatvāditi cet hanta na yāvacchāstrasya prayojanavattāvadhāraṇaṃ na tāvacchāstrapravṛttiḥ na yāvacchāstrapravṛttir na tāvacchāstrasya yathārthatvāvadhāraṇaṃ na yāvacchāstrasya yathārthatvāvadhāraṇaṃ na tāvacchāstrasya karturāptatvamavadhāryate āptatvānavadhṛtau ca kutas tadabhihitaprayojanavattāvadhāraṇam iti cakrakamāpadyate atha manyase mā bhavatu prayojanavattāvadhāraṇam artharūpaprayojanavattāsaṃdeha eva pravartako bhaviṣyati kṛṣyādāv api hi pravṛttir arthasaṃdehādeva na hi tatra kṛṣīvalānāṃ phalalābhāvadhāraṇaṃ vidyate antarāvagrahāderapisaṃbhāvyamānatvāt nanvevamasatyapi prayojanābhidhāne saprayojananiṣprayojanaśāstradarśanācchāstratvam eva prayojanavattāsaṃdehopadarśakam astu tathāpyalaṃ prayojanābhidhānena ||
children.translated_text: If you think, "This is the statement of a purpose by a trustworthy person, and therefore it is true here," then, sir, how is this speaker of the purpose trustworthy? If it is because the treatise stated by him is true, no: until the usefulness of the treatise is determined, there is no undertaking of the treatise; until the treatise is undertaken, its truth is not determined; until its truth is determined, the trustworthiness of the maker of the treatise is not determined; and when trustworthiness is not determined, how can the usefulness of the purpose stated by him be determined? Thus a circularity results. If you think, "Let the usefulness of the purpose not be determined; mere doubt about the purpose in the form of a desirable object will prompt activity. For even in farming, activity arises from doubt about the desired gain, not from certainty of obtaining the result, since interruption by drought and the like is also possible," still, even without any statement of purpose, because one sees both purposeful and purposeless treatises, let treatise-hood itself indicate doubt about usefulness. Therefore the statement of a purpose is still unnecessary.

children.text: naivaṃ nahi sāmānyena prayojanasaṃdehaḥ prayojanaviśeṣārthinaṃ tathā pravartayati yathābhipretaprayojanaviśeṣaviṣayaḥ saṃdehaḥ abhipretaviśeṣaviṣayaśca saṃdeho na viśeṣaviṣayasmaraṇamantarā bhavati ato ye tāvad anavadhṛtāgniveśaprāmāṇyās teṣāṃ dhātusāmyasādhanamidaṃ śāstraṃ na vetyevam ākāraviśeṣasaṃdehotpādanārthaṃ prayojanaviśeṣābhidhānaṃ ye punaḥ paramarṣer agniveśasyādyata evāvadhṛtaprāmāṇyāsteṣāṃ tadabhihitaprayojanavattāvadhāraṇenaiva pravṛttir iti yuktaṃ prayojanābhidhānam ||
children.translated_text: Not so. Doubt about purpose in general does not impel a person who seeks a particular purpose in the way that doubt concerning the specifically desired purpose does. And doubt concerning a desired particular does not arise without recollection of that particular object. Therefore, for those who have not yet determined the authority of <s>Agnivesa</s>, the statement of the specific purpose is meant to produce a particular form of doubt, namely, "Is this treatise a means for producing equilibrium of the bodily elements or not?" But for those who, from the start, have determined the authority of the supreme seer <s>Agnivesa</s>, engagement follows simply from the determination that the purpose stated by him is useful. Thus the statement of the purpose is appropriate.

children.text: prayojanābhidhāyivākye tu svalpaprayatnabodhye prayojanasāmānyasaṃdehādeva pravṛttirupapannā na punaranekasaṃvatsarakleśabodhye śāstre ||
children.translated_text: In the sentence stating the purpose, since it is understood with little effort, engagement is justified from doubt about purpose in general; but that is not so in a treatise whose understanding requires the labor of many years.

children.text: tadevaṃ yaducyate prayojanābhidhāyivākyapravṛttāv api prayojanamabhidhātavyaṃ tathā cānavasthā iti tannirastaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In this way the claim is refuted that, even for engagement with the sentence stating the purpose, a purpose must be stated, and that this would lead to infinite regress.

children.text: athetyādi sūtre 'thaśabdo brahmādipraṇītatantreṣv alpāyurmedhasāmarthānavadhāraṇasya tathābhīṣṭadevatānamaskāraśāstrakaraṇārthagurvājñālābhayor ānantarye prayukto'pi śāstrādau svarūpeṇa maṅgalaṃ bhavatyudakāharaṇapravṛttodakumbhadarśanam iva prasthitānām ||
children.translated_text: In the aphorism beginning with "atha," the word <s>atha</s>, though used to indicate the immediate sequence after the failure of people of short life and limited intellect to determine the meanings in the treatises composed by <s>Brahma</s> and the others, and likewise after the salutation to the chosen deity and the obtaining of the teacher's command to compose the treatise, is itself auspicious at the beginning of a treatise, like the sight of a full water-pot for people setting out after beginning to fetch water.

children.text: granthādau maṅgalasevānirastāntarāyāṇāṃ granthakartṛśrotṝṇām avighneneṣṭalābho bhavatīti yuktaṃ maṅgalopādānam ||
children.translated_text: At the beginning of a book, for authors and listeners whose obstacles have been removed by attending to an auspicious act, the desired result is obtained without impediment; therefore the adoption of an auspicious element is proper.

children.text: athaśabdasya maṅgalatve smṛtir oṃkāraś cāthaśabdaśca dvāv etau brahmaṇaḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: There is a traditional verse for the auspiciousness of the word <s>atha</s>: "The syllable <s>om</s> and the word <s>atha</s>, these two, formerly of <s>Brahma</s>,

children.text: kaṇṭhaṃ bhittvā viniryātau tena māṅgalikāv ubhau iti ||
children.translated_text: came forth after piercing his throat; therefore both are auspicious."
And in other treatises too this word <s>atha</s> is seen as auspicious at the beginning.

children.text: yathā atha śabdānuśāsanam athāto dharmaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ vai ityādau ||
children.translated_text: For example: "Now, instruction concerning words," "Now, therefore, we shall explain <s>dharma</s>," and so on.

children.text: abhīṣṭadevatānamaskārastu granthādau śiṣṭācāraprāptaḥ paramaśiṣṭenāgniveśena kṛta eva anyathā śiṣṭācāralaṅghanena śiṣṭatvameva na syād vyākhyānāntarāyabhayaśca tathā granthāviniveśitasyāpi namaskārasya pratyavāyāpahatvācca na granthaniveśanam ||
children.translated_text: As for the salutation to the chosen deity, it is required by the conduct of cultivated people at the beginning of a book, and the supremely cultivated <s>Agnivesa</s> certainly performed it. Otherwise, by transgressing the conduct of cultivated people, his very cultivated status would not exist. Also there would be fear of an obstacle to the exposition; and since even a salutation not inserted into the book removes fault, it need not be inserted into the text.

children.text: yathā ca gurvājñālābhānantaram etat tantrakaraṇaṃ tathā atha maitrīparaḥ puṇyam ityādau sphuṭameva ||
children.translated_text: And that this composition of the <s>tantra</s> (treatise) comes immediately after obtaining the teacher's command is perfectly clear in the passage beginning, 'Now, intent on friendliness, merit...'

children.text: granthakaraṇe ca gurvanumatipratipādanena granthasyopādeyatā pradarśitā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And in the making of the book, by stating the teacher's approval, the acceptability of the book is shown.

children.text: yat punaḥ śiṣyapraśnānantaryārthatvam athaśabdasya varṇyate tanna māṃ dhinoti nahi śiṣyān puro vyavasthāpya śāstraṃ kriyate śrotṛbuddhisthīkāre tu śāstrakaraṇaṃ yuktaṃ na ca buddhisthīkṛtāḥ praṣṭāro bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: But the explanation that the word <s>atha</s> means immediacy after a pupil's question does not satisfy me. For a <s>śāstra</s> is not composed after arranging pupils in front; rather, composition of a <s>śāstra</s> is appropriate when the listeners have been established in the mind, and questioners are not so established in the mind.

children.text: ataḥśabdo 'dhikāraprāgavadhyupadarśakaḥ ata ūrdhvaṃ yad upadekṣyāmo dīrghaṃjīvitīyaṃ taditi yadi vā hetau yena brahmādipraṇītāyurvedatantrāṇām uktena nyāyenotsambandhatvam iva ato hetor dīrghaṃjīvitīyaṃ vyākhyāsyāma iti yojanīyam ||
children.translated_text: The word <s>ataḥ</s> indicates the prior limit of the topic: 'From this point onward, what we shall teach is the <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s>.' Or it is to be construed causally: since the <s>Āyurveda</s> treatises propounded by <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, for the reason already stated, are as though disconnected, therefore we shall explain the <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s>.

children.text: dīrghaṃjīvitīyam ityatra dīrghaṃjīvitaśabdo 'sminn astīti matvarthe adhyāyānuvākayor luk ca iti chapratyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the expression <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s>, since the word <s>dīrghaṃjīvita</s> is present in it, the affix <s>cha</s> is used in the possessive sense, with elision according to the rule, 'and there is <s>luk</s> in the cases of chapter and recitation-section.'

children.text: yadi vā dīrghaṃjīvitaśabdam adhikṛtya kṛto grantho 'dhyāyarūpastantrarūpo vā ityasyāṃ vivakṣāyām adhikṛtya kṛte granthe ityadhikārāt śiśukrandayamasabha ityādinā chaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, when the intended meaning is 'a book, whether in the form of a chapter or of a treatise, made with reference to the word <s>dīrghaṃjīvita</s>,' then, because of the governing rule 'in a book made with reference to something,' the affix <s>cha</s> is supplied by the rule beginning with <s>śiśukranda</s> and <s>yamasabha</s>.
The same should be understood elsewhere too in cases of this kind.

children.text: atra ca satyapi śabdāntare dīrghaṃjīvitaśabdenaiva saṃjñā kṛtā dīrghaṃjīvitaśabdasyaiva pravacanādau niveśāt praśastatvācca ||
children.translated_text: And here, although other words are available, the designation is made specifically with the word <s>dīrghaṃjīvita</s>, because that very word is placed at the beginning of the exposition and because it is auspicious.

children.text: dīrghaṃjīvitaśabdo 'sminn asti iti dīrghaṃjīvitaśabdam adhikṛtya kṛto vā ityanayā vyutpattyā dīrghaṃjīvitīyaśabdas tantre 'dhyāye ca pravartanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By either derivation, 'the word <s>dīrghaṃjīvita</s> is present in it' or 'it is made with reference to the word <s>dīrghaṃjīvita</s>,' the term <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s> is to be applied both to the treatise and to the chapter.

children.text: tena dīrghaṃjīvitīyaṃ vyākhyāsyāma ityanena tantraṃ prati vyākhyānapratijñā labdhā bhavati punar dīrghaṃjīvitīyam iti padam āvartyādhyāyapadasamabhivyāhṛtam adhyāyavyākhyānapratijñāṃ lambhayati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, by the statement 'we shall explain the <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s>,' a pledge to explain the treatise is obtained; and when the word <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s> is repeated and joined with the word <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter), it brings about the pledge to explain the chapter.

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ cāvṛtya padasya yojanaṃ yathā apāmārgataṇḍulīye gaurave śirasaḥ śūle pīnase ityādau śirasa iti padaṃ gaurave ityanena yujyate āvṛtya śūle ityanena ca ||
children.translated_text: And the construction of a repeated word is observed, as in the <s>Apāmārgataṇḍulīya</s>, in the passage 'in heaviness of the head, in pain, in coryza,' and so on: the word 'of the head' is connected with 'heaviness,' and, by repetition, also with 'pain.'

children.text: ataśca yaducyate akṛtatantrapratijñasyādhyāyapratijñā ūnakāyamāneti tannirastaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus the claim that, without having made a pledge concerning the treatise, the pledge concerning the chapter appears deficient is refuted.

children.text: yadi vā adhyāyapratijñaivāstu tayaiva tantrapratijñāpyarthalabdhaiva na hy adhyāyas tantravyatiriktaḥ tenāvayavavyākhyāne tantrasyāpyavayavino vyākhyā bhavatyeva yathā aṅgulīgrahaṇena devadatto'pi gṛhīto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Or else, let there be only a pledge concerning the chapter; by that very pledge the pledge concerning the treatise is also obtained by implication. For a chapter is not separate from the treatise, and when a part is explained the whole of which it is a part is also explained, just as when a finger is grasped, <s>Devadatta</s> too is grasped.

children.text: avayavāntaravyākhyānapratijñā tu na labhyate tāṃ tu pratyadhyāyameva kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: But a pledge to explain the other parts is not obtained; he will make that for each chapter separately.

children.text: adhyāyamiti adhipūrvādiṅaḥ iṅaśca iti karmaṇi ghañā sādhyam ||
children.translated_text: The form <s>adhyāyam</s> is to be derived from the root <s>iṅ</s> preceded by <s>adhi</s>, with the suffix <s>ghañ</s> in the object sense, under the rule '<s>iṅaś ca</s>'.
Therefore, that which is studied is an <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter).

children.text: na cānayā vyutpattyā prakaraṇacatuṣkasthānādiṣvatiprasaṅgaḥ yato yogarūḍheyam adhyāyasaṃjñādhyāyasya prakaraṇasamūhaviśeṣa eva dīrghaṃjīvitīyādilakṣaṇe paṅkajaśabdavadvartate na yogamātreṇa vartate ||
children.translated_text: Nor, by this derivation, is there overextension to the fourfold groups of sections, to <s>sthānas</s>, and so forth, because this designation <s>adhyāya</s> is conventionally fixed through etymology. It applies only to a particular collection of sections characterized by names such as <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s>, just as the word <s>paṅkaja</s> applies in its fixed sense, not merely by etymology.

children.text: vakṣyati hi adhikṛtyeyamadhyāyanāmasaṃjñā pratiṣṭhitā iti nāmasaṃjñā yogarūḍhasaṃjñetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For he will say, 'This chapter-name designation has been established with reference to the topic'; the phrase 'name-designation' means a conventionally fixed etymological designation.
Or else it is used in the meanings of instrument and locus.
The word <s>adhyāya</s> is established by irregular formation in the sūtra '<s>adhyāya</s>, <s>nyāya</s>, <s>udyāva</s>, and <s>saṃhāra</s>.'
An <s>adhyāya</s> is that in which, or that by which, a particular meaning is studied.
The exclusion of overextension follows the reasoning already stated.

The form <s>vyākhyāsyāmaḥ</s>, 'we shall explain,' is to be derived from the root <s>khyā</s>, preceded by <s>vi</s> and <s>ā</s>, with the future formation; the transmitted text here has a corrupt character in the grammatical notation.

children.text: cakṣiṅo hi prayoge'nicchato 'pi vyākhyātuḥ kriyāphalasambandhasya durnivāratvena svaritañita ityādinātmanepadaṃ syāditi ||
children.translated_text: For, if the root <s>cakṣiṅ</s> were used, then, because connection with the fruit of the action would be hard to avoid even for an explainer who does not intend it, the middle voice would follow by the rule beginning <s>svaritañitaḥ</s>.
The prefix <s>vi</s> means distinction; and the distinctions are detailed exposition, concise statement, and the like.

children.text: āṅ ayaṃ kriyāyoge ye tu maryādāyām abhividhau vā āṅprayogaṃ manyante teṣām abhiprāyaṃ na vidmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This <s>āṅ</s> is connected with the action. But as for those who think that the use of <s>āṅ</s> is in the sense of limit or inclusion, we do not know their intention.

children.text: yato maryādāyāmabhividhau cāṅaḥ prātipadikena yogaḥ syāt yathā āsamudrakṣitīśānām ā pāṭalīputrād vṛṣṭo deva ityādau ihāpi ca tathā ||
children.translated_text: For, in the senses of limit and inclusion, <s>āṅ</s> would be construed with a nominal stem, as in '<s>ā-samudra-kṣitīśānām</s>' and 'the god rained as far as <s>Pāṭalīputra</s>,' and so it would have to be here as well.

children.text: kriyāyogavirahe upasargāḥ kriyāyoge iti niyamād āṅa upasargatvaṃ na syāt tataścānupasargeṇāṅā vyavadhānād ver upasargasya prayogo na syāt ||
children.translated_text: If there were no connection with an action, then, because of the restriction 'preverbs are such when connected with an action,' <s>āṅ</s> would not have preverb status. Consequently, since a non-preverb <s>āṅ</s> would intervene, the use of the preverb <s>vi</s> would not be possible.

children.text: yenāvyavahitaḥ sajātīyavyavahito vā dhātor upasargo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For a preverb belongs to a verbal root when it is uninterrupted, or when it is interrupted only by something of the same class.

children.text: vyāṅor ubhayor apyanupasargatve tatsambandhocitabhūriprātipadikakalpanāgauravaprasaṅgaḥ syāt tasmāt kriyāyogitvam evāṅo nyāyyam ||
children.translated_text: If both <s>vi</s> and <s>āṅ</s> lacked preverb status, there would result the cumbersome supposition of many nominal stems suitable for connection with them. Therefore it is proper that <s>āṅ</s> is connected with the action.

children.text: atha ataḥ dīrghaṃ jīvitīyam adhyāyaṃ vi ā khyāsyāma ityaṣṭapadatvam ||
children.translated_text: Thus the expression 'Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s>' has eight words when analyzed as <s>atha</s>, <s>ataḥ</s>, <s>dīrgham</s>, <s>jīvitīyam</s>, <s>adhyāyam</s>, <s>vi</s>, <s>ā</s>, and <s>khyāsyāmaḥ</s>.

children.text: nanu kathamagniveśaḥ sakalapadārthāśeṣaviśeṣajñānavyākhyeyam āyurvedaṃ vyākhyāsyati yato na tāvad bheṣajādīnām aśeṣaviśeṣapratyakṣajñeyaḥ sarvapadārthānāṃ viśeṣāṇāṃ pratyakṣāviṣayatvāt anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ tu sarvapadārthāvadhāraṇaṃ duṣkarameva yata ekam eva madhu svarūpeṇa jīvayati mārayati coṣṇaṃ samaghṛtaṃ ca kaphaprakṛterhitamahitaṃ vātaprakṛteḥ anūpe sātmyamasātmyaṃ marau śīte sevyamasevyaṃ grīṣme hitam avṛddhe vṛddhe cāhitam alpaṃ guṇakaram ābādhakaram atyupayuktam āmatāṃ gatam udare upakramavirodhitvād ativibhramakaraṃ kākamācīyuktaṃ pakvanikucena ca sahopayuktaṃ maraṇāya athavā balavarṇavīryatejaupaghātāya bhavati ityevamādi tattad yuktaṃ tattacchataśaḥ karoti ata evaikasyaiva madhuno rūpaṃ yadānena prakāreṇa duradhigamaṃ tadātra kaiva kathā nikhilapadārthāśeṣaviśeṣajñānasya ajānaṃśca vyācakṣāṇaḥ kathamupādeyavacana iti kṛtvā guror āptāt pratipannaṃ pratipādayiṣyāma iti darśayan tāmimāṃ śaṅkāṃ nirācikīrṣur gurūktānuvādarūpatāṃ svagranthasya darśayannāha iti ha smāha bhagavānātreya iti ||
children.translated_text: But, it may be objected, how will <s>Agnivesa</s> explain <s>Ayurveda</s>, whose object to be explained is knowledge of all the innumerable particularities of all substances? For he cannot have direct knowledge of all the particularities of medicines and the like, since the particularities of all substances are not objects of perception. And determination of all substances by positive and negative concomitance is very difficult indeed. For the same honey, by its own nature, gives life and also kills; when hot and mixed with ghee it is beneficial or harmful for a person of phlegmatic constitution and for a person of windy constitution; in marshy country it is wholesome or unwholesome, in desert country; in cold season it is to be used, in summer not to be used; for one not aged it is beneficial, but for an aged person harmful; in small quantity it produces good qualities, when overused it is injurious; when it has become unripe in the belly, because it opposes the treatment, it produces extreme disorder; when used together with <s>kakamaci</s> or with ripe <s>nikuca</s>, it leads to death, or else to impairment of strength, complexion, vigor, and brilliance. Thus, when combined with this or that, it does this or that in hundreds of ways. Therefore, when the nature even of this one honey is hard to ascertain in this manner, what need be said here of knowledge of the innumerable particularities of all substances? And if one explains without knowing, how can his statement be acceptable? To remove this doubt, showing that "we shall expound what was received from a trustworthy teacher," and showing that his own treatise has the form of repetition of the teacher's statement, he says: "Thus indeed the venerable <s>Atreya</s> used to say."

children.text: atra itiśabdo vakṣyamāṇārthaparāmarśakaḥ haśabdo'vadhāraṇe yathā na ha vai saśarīrasya priyāpriyayorapahatirastīti atra na heti naivetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the word <s>iti</s> refers back to the meaning that is about to be stated. The particle <s>ha</s> has the sense of restriction, as in, "For indeed, for one who has a body there is no removal of the pleasant and the unpleasant"; here <s>na ha</s> means "certainly not."

children.text: atra smāha iti smaśabdaprayogena bhūtamātra eva liḍarthe laṭ sme iti laṭ na bhūtānadyatanaparokṣe ātreyopadeśasyāgniveśaṃ pratyaparokṣatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Here, in <s>smaha</s>, by the use of the particle <s>sma</s>, the present tense has the sense of the perfect merely in relation to the past, according to the rule "the present is used when <s>sma</s> is present"; it is not the perfect denoting an unseen event earlier than the present day, because <s>Atreya</s>'s instruction to <s>Agnivesa</s> was not unseen by him.

children.text: yathā ca bhūtamātre liḍ bhavati tathāca darśayiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And we shall show how the perfect is used merely with reference to the past.

children.text: bhagaṃ pūjitaṃ jñānaṃ tadvān yathoktam utpattiṃ pralayaṃ caiva bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaga</s> is revered knowledge; one who possesses that is so called, as has been said: "One who knows the origin and dissolution of beings, their coming and going,

children.text: vetti vidyāmavidyāṃ ca sa vācyo bhagavāniti yadi vā bhagaśabdaḥ samastaiśvaryamāhātmyādivacanaḥ yathoktam aiśvaryasya samagrasya vīryasya yaśasaḥ śriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and knowledge and ignorance, he is to be called <s>bhagavan</s>." Or else the word <s>bhaga</s> denotes complete sovereignty, greatness, and the like, as has been said: "Of complete sovereignty, power, fame, splendor,
knowledge, and detachment, these six are termed <s>bhaga</s> by the interpreters."
<s>Atreya</s> means a descendant of <s>Atri</s>. By this his purity of lineage is shown.

children.text: atrānye varṇayanti caturvidhaṃ sūtraṃ bhavati gurusūtraṃ śiṣyasūtraṃ pratisaṃskartṛsūtram ekīyasūtraṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Here some explain that there are four kinds of sūtra: the teacher's sūtra, the student's sūtra, the redactor's sūtra, and the sūtra of an individual teacher.

children.text: tatra gurusūtraṃ yathā naitad buddhimatā draṣṭavyam agniveśa ityādi pratisaṃskartṛsūtraṃ yathā tamuvāca bhagavānātreyaḥ ityādi śiṣyasūtraṃ yathā naitāni bhagavan pañcakaṣāyaśatāni pūryante ityādi ekīyasūtraṃ yathā kumārasya śiraḥ pūrvamabhinirvartata iti kumāraśirā bharadvājaḥ ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Among these, a teacher's sūtra is, for example, "This should not be regarded by an intelligent man, O <s>Agnivesa</s>," and so on. A redactor's sūtra is, for example, "The venerable <s>Atreya</s> said to him," and so on. A student's sūtra is, for example, "O venerable one, these five hundred decoctions are not completed," and so on. A sūtra of an individual teacher is, for example, "The head of the child is formed first; therefore <s>Kumarasiras Bharadvaja</s>," and so on.
Therefore the first sūtra, the pledge to explain, belongs to the teacher alone, because the student <s>Agnivesa</s> has no authority in the explanation.
And the second sūtra belongs to the redactor.

children.text: itiśabdena ca prakāravācinā dīrghaṃjīvitīyaṃ vyākhyāsyāma iti parāmṛśyate tenāha smeti bhūtānadyatanaparokṣa eva bhavati pratisaṃskartāraṃ pratyātreyopadeśasya parokṣatvāt ||
children.translated_text: And by the word <s>iti</s>, which denotes a mode, the phrase "we shall explain <s>Dirghamjivitiya</s>" is referred to. Therefore the expression <s>aha sma</s> is indeed a perfect referring to an unseen event earlier than the present day, because <s>Atreya</s>'s instruction was unseen by the redactor.

children.text: anena ca nyāyena tamuvāca bhagavānātreya ityādāv api liḍvidhir upapanno bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By this same principle, the grammatical prescription of the perfect is also appropriate in passages such as "The venerable <s>Atreya</s> said to him."

children.text: suśrute ca yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ iti pratisaṃskartṛsūtramiti kṛtvā ṭīkākṛtā liḍvidhir upapāditaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Susruta</s>, too, because the phrase "as the venerable <s>Dhanvantari</s> said" is a redactor's sūtra, the commentator has justified the prescription of the perfect.

children.text: atra brūmaḥ yattāvaduktaṃ śiṣyasyāgniveśasya vyākhyānānadhikārādidaṃ guroḥ sūtraṃ tanna nahi jātyā gurutvam asti yataḥ sa evātreyaḥ svagurum apekṣya śiṣyaḥ agniveśādīn apekṣya guruḥ evamagniveśo 'pi granthakaraṇakāle svabuddhisthīkṛtāñśiṣyān prati gururiti na kaścid doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here we reply: as for what was said, that this is the teacher's sūtra because the student <s>Agnivesa</s> lacks authority to explain, that is not so. For teacherhood is not fixed by birth, since that very <s>Atreya</s>, with reference to his own teacher, is a student, while with reference to <s>Agnivesa</s> and the others he is a teacher. In the same way, <s>Agnivesa</s> too, at the time of composing the treatise, is a teacher with respect to the students established in his own mind; thus there is no fault.

children.text: yatpunardvitīyasya pratisaṃskartṛsūtratayā bhūtānadyatanaparokṣe liḍvidhir upapādyate tatra vicāryaṃ kim idaṃ dvitīyaṃ sūtraṃ pūrvavākyaikatāpannaṃ na vā yadyekavākyatāpannaṃ tadā suśrute tathā vyākhyāsyāmo yathovāca dhanvantarir iti yojanīyaṃ tathāca tathā vyākhyāsyāma iti kriyaikavākyatāpannam uvācetipadaṃ na bhinnakartṛkaṃ bhavitum arhati tathā ca kuto liḍvidhiḥ atha naikatāpannaṃ tadā gaur aśvaḥ puruṣo hastītivannārthasaṃgatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, as for the point that the prescription of the perfect as referring to an unseen event earlier than the present day is justified because the second sūtra belongs to the redactor, this must be examined. Is this second sūtra syntactically unified with the preceding sentence or not? If it is syntactically unified, then in the <s>Susruta</s> it must be construed as, "We shall explain in the manner in which <s>Dhanvantari</s> spoke." And in that case the word <s>uvaca</s>, being syntactically unified with the action "we shall explain in that manner," cannot have a different agent. So whence would there be the prescription of the perfect? But if it is not unified with it, then there is no connection of meaning, as in "cow, horse, man, elephant."

children.text: kiṃca jatūkarṇādau pratisaṃskartṛśrutigandho 'pi nāsti tat kathaṃ nānāśrutaparipūrṇakaṇṭhaḥ śiṣyo jatūkarṇaḥ prāñjalir adhigamyovāca ityādau liḍvidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, in passages concerning <s>Jatukarna</s> and the like there is not even the slightest hint in scripture of a redactor. So how can the prescription of the perfect apply in passages such as, "The student <s>Jatukarna</s>, whose throat was filled with many scriptures, approached with joined palms and said"?

children.text: anena nyāyena carake 'pi pratisaṃskartṛsūtrapakṣe liḍvidhirnāsti tasmāccarake 'gniveśaḥ suśrute suśruta eva sūtrāṇāṃ praṇetā kvacit kiṃcidarthaṃ stotuṃ nindituṃ vākhyāyikārūpaṃ purākalpaṃ darśayan kimapi sūtraṃ gurūktānuvādarūpatayā kimapyekīyamatānuvādarūpatayā likhati pratisaṃskartā tv ayaṃ granthaṃ pūrayati tadādyagranthakartṛtayaiva ||
children.translated_text: By this reasoning, even in <s>Caraka</s>, on the view that there was a redactor, there is no rule requiring the perfect tense. Therefore in <s>Caraka</s> it is <s>Agniveśa</s>, and in <s>Suśruta</s> it is <s>Suśruta</s> himself, who is the originator of the sūtras. In places, in order to praise or criticize some point, he presents an ancient account in the form of a narrative; he writes some sūtras as a repetition of what was said by the teacher, and some as a repetition of the opinion of a certain school. But this redactor fills out the treatise only in the capacity of author of the later portion of the book.

children.text: liḍvidhistu bhūtānadyatanamātra eva chandovihito bhāṣāyāmapi varṇanīyaḥ anyathā uvāceti padaṃ jatūkarṇādau na syāt tathā ca harivaṃśe dhanyopākhyāne māmuvāca iti tathā ahamuvāca iti ca na syāt yathā sa māmuvācāmbucaraḥ kūrmo mānuṣavat svayam ||
children.translated_text: The rule for the perfect tense, however, is prescribed in Vedic usage only for a past event not belonging to the present day, and must be described in ordinary language as well. Otherwise the word "uvāca" would not occur in <s>Jatūkarṇa</s> and the like; likewise in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, in the tale of <s>Dhanya</s>, there could not be "he said to me" or "I said," as in: "That water-dwelling tortoise himself spoke to me like a man,"

children.text: kimāścaryaṃ mayi mune dhanyaścāhaṃ kathaṃ vibho iti tathā svayaṃbhuvacanāt so 'haṃ vedān vai samupasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "What wonder is there in me, O sage? How am I blessed, O lord?" And similarly: "At the word of <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, I approached those Vedas."
"And he spoke to these four."

children.text: yadapi iti ha smāha ityatra itiśabdena pūrvasūtraṃ parāmṛśyate tanna yena dīrghaṃjīvitīyādisūtramātrasya tadarthasya vā gurūktatvapratipādane sati naivottaratrābhidheyābhidhānena nikhilatantrasya gurūktānuvādarūpatayā karaṇaṃ śrotṛśraddhākaraṇaṃ pratipāditaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: As for the claim that, in the expression "iti ha smāha," the word "iti" refers back to the preceding sūtra, that is not so. For if only the sūtra beginning with <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s>, or only its meaning, were established as spoken by the teacher, then the later statement of the subject matter would not establish that the whole treatise was composed as a repetition of what the teacher said, nor would it produce confidence in the hearers.

children.text: bhavati tu bhāvayituṃ yathā purā vyākhyātaṃ tasmāttadeva nyāyyamiti ||
children.translated_text: But it is possible to cause such understanding, as was explained earlier; therefore that alone is reasonable.

children.text: agniveśasya vyākhyāsyāma iti bahuvacanam ekasminn apy asmadaḥ prayogādbahuvacanaprayogasya sādhutvāt sādhu hi vadanti vaktāro vayaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: In "we shall explain <s>Agniveśa</s>'s text," the plural is used because the plural use of "we" is correct even when one person is meant; speakers properly say, "We shall do it."

children.text: bhagavānātreya ityatra tv ekavacananirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ bhagavānityanenaivātreyasya gurorgauravasya darśitatvāt ||
children.translated_text: But in "the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>," the singular is used, because by the word "venerable" itself the dignity of <s>Ātreya</s> as teacher has been shown.
He states who those great seers are with the words beginning "<s>Āṅgirasa</s>" and so on.

children.text: bahvṛṣīṇām atra kīrtanaṃ granthādau pāpakṣayahetutvena tathāyurvedasyaivaṃvidhamahāpuruṣasevitatvena sevyatvopadarśanārthaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: The mention of many seers here at the beginning of the book is both because it is a cause of the destruction of sin and in order to show that <s>Āyurveda</s>, since it was attended by such great persons, is itself worthy of attendance.

children.text: eṣu ca madhye kecid yāyāvarāḥ kecicchālīnāḥ kecidayonijāḥ evaṃprakārāśca sarve mīlitā boddhavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among these, some should be understood as wandering ascetics, some as household ascetics, and some as not born from a womb; all of them, of such various kinds, are to be understood as gathered together.

children.text: bhikṣurityātreyaviśeṣaṇaṃ vakṣyati hi tanneti bhikṣur ātreyaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: "Mendicant" is an epithet of <s>Ātreya</s>, for he will say, "That mendicant <s>Ātreya</s> did not."
"<s>Vaikhānasa</s>" is a designation applied because of a particular rite.
The <s>Vālakhilyas</s> are certain seers of very small size.
They are "treasures" as it were, because they are inexhaustible repositories.
"Self-restraint" means the state of being restrained.
"This" means what is going to be stated later.

children.text: dhāraṇāddharmaḥ sa cātmasamavetaḥ kāryadarśanānumeyaḥ arthaḥ suvarṇādiḥ kāmyata ita kāmo vanitāpariṣvaṅgādiḥ mokṣaḥ saṃsāravimokṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is so called because it upholds; it inheres in the self and is inferred from its effects. <s>Artha</s> is gold and the like. <s>Kāma</s> is so called because it is desired, such as the embrace of a woman and the like. <s>Mokṣa</s> is liberation from transmigration.
Health, because it is the absence of disease, is equilibrium of the bodily elements.
"Root" means cause.

children.text: uttamamiti pradhānaṃ tenārogyaṃ caturvarge pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ rogagṛhītasya kvacidapi puruṣārthe 'samarthatvād ityuktam ||
children.translated_text: "Highest" means principal. Thus it is said that health is the principal cause among the four aims of life, because a person seized by disease is incapable with respect to any human purpose.

children.text: tasyāpahartāra iti ārogyasyāpahartāraḥ idam eva ca rogāṇām ārogyāpaharaṇaṃ yad anarthalābhaḥ na punar utpanno rogaḥ paścād ārogyam apaharati bhāvābhāvayoḥ parasparābhāvātmakatvāt ||
children.translated_text: "Those that remove it" means those that remove health. And this very removal of health by diseases is the acquisition of an undesirable condition. It is not that a disease, once arisen, subsequently removes health, because an existent thing and a non-existent thing are mutually of the nature of each other's absence.

children.text: śreyaso jīvitasya ceti śreyovajjīvitaṃ hitatvena sukhatvena cārthe daśamahāmūlīye vakṣyamāṇaṃ tasya jīvitasyāpahartāra iti yojanīyam aśreyojīvitamahitatvena duḥkhahetutayā cānupādeyam iti kṛtvā tadapaharaṇamiha noktam ||
children.translated_text: In "of welfare and of life," the construction is: diseases are removers of that life which has welfare, and which will be described in the section <s>Daśamahāmūlīya</s> as beneficial and happy. Since a life without welfare is not to be accepted, being harmful and a cause of suffering, its removal is not mentioned here.

children.text: atra sukhitajīvitopaghāto dharmādyupaghātenaiva labdhaḥ tena vayaṃ paśyāmaḥ śreyaḥśabdena sāmānye nābhyudayavācinā dharmādayo 'bhidhīyante jīvitaśabdena ca jīvitamātraṃ yato jīvitaṃ svarūpeṇaiva sarvaprāṇināṃ nirupādhyupādeyaṃ vacanaṃ hi ācakame ca brahmaṇa iyamātmā āśīḥ āyuṣmān bhūyāsam iti ||
children.translated_text: Here the injury to happy life is already included through the injury to <s>dharma</s> and the other aims. Therefore we consider that by the word "welfare," in its general sense of prosperity, <s>dharma</s> and the others are denoted, and by the word "life" mere life is denoted, because life by its own nature is to be accepted unconditionally by all living beings. For there is the statement: "This self desired this blessing from <s>Brahman</s>: may I be long-lived."

children.text: yattvatyantaduḥkhagṛhītasya jīvitaṃ jihāsitaṃ tatra duḥkhasyātyantajihāsitasyānyathā hātum aśakyatvāt priyamapi jīvitaṃ tyaktum icchati na svarūpeṇa ||
children.translated_text: But when a person afflicted by extreme suffering wishes to abandon life, then, because the intensely hated suffering cannot otherwise be abandoned, he wishes to give up even dear life, not life in its own nature.
"Obstacle" is to be understood as an obstacle to the accomplishment of <s>dharma</s> and the other aims.
"This" means having the form of the manifestation of disease.
"Of them" means of the diseases.
"Refuge" means protector.
Because he is capable, he is called <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: dhyānaṃ samādhiviśeṣaḥ tadupalabdhisādhanatvāccakṣur iva dhyānacakṣuḥ tena sa vakṣyati śamopāyaṃ yathāvad amaraprabhuḥ iti dhyānacakṣuṣā dadṛśuriti yojanā ||
children.translated_text: Meditation is a particular kind of concentration. Since it is the means for obtaining that, it is called the eye of meditation, like an eye. Therefore the construction is: with the eye of meditation they saw that the lord of the immortals would state the means of pacification correctly, as he will say, "the lord of the immortals, the means of pacification, as it really is."

children.text: athaiteṣu madhye bharadvājaḥ katham indram upāgamad ityāha ka ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, among these sages, how did <s>Bharadvāja</s> approach <s>Indra</s>? He explains this with the words beginning "who?"

children.text: śacīpatim ityanena śacīsambhogavyāsaktam apyaham upāsituṃ kṣama iti bharadvājo darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By the expression "husband of <s>Śacī</s>," <s>Bharadvāja</s> shows: "I am able to attend upon him even though he is absorbed in enjoyment with <s>Śacī</s>."
"Purpose" means objective.
"I should be appointed" means "I should be set to work."
In the expression "atra," the word <s>atra</s> is used here, in relation to the present purpose, in the sense of "because."

children.text: yathā subhikṣam ityāgataḥ yasmāt subhikṣaṃ tasmādāgata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For example, in the expression "he came because there was plenty of food," the meaning is: because there was abundance, therefore he came.

children.text: niyojita iti caurādiko ṇica na hetau ||
children.translated_text: And in <s>niyojita</s>, the causative suffix <s>ṇic</s> belongs to the <s>curādi</s> class; it is not used in the sense of causing another to act.

children.text: anena prakaraṇena bharadvājasyāyurvedāgame viśeṣeṇārthitvānna preraṇamiti darśitaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By this section it is shown that, since <s>Bharadvāja</s> had a special desire for the transmission of <s>Āyurveda</s>, there was no need for prompting.

children.text: provāceti samyaguvāca na tu praśabdaḥ prapañcārthaḥ padairalpair ityuktatvāt ||
children.translated_text: The word <s>provāca</s> means "he spoke correctly," and the prefix <s>pra</s> does not have the sense of elaboration, because it has been said that he spoke "with few words."

children.text: kasmāt padair alpair uvācetyāha matiṃ buddhvā vipulām iti yasmād vipulamatiṃ bharadvājaṃ pratipannavān tasmāt padair alpair uvāceti bhāvaḥ matiś ca bahuviṣayatvenopacārād vipulety ucyate sā ca matiḥ śuśrūṣāśravaṇagrahaṇadhāraṇohāpohatattvābhiniveśavatīha vipulā boddhavyā ||
children.translated_text: Why did he speak with few words? The text answers, "having understood his vast intelligence." Since he recognized <s>Bharadvāja</s> as one of vast intellect, he spoke with few words; this is the intention. And intelligence is called "vast" figuratively because it has many objects. Here that intelligence should be understood as vast because it was endowed with the wish to listen, hearing, grasping, retention, reasoning, rejection of error, and firm adherence to truth.

children.text: atra cendreṇa divyadṛśā bharadvājābhiprāyam agrata eva buddhvāyurveda upadiṣṭaḥ tena bharadvājasyendrapṛcchādīha na darśitaṃ kiṃvā bhūtam apīndrapṛcchādi granthavistarabhayād iha na likhitam ||
children.translated_text: Here <s>Indra</s>, by divine sight, understood <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s intention beforehand and taught <s>Āyurveda</s>; therefore <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s questioning of <s>Indra</s> and the like is not shown here. Or else, even if questioning of <s>Indra</s> and the like did occur, it was not written here out of concern for making the book too extensive.
He states what kind of <s>Āyurveda</s> it was that was taught in few words, beginning with "cause" and so on.

children.text: hetuliṅgauṣadhajñānamiti hetvādīni jñāyante 'neneti hetuliṅgauṣadhajñānaṃ yāvac cāyurvedavācyaṃ tāvaddhetvādyantarbhūtam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Knowledge of causes, signs, and medicines" means the knowledge by which causes, signs, and medicines are known. The sense is that everything expressed by the term <s>Āyurveda</s> is included within causes and the rest.

children.text: hetugrahaṇena saṃnikṛṣṭaviprakṛṣṭavyādhihetugrahaṇaṃ liṅgagrahaṇena ca vyādher ārogyasya ca kṛtsnaṃ liṅgamucyate tena vyādhyārogye 'pi liṅgaśabdavācye yatastābhyāmapi hi talliṅgaṃ liṅgyata eva vakṣyati hi viṣamārambhamūlānāṃ jvara eko hi lakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: By mentioning causes, the text includes the proximate and remote causes of disease. By mentioning signs, it refers to the whole range of signs of disease and health. Thus disease and health too fall under what is denoted by the word <s>liṅga</s> (sign), because through them that which is signified is indeed indicated. For he will say, "Fever alone is the sign of disorders whose beginnings and roots are irregular."

children.text: viṣamārambhamūlādyair jvara eko nigadyate ityādi auṣadhagrahaṇena ca sarvapathyāvarodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Passages such as "Fever alone is called so because of irregular beginnings, roots, and the like" are meant. And by mentioning medicine, all wholesome regimen is included.
The body too is included here under both cause and sign.
Since it is the supreme, excellent <s>ayana</s> (path) for the healthy and the sick, it is called <s>svasthāturaparāyaṇa</s>, "the supreme path for the healthy and the sick."

children.text: kimanyo'yaṃ hetuliṅgauṣadhajñānarūpa āyurvedo brahmabuddhādāyurvedād utānanya ityāha trisūtram ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Is this <s>Āyurveda</s>, consisting of knowledge of causes, signs, and medicines, different from the <s>Āyurveda</s> understood by <s>Brahmā</s> and the Buddha and others, or not different? To answer this he says, beginning with "three-sūtra."

children.text: pitāmaho'pi yaṃ trisūtraṃ bubudhe tamindraḥ provāca ||
children.translated_text: The very three-sūtra teaching that the Grandfather too understood, <s>Indra</s> spoke.

children.text: trīṇi hetvādīni sūtryante yasmin yena vā tantrisūtram ||
children.translated_text: That in which, or by which, the three, namely causes and the rest, are threaded together is <s>trisūtra</s>.
There, it is a <s>sūtra</s> because it indicates and because it threads together a continuity of meaning.

children.text: etena taṃ yathā brahmā trisūtraṃ bubudhe tathaiva hetuliṅgauṣadhajñānam indraḥ provācetyaviplutamāgamaṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By this he shows the unbroken transmission: just as <s>Brahmā</s> understood it as <s>trisūtra</s>, so too <s>Indra</s> spoke it as knowledge of causes, signs, and medicines.
"He understood" means that he knew it; it does not mean that he made it.
For that very reason it is said to be <s>śāśvata</s>, that is, eternal.
And that eternality is to be demonstrated at the end of the <s>Sūtrasthāna</s>.

children.text: athoddiṣṭam āyurvedaṃ kathaṃ gṛhītavān bharadvāja ityāha so 'nantetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, how did <s>Bharadvāja</s> grasp the <s>Āyurveda</s> that had been stated? To answer this he says, beginning with "he, the boundless..."

children.text: avidyamānāv antapārau yasyāsāv anantapāraḥ atra pāraśabdena gobalīvardanyāyenādir ucyate pāraśabdo hy ubhayor api nadīkūlayor vivakṣāvaśād vartate kiṃvā ananto mokṣaḥ pāram utkṛṣṭaṃ phalaṃ yasyāyurvedasyāsāv anantapāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: That whose ends and farther shores do not exist is <s>anantapāra</s>, "boundless." Here, by the word <s>pāra</s>, the beginning is meant, according to the maxim of the cow and the bull; for the word <s>pāra</s> may refer, according to intention, to either bank of a river. Or else <s>ananta</s> means liberation, and <s>pāra</s> means the supreme fruit: that <s>Āyurveda</s> whose supreme fruit is liberation is <s>anantapāra</s>.

children.text: vakṣyati hi cikitsā tu naiṣṭhikī yā vinopadhām iti ||
children.translated_text: For he will say, "But the final therapy is that which is without material adjunct."
Here <s>naiṣṭhikī</s>, "final," means that which is a means to liberation.

children.text: trayo hetvādayaḥ skandharūpā yasya sa triskandhaḥ skandhaśca sthūlāvayavaḥ pravibhāgo vā ||
children.translated_text: That which has the three, causes and the rest, in the form of <s>skandhas</s> is <s>triskandha</s>. A <s>skandha</s> is a gross limb or a division.
He whose mind was on the grasping of <s>Āyurveda</s> alone was <s>tanmanas</s>, "having his mind on that."
Because he reflected and possessed excellence of knowledge, he was a <s>muni</s>.

children.text: etena yasmādayaṃ mahāmatis tanmanāḥ muniśca tenānantapāramapyāyurvedaṃ hetvādiskandhatrayamālambanaṃ kṛtvā yathāvadacirādeva pratipannavān ityāśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this the intention is that, because he was of great intelligence, had his mind fixed on it, and was a <s>muni</s>, he properly understood even the boundless <s>Āyurveda</s> very quickly by taking as its support the three groups of causes and the rest.
<s>Acirāt</s> means "in a short time."

children.text: atra ca yathā brahmā trisūtraṃ bubudhe yathā cendro hetuliṅgauṣadhajñānaṃ provāca tathaiva bharadvājo'pi triskandhaṃ taṃ bubudhe ityanenāyurvedasyāviplutāgamatvam upadarśyate tena trisūtratriskandhayor na punaruktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And here, just as <s>Brahmā</s> understood it as <s>trisūtra</s>, and just as <s>Indra</s> spoke the knowledge of causes, signs, and medicines, so too <s>Bharadvāja</s> understood that threefold-grouped teaching. By this, the unbroken transmission of <s>Āyurveda</s> is shown; therefore there is no repetition between <s>trisūtra</s> and <s>triskandha</s>.
"By that" means by the <s>Āyurveda</s> received from <s>Indra</s>.
"Unmeasured" means "as if unmeasured," because it was extremely long.

children.text: āyuḥśabdaścāyuḥkāraṇe rasāyanajñāne boddhavyaḥ yenottarakālaṃ hi rasāyanopayogād ayaṃ bharadvājo'mitamāyuravāpsyati na ṛṣibhya āyurvedakathanāt pūrvaṃ rasāyanamācarati sma kiṃvā sarvaprāṇyupakārārthādhītāyurvedajanitadharmavaśāt tatkālam evāmitamāyur lebhe bharadvāja iti boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: And the word <s>āyus</s> (life) should be understood as referring to the cause of life, namely knowledge of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). For later, through the use of <s>rasāyana</s>, this <s>Bharadvāja</s> will obtain an unmeasured life; it is not that he practiced <s>rasāyana</s> before telling <s>Āyurveda</s> to the seers. Or else, it should be understood that <s>Bharadvāja</s> obtained unmeasured life at that very time through the force of the merit produced by studying <s>Āyurveda</s> for the benefit of all living beings.

children.text: tacceti śrutaṃ yadā tamiti pāṭhaḥ tadā tam āyurvedam ||
children.translated_text: As for "and that": when the reading is "when he had heard that, that," then "that" refers to that <s>Āyurveda</s>.
<s>Anavaśeṣayan</s> means "completely," without leaving anything out.
Immediately after studying <s>Āyurveda</s>, he gave it to the seers.
"Desiring to make life long" refers both to living beings and to himself.

children.text: jñānārthaṃ jñānarūpaṃ vā cakṣur jñānacakṣuḥ tena jñānacakṣuṣā ||
children.translated_text: <s>jñānacakṣus</s>, 'the eye of knowledge,' is an eye for the sake of knowledge, or an eye whose nature is knowledge; by that eye of knowledge.

children.text: gṛhītena tenāyurvedena kiṃ dadṛśurityāha sāmānyaṃ cetyādi ||
children.translated_text: What did he see by means of that <s>Āyurveda</s> which he had grasped? He states this with 'sāmānya and so on.'

children.text: eṣāṃ cottaratra lakṣaṇaṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ padārthānāṃ viśvarūpāṇāṃ bhaviṣyati tenaitat tatraiva vyākaraṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: Later the definition of these six <s>padārthas</s> (categories), which have manifold forms, will be given; therefore this matter should be explained there itself.
'That' means <s>sāmānya</s> and the others.
'The method stated in the <s>tantra</s>' means the form of avoiding what is unwholesome and adopting what is wholesome.
<s>śarman</s> means happiness.
'Supreme' means not overcome by suffering.
'Imperishable' means not going away.
With the passage beginning 'atha,' he shows that <s>Ātreya</s>, the pupil of <s>Bharadvāja</s> and also named <s>Punarvasu</s>, was the teacher of <s>Agniveśa</s> and the others.

children.text: atra kecidbharadvājātreyayoraikyaṃ manyante tanna bharadvājasaṃjñayā ātreyasya kvacid api tantrapradeśe 'kīrtanāt hārīte cātreyādigurutayā bharadvāja uktaḥ śakrād aham adhītavān ityādinā mattaḥ punarasaṃkhyeyās trisūtraṃ triprayojanam ||
children.translated_text: Here some think that <s>Bharadvāja</s> and <s>Ātreya</s> are one and the same. That is not so, because nowhere in any place of the treatise is <s>Ātreya</s> mentioned by the name <s>Bharadvāja</s>; and in the <s>Hārīta</s> too <s>Bharadvāja</s> is stated to be the teacher of <s>Ātreya</s> and the others, in the passage beginning 'I learned it from <s>Śakra</s>' and continuing, 'From me again, innumerable sages learned the threefold source and the threefold purpose.'
'Among them the seven great seers ending with <s>Ātreya</s> knew it,'
down to the end of the statement, 'From <s>Ātreya</s> the seer <s>Hārīta</s> learned it.'

children.text: vāgbhaṭena tu yaduktaṃ brahmā smṛtvāyuṣo vedaṃ prajāpatim ajigrahat ||
children.translated_text: But what <s>Vāgbhaṭa</s> said is this: '<s>Brahmā</s>, having recollected the Veda of life, taught it to <s>Prajāpati</s>.'

children.text: so 'śvinau tau sahasrākṣaṃ so 'triputrādikān munīn vā ityanenātreyasyendraśiṣyatvaṃ tadāyurvedasamutthānīyarasāyanapāde ādiśabdena vakṣyamāṇendraśiṣyatāyogāt samarthanīyam ||
children.translated_text: 'He taught it to the <s>Aśvins</s>; they to <s>Sahasrākṣa</s>; he to the sages such as the son of <s>Atri</s>.' By this statement, <s>Ātreya</s>'s discipleship under <s>Indra</s> is to be justified, since in the <s>Āyurvedasamutthānīya</s> rasāyana chapter his discipleship under <s>Indra</s> will be stated through the word 'and others.'

children.text: tatra hīndreṇa punar maharṣīṇām āyurveda upadiṣṭa iti vaktavyam ||
children.translated_text: For there it has to be said that <s>Indra</s> again taught <s>Āyurveda</s> to the great seers.

children.text: maitrīparo maitrīpradhānaḥ maitrī ca sarvaprāṇiṣvātmanīva buddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>maitrīpara</s> means chiefly devoted to friendliness; and friendliness is the thought toward all living beings as toward oneself.
This refers to the passage beginning 'of him' and so on.
It is a <s>veda</s> because it makes known.
'Approved by knowers of the Veda' means honored by those who know the Veda.

children.text: atha kasmād āyurvedalakṣaṇo vedaḥ puṇyatamo vedavidāṃ ca pūjita ityāha vakṣyata ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, why is the Veda called <s>Āyurveda</s> especially meritorious and honored by knowers of the Veda? He answers with the passage beginning 'it will be stated.'

children.text: yaditi yasmāt evamuktaṃ bhavati yadanye ṛgvedādayaḥ prāyaḥ paralokahitamevārthaṃ vadanti tena puṇyāḥ puṇyatamaścāyamāyurvedo yad yasmānmanuṣyāṇāmubhayorapi lokayor yaddhitam āyurārogyasādhanaṃ dharmasādhanaṃ ca tadvakṣyate tenātiśayena puṇyatamastathā vedavidāṃ ca pūjita iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Because' means 'inasmuch as.' The meaning is this: the other Vedas, such as the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, for the most part teach only what is beneficial for the next world, and therefore they are meritorious. But this <s>Āyurveda</s> is most meritorious because it will teach what is beneficial for human beings in both worlds: the means to life and health, and also the means to <s>dharma</s>. Therefore it is especially most meritorious, and also honored by knowers of the Veda.

children.text: kecit vakṣyate yaḥ iti paṭhanti tatrāpi hetugarbhamiti vyākhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: Some read, 'which will be stated.' In that reading too it should be explained as containing an implicit reason.

children.text: jīvitapradātṛtvādāyurvedasya puṇyatamatvaṃ boddhavyaṃ yataś caturvargasādhanībhūtajīvitapradam eva sarvottamaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Because <s>Āyurveda</s> gives life, its status as most meritorious should be understood, since that which gives life, the basis for attaining the four human aims, is highest of all.

children.text: ucyate ca na hi jīvitadānāddhi dānamanyadviśiṣyate iti ||
children.translated_text: And it is also said, 'No other gift is indeed superior to the gift of life.'

children.text: sampratyāyurvedābhidheyatayā sūtrite sāmānyādau sāmānyasya prathamasūtritatvāt tathā sāmānyajñānamūlatvāccāyurvedapratipādyasya hetvādeḥ sāmānyamevāgre nirdiśati sarvadetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, since <s>sāmānya</s> and the rest have been indicated as the subject matter of <s>Āyurveda</s>, and since <s>sāmānya</s> was first indicated, and since knowledge of <s>sāmānya</s> is the root of the causes and other matters taught by <s>Āyurveda</s>, he first states <s>sāmānya</s> itself, beginning with 'always.'

children.text: sarvadā sarvasmin kāle nityage cāvasthike ca ||
children.translated_text: 'Always' means at every time, both in what is permanent and in what is conditional.

children.text: sarvabhāvānāmityatra sarvaśabdaḥ kṛtsnavācī bhavanti sattāmanubhavantīti bhāvā dravyaguṇakarmāṇītyarthaḥ natu bhavantyutpadyanta iti bhāvāḥ tathā sati pṛthivyādiparamāṇūnāṃ nityānāṃ sāmānyasya pārthivadvyaṇukādivṛddhaṃ kāryam asaṃgṛhītaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In 'of all entities,' the word 'all' denotes entirety. <s>Bhāvas</s> are things that are, that experience existence; the meaning is substances, qualities, and actions. It does not mean 'entities' because they come into being. If that were so, the eternal atoms such as earth-atoms would not be included, and the effect, such as the increase of earthy dyads and the like, caused by <s>sāmānya</s> would be left out.
And <s>sāmānya</s> is what will be defined in the passage beginning '<s>sāmānya</s> produces oneness.'
<s>vṛddhi</s> is increase; its cause is a cause of increase.

children.text: etacca sāmānyaṃ sāmānyavato māṃsadravyāder vṛddhikāraṇasya lakṣaṇatvena vṛddhikāraṇamityuktam ||
children.translated_text: And this <s>sāmānya</s> is called a cause of increase because it serves as the definition of an increase-cause, such as meat-substance that possesses sameness.

children.text: yato na sāmānyaṃ māṃsatvādijātirūpaṃ vṛddhau kāraṇaṃ bhavati tathāhi sati sāmānyaṃ bhāsatvarūpaṃ yathā vardhake bhojyarūpe māṃse'sti tathā śarīradhāturūpe vardhanīye'pyasti tataśca nityaṃ māṃsatvasambandhād amāṃsādānām api māṃsena vardhitavyaṃ tasmādvṛddhikāraṇalakṣaṇatvena sāmānyaṃ vṛddhikāraṇamityuktam ||
children.translated_text: For <s>sāmānya</s>, in the form of the universal such as meat-ness, is not itself the cause of increase. If it were so, just as the <s>sāmānya</s> in the form of meat-ness exists in edible meat that increases the body, so it also exists in the bodily tissue that is to be increased; and then, because of the permanent relation with meat-ness, even things other than meat would have to be increased by meat. Therefore <s>sāmānya</s> is called a cause of increase because it defines the cause of increase.

children.text: ata eva vaiśeṣike'pyuktaṃ trayāṇām akāryatvam akāraṇatvaṃ ca iti ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason it is also said in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system, 'The three have neither the status of effect nor the status of cause.'
Here 'of the three' means of <s>sāmānya</s>, <s>viśeṣa</s>, and <s>samavāya</s>.

children.text: ye tu samānam eva sāmānyam iti kṛtvā dravyādyeva sāmānyaśabdenābhidadhati teṣāṃ mate sāmānyaṃ ca viśeṣaṃ ca ityādigranthoktasya sāmānyasya na kiṃcidanenoktaṃ syād ityasaṃbandhārthatvaṃ prakaraṇasya syāt ||
children.translated_text: But those who, taking <s>sāmānya</s> to be simply what is the same, use the word <s>sāmānya</s> for substance and the like themselves: on their view, nothing would be said by this statement about the <s>sāmānya</s> taught in the passage 'sāmānya and viśeṣa,' and the topic would become incoherent and unconnected.

children.text: etacca vṛddhikāraṇatvaṃ sāmānyasya na lakṣaṇaṃ kiṃ tarhyāyurvedopayoginā dharmeṇa nirdeśaḥ lakṣaṇaṃ tu sāmānyamekatvakaram iti kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: And this causality of increase is not the definition of <s>sāmānya</s>. Rather, it is a statement of it through a property useful for <s>Āyurveda</s>. Its definition, however, he will give as '<s>sāmānya</s> produces oneness.'

children.text: evaṃ dravyādāvapi coddeśānantaraṃ nirdeśaṃ kariṣyati khādīnyātmā ityādinā tato ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, after the summary mention of substance and the other categories too, he will make the specific statement beginning 'space and the others, self,' and so on; therefore...

children.text: mātrāśitīye mātrāvadāhārasya balādihetutvaṃ pratipāditaṃ tacca ṛtusātmyamapekṣya kṛtasyāhārasya bhavati tena ṛtupravibhāgapūrvakam ṛtusātmyābhidhāyakaṃ tasyāśitīyaṃ brūte ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Mātrāśitīya</s>, it has been taught that food taken in proper measure is a cause of strength and the like; and that occurs when food is prepared with regard to seasonal suitability. Therefore he states the <s>Tasyāśitīya</s>, which, preceded by a division of the seasons, explains seasonal suitability.
The expression 'beginning with what is eaten' means what is eaten, drunk, licked, and chewed.

children.text: balaṃ varṇaśceti cakāreṇa pūrvādhyāyoktasukhāyuṣī api gṛhyete yadi vā balavarṇābhyāmeva nāntarīyakaṃ kṛtsnaṃ dhātusāmyakāryaṃ sukhādi gṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: 'Strength and complexion': by the word 'and' the happy life and long life mentioned in the preceding chapter are also included. Or else, through strength and complexion alone, all effects of equilibrium of the bodily elements, such as happiness, which necessarily accompany them, are included.
By the word 'known,' he indicates the practice of seasonal suitability preceded by correct knowledge.
By mentioning activity, he includes sexual intercourse, exercise, massage, and the like.
'Dependent on activity and food' means having activity and food as its sphere.

children.text: ṛtujñānamantarā ṛtusātmyajñānaṃ na sambhavatītyṛtūnām upayuktasvarūpajñānārthamāha ihetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Since knowledge of seasonal suitability is not possible without knowledge of the seasons, in order to teach the relevant nature of the seasons he says, 'here,' and so on.

children.text: ṛtupratipādanaprastāve saṃvatsaraṃ vidyāditi saṃvatsarapratipādanamṛtūnāmeva militānāṃ saṃvatsaratvapratipādanārtham ||
children.translated_text: When the division of seasons is being explained, the teaching 'one should know the year' is meant to show that the seasons themselves, when combined, are the year.

children.text: melakaśca buddhyā vyavahriyate na tu paramārthataḥ ṛtūnāṃ melako'sti ||
children.translated_text: And their combination is treated conceptually for practical usage; in ultimate reality there is no combination of the seasons.

children.text: ṛtūnāṃ saṃvatsarātmakatvaṃ punaḥ punasta evartavaḥ parāvartanta iti jñānārthamavaśyaṃ pratipādanīyam ||
children.translated_text: The fact that the seasons have the nature of a year must necessarily be taught, so that one may know that these same seasons revolve again and again.

children.text: iheti iha prakaraṇe ṣaḍaṅgaṃ vidyāt anyatra tu rogabhiṣagjitīyādau tattatkāryavaśād anyathāpi ||
children.translated_text: 'Here' means: in this section one should know the year as six-limbed; elsewhere, however, as in the <s>Rogabhiṣagjitīya</s> and similar chapters, it may be otherwise according to the respective purpose.
And it has been said: 'Time is characterized by cold, heat, and rain,' and so on.

children.text: ṣaḍaṅgamiti samāhāre dviguḥ ṛtuvyatirekeṇa saṃvatsarasyāvidyamānatvāt yadi vā samudāyibhyo'nyaḥ samudāya ityāśritya bahuvrīhiḥ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Six-limbed' is a <s>dvigu</s> compound in the collective sense, since the year does not exist apart from the seasons. Or else, relying on the view that a collection is other than its constituents, it should be taken as a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>.
'There' means: in the statement of the division of seasons.
Movement, that is, going, toward the northern direction is the northern course.

children.text: ādadāti kṣapayati pṛthivyāḥ saumyāṃśaṃ prāṇināṃ ca balamityādānam ||
children.translated_text: Because it takes away, that is, diminishes, the watery portion of the earth and the strength of living beings, it is called <s>ādāna</s> (taking away).

children.text: trīn śiśirādīnityanenaiva labdhe'pi grīṣmāntatve grīṣmāntāniti śiśirasyādiriti vigrahasya tathādiśabdasya prakāravācitāyāḥ pratiṣedhārtham ||
children.translated_text: Although the fact that it ends with summer is already obtained by the words 'the three beginning with winter,' he says 'ending with summer' in order to rule out the analysis 'winter is the beginning' and also the sense that the word 'beginning' denotes a general type.
In the same way, the phrase 'ending with hemanta' is to be explained.
Movement toward the southern direction is the southern course.

children.text: visṛjati janayati āpyamaṃśaṃ prāṇināṃ ca balamiti visargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it releases, that is, produces, the watery portion and the strength of living beings, it is called <s>visarga</s> (release).
The formation of these names is for the sake of practical usage and also for conveying the meaning understood from their etymology.
He indicates the character of <s>visarga</s> in the passage beginning, 'But in <s>visarga</s> again...'.

children.text: yadyapi cādānamādau paṭhitaṃ tathāpi pratilomatantrayuktyādau visargaguṇakathanaṃ yadi vā prathamamādānasyottarāyaṇarūpasya praśastatvādagre'bhidhānam iha tu visargasya balajanakatvenābhipretatvādagre 'bhidhānam ||
children.translated_text: Although <s>ādāna</s> is read first, the qualities of <s>visarga</s> are nevertheless stated first by the reverse-order interpretive principle. Or else, because <s>ādāna</s>, in the form of the northern course, is excellent, it is mentioned first there; but here, because <s>visarga</s> is intended as producing strength, it is mentioned first.
'Not excessively dry' means winds whose roughness is weakened by connection with the gentle time of <s>visarga</s>; they blow in that way.
'The others, however, in <s>ādāna</s>' means winds not calmed and excessively dry, since their undesirable dryness comes from connection with fiery <s>ādāna</s>.
The words 'and the moon,' and so on, are connected with the present topic, <s>visarga</s>.

children.text: avyāhatabala iti kālamārgameghavātādibhistadā sūryasya somaparipanthino hatabalatvāt ||
children.translated_text: 'Of unobstructed strength' means that at that time, by reason of season, path, clouds, winds, and the like, the sun, the opponent of the moon, has its strength impaired.
'By śiśirā' means by cold ones.
The division is as 'śaśvat'.
'Gentle' means predominated by the qualities of the moon.
'Fiery' means predominated by the qualities of fire, that is, possessing unobstructed strength.

children.text: nanvetāvataivādityacandravātānāṃ balavattvamabalavattvaṃ ca kathaṃ bhavatītyāha tāvetāvityādi ||
children.translated_text: But one may object: how, merely from this, do the sun, moon, and winds become strong or weak? To answer this he says, 'these two,' and so on.

children.text: kālo devatārūpaḥ sa ca nityarūpo'pi prāṇināmadṛṣṭena nānārūpeṇa gṛhītaḥ san kadācit sūryabalavāyubalasomabalādīn karoti svabhāvaḥ sūryasya saumyāṃśakṣayakartṛtvādir vāyor virūkṣaṇādiḥ somasyāpyāyanādiḥ mārgo dakṣiṇa uttaraśca tatra dakṣiṇaḥ karkaṭādayo dhanurantāḥ makarādiruttaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Time is in the form of a deity; and although it is eternal in nature, when apprehended in various forms through the unseen karma of living beings, it sometimes produces the strength of the sun, the strength of wind, the strength of the moon, and so on. 'Nature' means, for example, the sun's making the watery portion diminish, wind's drying, and the moon's moistening. 'Path' means the southern and northern courses: there the southern path consists of the signs beginning with <s>Karkaṭa</s> and ending with <s>Dhanuṣ</s>, while the northern begins with <s>Makara</s>.

children.text: ete ca kālasvabhāvamārgaparigrahā yathāsambhavaṃ boddhavyāḥ na hi some mārgaparigrahaḥ kiṃcid viśeṣamāvahati vāyośca mārgaparigraha eva nāsti ||
children.translated_text: These acceptances as time, nature, and path are to be understood as applicable in each case. For acceptance of path brings no particular difference in the case of the moon, and in the case of wind there is no acceptance of path at all.
'Accepted' means connected.

children.text: kālartvādīnāṃ nirvṛtipratyayabhūtā niṣpattikāraṇabhūtāḥ upadiśyante ācāryaiḥ iti śeṣaḥ kālaḥ saṃvatsaro'yanadvayaṃ ca ṛtavaḥ śiśirādayaḥ dehasya balaṃ dehabalam ||
children.translated_text: They are taught by the teachers as grounds of ascertainment, that is, as causes of production, for time, seasons, and the like; this is the supplied construction. 'Time' means the year and the two courses; 'seasons' are winter and the rest; bodily strength is the strength of the body.

children.text: anye tu bruvate saṃvatsarasyāyanadvayasya ca ṛtumelakarūpatvād ṛtugrahaṇe naiva grahaṇaṃ labdhaṃ tena kālagrahaṇaviśeṣaṇaṃ tena kālarūpaḥ ṛturiti strīṇāmevārtavadarśanaṃ yadṛtustadvyāvartyate ||
children.translated_text: Others, however, say: because the year and the two courses have the form of a collection of seasons, they are already obtained simply by the mention of seasons. Therefore the mention of time is a qualifier; by it, the season that is a form of time is distinguished from women's menstruation, which is also called <s>ṛtu</s>.
In the expression 'having become a ground,' the word 'become' is used in the sense of comparison.

children.text: kecid vyākhyānayanti arkavāyū ityekatayā paṭhitvā somaśca iti yat pṛthak paṭhati tenārkvāyvor militayor ādānaṃ prati kāraṇatvaṃ visargaṃ prati pṛthageva somasya kāraṇatvamiti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: Some commentators explain as follows: by reading 'sun and wind' as a single unit, and then reading 'and the moon' separately, he shows that the sun and wind together are causes with respect to <s>ādāna</s>, while the moon alone is separately the cause with respect to <s>visarga</s>.
In this way it should be understood also in cases such as the taking away of strength and the production of strength.
The passage beginning with "there" and so on.
<s>Ādadāna</s>, "taking up," means drying up.
"Of the world" means of what is stationary and moving.
<s>Sneha</s> means the essence, that is, the gentle or moist part.

children.text: na kevalaṃ raviḥ vāyavaśca śoṣayantaḥ snehamiti sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The construction is that not only the sun, but also the winds, dry up the <s>sneha</s>.

children.text: tīvrāśca rūkṣāśca tīvrarūkṣāḥ yadi vā tīvraṃ raukṣyaṃ yeṣāṃ te tīvrarūkṣāḥ etaccādāne tīvreṇa raviṇā sambandhād vāyorbhavati yogavāhitvādvāyoḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tīvrarūkṣāḥ</s> means intense and dry; or, those whose dryness is intense are <s>tīvrarūkṣāḥ</s>. And this, in the period of <s>ādāna</s>, belongs to the wind because of its connection with the intense sun, or because of the wind's being a <s>yogavāhin</s> (carrier of associated qualities).

children.text: uktaṃ hi yogavāhī paraṃ vāyuḥ saṃyogādubhayārthakṛd ityādi ||
children.translated_text: For it has been said: "Wind is the supreme <s>yogavāhin</s>; from conjunction it accomplishes the purpose of both," and so on.

children.text: yathākramamiti śiśire raukṣyamalpaṃ tiktaṃ rasamalpaṃ ca daurbalyaṃ tathā vasante madhyaṃ raukṣyaṃ kaṣāyaṃ rasaṃ madhyaṃ daurbalyaṃ tathā grīṣme prakṛṣṭaṃ raukṣyaṃ kaṭukaṃ rasaṃ mahacca daurbalyaṃ darśayati ||
