children.text: etacca vairodhikakathanaṃ viśeṣavacanena bādhyate tena laśunasya kṣīreṇa pānaṃ kvacin na virodhi yaduktaṃ sādhayecchuddhaśuṣkasya laśunasya catuṣpalam ||
children.translated_text: And this statement of incompatibility is overridden by a specific prescription. Therefore drinking garlic with milk is in some cases not incompatible, as is said: 'One should cook four <s>palas</s> of purified, dried garlic ...'

children.text: kṣīrodake'ṣṭaguṇite kṣīraśeṣaṃ ca pāyayet tathā mūlakasvarasaṃ kṣīram ityādiprayogeṣūnneyam ||
children.translated_text: '... in milk and water increased eightfold, and should have the patient drink it when only the milk remains.' The same should be inferred in prescriptions such as 'radish juice and milk.'

children.text: kiṃvā anekadravyasaṃyogād atra virodhinām avirodhaḥ virodhimātrasaṃyoga eva virodhī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Or, because there is a combination of many substances here, the incompatible things are not incompatible; only a combination consisting merely of incompatible things is incompatible.

children.text: yattu madhuna uṣṇena vamanena saṃyuktasya satyapi madanaphalādidravyasaṃyoge 'virodhārthamuktam apakvagamanādi tanmadhuno dravyāntarasaṃyoge 'pyuṣṇasambandhatve virodhitvopadarśanārthaṃ yato viṣānvayaṃ madhu viṣasya coṣṇavirodhi ||
children.translated_text: But what is said, beginning with 'going undigested,' concerning honey combined with a warm emetic, even though it is combined with substances such as <s>madanaphala</s>, is stated with reference to non-incompatibility in order to show that honey is incompatible when associated with heat even in combination with another substance; for honey has an affinity with poison, and poison is incompatible with heat.

children.text: laśunādīnāṃ tu dravyāntarāsaṃyoge satyeva melako viruddha iti śāstravacanādunnīyate ||
children.translated_text: In the case of garlic and the like, however, it is inferred from the scriptural statement that the mixture is incompatible only when there is no combination with another substance.
'With things opposed to that' means with things that remove impotence and the like.
'With such things' means with things opposed to diseases produced by incompatible food.
<s>Abhisaṃskāra</s> means conditioning the body through constant use.
Or 'with such things' means with rejuvenative applications.
This should be understood as treatment of an illness not yet arisen.

children.text: saṃgrahe dravyasaṃkhyā rasāśrayā iti bhedaścaiṣām ityādinā rasasaṃkhyā hi paramārthato dravyasaṃkhyaiva nirguṇatvād rasānām iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the summary, by statements such as 'the number of substances rests on tastes' and 'these are the divisions of them,' the intention is that the number of tastes is in ultimate reality just the number of substances, since tastes themselves have no qualities.

children.text: kāraṇaṃ rasasaṃkhyāyā iti rasānāṃ tatra yogyatvād ityādinā vibhaktayo bhedaḥ tatra madhura ityādinā ||
children.translated_text: The cause of the number of tastes is stated in the passage beginning 'because they are suitable there'; their divisions are stated in the passage beginning 'there, sweet,' and so on.

children.text: uddeśo dravyāṇāṃ śītaṃ vīryeṇa ityādinā apavādo dravyāṇāṃ madhuraṃ kiṃcit ityādinā ||
children.translated_text: The enumeration of substances is given in the passage beginning 'cold by potency'; the exceptions among substances are given in the passage beginning 'some sweet thing,' and so on.

children.text: samprati sāmānyenoktānāṃ guṇakarmabhyāṃ prativyaktyanuktānāṃ prativyaktiprāya upayogidravyasya viśiṣṭaguṇakarmakathanārtham annapānavidhir adhyāyo'bhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Now, for substances whose qualities and actions have been stated generally, but not mostly one by one for each individual item, the chapter on the rule of food and drink is set forth in order to state the specific qualities and actions of useful substances chiefly item by item.
Here the <s>cha</s> suffix that has arisen is elided.

children.text: atrānne kāṭhinyasāmānyāt khādyaṃ pāne ca dravatvasāmānyāllehyam avaruddhaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Here, because of the common feature of hardness in food, what is chewable should be understood as included; and in drink, because of the common feature of liquidity, what is lickable is included.

children.text: annapānaṃ vidhīyate viśiṣṭaguṇakarmayogitayā pratipādyate 'nenetyannapānavidhiḥ dravyāṇāṃ guṇakarmakathanam eva cānnapānavidhiḥ yatastaddhi jñātvānnapānaṃ vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Food and drink are prescribed, that is, taught as connected with specific qualities and actions, by this; therefore it is called the rule of food and drink. And the rule of food and drink is just the statement of the qualities and actions of substances, since, after knowing that, food and drink are prescribed.
What does that food and drink do? He states this with the words beginning "desired."

children.text: iṣṭamiti abhimataṃ hitaṃ ca kiṃvā iṣṭaṃ priyaṃ hitaṃ tu vidhivihitaśabdenaiva prāpyate ||
children.translated_text: "Desired" means approved and beneficial; or "desired" means pleasing, while "beneficial" is obtained precisely through the word "prescribed according to rule."

children.text: vidhir vakṣyamāṇarasavimāne tadetadāhāravidhānam ityādigranthavācyaḥ tathendriyopakramaṇīye nāratnapāṇiḥ ityādinoktaṃ vidhānaṃ tena vidhinā vihitaṃ vidhivihitam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>vidhi</s> (rule) is what is denoted by the forthcoming passage in the Rasavimāna, beginning "this prescription of diet," and likewise the prescription stated in the Indriyopakramanīya with the words beginning "not one with jewels in hand." What is prescribed by that rule is "prescribed according to rule."
Here, in the series beginning with color, sound is not included because sound is generally absent in food and drink.

children.text: varṇādiṣu yadyat prathamam annapāne gṛhyate tattat pūrvam uktam ||
children.translated_text: Among color and the rest, whatever is apprehended first in food and drink is mentioned first.

children.text: rasastu sparśasya paścādgṛhyamāṇo'pi prādhānyakhyāpanārthaṃ sparśasyāgre kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But <s>rasa</s> (taste), although apprehended after touch, is placed before touch in order to show its predominance.

children.text: prāṇinām ityanenaiva labdhe'pi prāṇisaṃjñakānām iti vacanaṃ sthāvaraprāṇipratiṣedhārthaṃ vṛkṣādayo hi vanaspatisattvānukāropadeśācchastre prāṇina uktāḥ na tu loke prāṇisaṃjñakāḥ kiṃtarhi jaṅgamā eva ||
children.translated_text: Although it is already obtained through the phrase "of living beings," the expression "of those called living beings" is meant to exclude stationary living beings. For trees and the like are called living beings in the treatise because of the teaching that plant beings resemble sentient beings, but in common usage they are not called living beings; rather, only moving creatures are.

children.text: iha ca manuṣyasyaivādhikṛtatve'pi sāmānyena sakalaprāṇiprāṇahetutayāhārakathanaṃ manuṣavyatirikte'pi prāṇinyāhārasya prāṇajanakatvopadarśanārtham ||
children.translated_text: And although the human being alone is the topic here, food is discussed generally as the cause of life for all living beings in order to show that food produces life even in beings other than humans.
It is called "life" because it is a cause of life, just as ghee is called long life.

children.text: atha kathaṃ tat prāṇamācakṣata ityāha pratyakṣaphaladarśanāditi ||
children.translated_text: Then how do they call it life? He answers: because its result is seen directly.

children.text: pratyakṣeṇaiva hy āhāraṃ vidhinā kurvatāṃ prāṇā anuvartanta iti tathā nirāhārāṇāṃ prāṇā nahy avatiṣṭhanta iti dṛśyata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For it is seen that the life-breaths continue in those who take food according to rule, and likewise that the life-breaths do not remain in those without food. This is the meaning.

children.text: pratyakṣaśabdaś ceha sphuṭapramāṇe vartate yataḥ prāṇānām annakāryatvam anumānagamyameva ||
children.translated_text: The word "direct" here means a clear means of knowledge, since the fact that the life-breaths are an effect of food is itself known by inference.

children.text: ānnakāryatva eva prāṇānāṃ hetumāha tadindhanā hītyādinā ||
children.translated_text: He gives the reason why the life-breaths are an effect of food with the words beginning "for they have that as fuel."

children.text: yasmād antaragnisthitiś cānnapānahetunā agnisthitiśca prāṇahetuḥ tato'nnaṃ prāṇā iti bhāvaḥ uktaṃ hi balam ārogyamāyuśca prāṇāścāgnau pratiṣṭhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since the maintenance of the inner <s>agni</s> (digestive fire) depends on food and drink, and the maintenance of fire is a cause of life, the intention is that food is <s>prāṇa</s> (life). For it has been said: strength, health, lifespan, and life-breaths are established in fire.

children.text: kiṃvā pūrvamannapānasya prāṇahetutvamuktaṃ tadindhanā hītyādināgnihetutvaṃ varṇyate ||
children.translated_text: Or, previously the causality of food and drink with respect to life was stated; with the words beginning "for they have that as fuel," their causality with respect to fire is described.
"It strengthens <s>sattva</s>" means that it produces mental strength.
"The arrangement of the <s>dhātus</s>" means the aggregate of the tissue-elements.
"The opposite" means what is used contrary to rule.

children.text: annapānaṃ vidhīyate yena taṃ vidhiṃ dravyaguṇakarmarūpaṃ tathā caraśarīrāvayavādirūpaṃ cākhilena kārtsnyenopadekṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We shall teach completely the rule by which food and drink are prescribed, in the form of substances, qualities, and actions, and likewise in the form of movement, body, parts, and so on.

children.text: yadyapi ceha dravyaṃ prati prati guṇakarmabhyāṃ na nirdekṣyati vakṣyati hi annapānaikadeśo'yamuktaḥ prāyopayogikaḥ iti tathāpyanuktānām api dravyāṇāṃ caraśarīrāvayavādyupadeśena tathā pūrvādhyāyoktapārthivādidravyaguṇakarmakathanena ca tadvidhānamapyuktaṃ bhavatītyata uktamakhileneti vakṣyati hi yathā nānauṣadhaṃ kiṃcid deśajānāṃ vaco yathā ||
children.translated_text: Although here each substance will not be described together with its qualities and actions, for he will say, "This one part of food and drink has been stated, being commonly used," nevertheless the prescription of even unstated substances is also stated through the teaching on movement, body, parts, and so on, and through the description in the preceding chapters of the substances, qualities, and actions of things made of earth and the other elements. Therefore he said "completely." For he will say: "Just as, according to the speech of those born in a region, there is nothing that is not a medicine,"

children.text: dravyaṃ tu tattathā vācyamanuktamiha yad bhavet tathā caraḥ śarīrāvayavāḥ ityādi kiṃvā vidhiśabdo 'śitapītalīḍhakhāditaprakāravācī tena cāśitādayaḥ sarva evākhilena vācyaḥ tatkāraṇabhūtāni tu dravyāṇi raktaśālyādīnyekadeśenoktāni ato vakṣyati annapānaikadeśo'yamuktaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: "but a substance that may be unstated here should be described in that same way; likewise movement, bodily parts, and so on." Or else the word <s>vidhi</s> denotes the modes of what is eaten, drunk, licked, and chewed; and by that word all such eaten things and the rest are to be described completely. But the substances that are their causes, such as red śāli rice, are mentioned only in part. Therefore he will say, "This one part of food and drink has been stated."

children.text: annapāne ca vaktavye yaddravyaṃ prāya upayujyate tasya sāmānyaguṇamabhidhāya vargasaṃgraheṇa guṇamupadekṣyati ||
children.translated_text: When food and drink are to be discussed, he will state the general quality of the substance that is mostly used, and then teach its qualities by collecting it into classes.

children.text: udakābhidhānaṃ cāgre kṛtam udakasyānne pāne ca vyāpriyamāṇatvāt ||
children.translated_text: The mention of water is made first because water functions in both food and drink.

children.text: tad ityudāharaṇaṃ kiṃvā sa svabhāvo yasya sa tatsvabhāvaḥ tasmāt kledanasvabhāvād ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "That" is an example; or else, that whose nature is such is "of that nature." Thus it means "because it has a moistening nature."

children.text: yadyapi udakamāśvāsakarāṇāṃ jalaṃ stambhanānām ityuktaṃ tathāpīhānuktakledanakarmābhidhānārthaṃ punarucyate ||
children.translated_text: Although it has been said, "among things that refresh, water," and "among things that check, water," nevertheless it is repeated here in order to state the previously unstated action of moistening.

children.text: iha jalalavaṇādīnāṃ yat karmocyate tatteṣāmitarakarmabhyaḥ pradhānaṃ jñeyam agryādhikāre tu tatkarmakartṛdravyāntarapraśastatā jñeyā ||
children.translated_text: Here, whatever action is stated for water, salt, and the rest should be understood as primary among their other actions. But in the section on foremost things, the excellence of another substance that performs that action should be understood.

children.text: kṣāraḥ pacantamagniṃ pācayati tena pācayatīti hetau ṇic ||
children.translated_text: Alkali cooks the digestive fire while it is cooking; therefore the causative in "it causes to cook" is used in the sense of causing.

children.text: snehayatītyādau tu tatkaroti tadācaṣṭe iti ṇic ||
children.translated_text: But in expressions such as "it makes oily," the causative means "it does that" or "it declares that."
"It joins together" means that it connects separated skin, flesh, and the like.
"Juice" means meat juice.

children.text: prīṇayatīti kṣīṇān puṣṇāti na tv atibṛhattvaṃ karoti tena māṃsakarmaṇā bṛṃhaṇena samaṃ naikyam ||
children.translated_text: "It satisfies" means that it nourishes those who are wasted, not that it makes them excessively large. Therefore it is not identical with the meat-action called <s>bṛṃhaṇa</s> (bulk-promoting).

children.text: jarjarīkarotīti ślathamāṃsādyupacayaṃ karoti yad uktaṃ hārīte surā jarjarīkarotyasṛṅmedobāhulyāt iti tathā hy atraivoktaṃ surā kṛśānāṃ puṣṭyartham iti ||
children.translated_text: "It makes flabby" means that it produces a loose accumulation of flesh and the like. As <s>Hārīta</s> has said, "<s>surā</s> makes one flabby because of an abundance of blood and fat." And accordingly it has been said right here: "<s>surā</s> is for the nourishment of the emaciated."

children.text: avadhamayatīti vilikhatītyarthaḥ anekārthatvād dhātūnāṃ vacanaṃ hi lekhanaḥ śītarasikaḥ iti tathā hārīte 'pyuktaṃ sīdhur avadhamayati vāyvagniprabodhanāt iti ||
children.translated_text: "It scrapes" means "it abrades," because verbal roots have many meanings. For there is the statement, "it is scraping and cold-tasting." Likewise <s>Hārīta</s> also said, "<s>sīdhu</s> scrapes because it awakens wind and fire."

children.text: ācinoti doṣān iti śeṣaḥ tantrāntaravacanaṃ hi vātapittakaphāṃstasmādācinoti ca phāṇitam iti ||
children.translated_text: The remainder is: "it accumulates the <s>doṣa</s>s." For the statement of another treatise is: "Therefore molasses also accumulates <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>."

children.text: piṇyākaḥ tilakalkaḥ nighaṇṭukāras tv āha piṇyāko haritaśigruḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Piṇyāka</s> is sesame paste. But the author of the lexicon says: "<s>Piṇyāka</s> is green <s>śigru</s>."
"It makes one languish" means it causes a loss of cheerfulness.

children.text: prabhūtāntarmalasya purīṣasya kartā prabhūtāntarmalaḥ yadyapi māṣo bahumalaḥ iti vakṣyati tathāpi māṣavikṛteḥ sūpasyeha guṇakathanaṃ tena na punaruktaṃ na cāvaśyaṃ prakṛtidharmo vikṛtimanugacchati yataḥ saktūnāṃ siddhapiṇḍikā gurvī eva bhavati tasmān māṣavikṛtāv api malavṛddhidarśanārtham etadabhidhānam ||
children.translated_text: "Having abundant inner waste" means that it produces abundant inner waste, namely feces. Although it will be said that <s>māṣa</s> is rich in waste, here the qualities of soup, a preparation of <s>māṣa</s>, are being described; therefore this is not repetition. Nor does a property of the original substance necessarily follow the derivative preparation, since a cooked lump made from flour is certainly heavy. Therefore this statement is made in order to show increase of waste even in a preparation of <s>māṣa</s>.

children.text: kṣārasya pācanatvaṃ guṇo'bhihitaḥ iha tu dṛṣṭiśukraghnatvaṃ doṣa iti pṛthagucyate ||
children.translated_text: The digestive power of alkali has been stated as a quality; here, however, its destruction of eyesight and semen is separately stated as a fault.
"Generally productive of <s>pitta</s>" means that sour taste, more particularly than the other salty and pungent substances, is productive of <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: evamanyatrāpi prāyaḥśabdo viśeṣārtho vācyaḥ kiṃvā prāyaḥśabdo'mlena sambadhyate ||
children.translated_text: So too elsewhere the word "generally" should be understood as having a specifying sense; or else the word "generally" is connected with "sour."

children.text: atra pittam ādāv amlajanyatayoktaṃ doṣaprādhānyasyāniyatatvāt uktaṃ hi na te pṛthak pittakaphānilebhya iti tathā samapittānilakaphā iti kiṃvā pittoṣmā vahniḥ sa cehānnapānapacane pradhānaṃ yaduktaṃ yadannaṃ dehadhātvojobalavarṇādipoṣakam ||
children.translated_text: Here <s>pitta</s> is mentioned first because it is produced by sour taste, since predominance among the <s>doṣa</s>s is not fixed. For it has been said: "They are not separate from <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>anila</s>," and likewise, "with <s>pitta</s>, <s>anila</s>, and <s>kapha</s> equal." Or else, the fire is the heat of <s>pitta</s>, and that is primary here in the digestion of food and drink, as has been said: "Whatever food nourishes the bodily tissues, vitality, strength, complexion, and the rest--

children.text: tatrāgnir hetur āhārān nahy apakvād rasādayaḥ iti teneha vahnikāraṇapittajanakam evādāv ucyate yataśca pittajanakamagre vaktavyam ato rasapradhānamapi madhuro nādāv uktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there the digestive fire is the cause; for from undigested food there are no <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues." Therefore here what produces <s>pitta</s>, the cause of fire, is stated first. And because that which produces <s>pitta</s> had to be stated first, sweet, though predominant among the tastes, was not mentioned first.

children.text: madhuna iti vicchedapāṭhena navānavasya madhunaḥ kaphākartṛtvaṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By reading it with the separation "of honey," he shows that fresh and old honey do not produce <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: iha ca ṣaḍrasasyaiva kathanametattrayeṇaiva anuktānāṃ lavaṇatiktakaṣāyāṇām api pākadvārā grahaṇāt yato lavaṇaḥ pākāt prāyo madhuraḥ tiktakaṣāyau kaṭukau pākato bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And here the statement concerns the six tastes alone, because through these three the unstated salty, bitter, and astringent tastes are also included by way of <s>pāka</s> (post-digestive transformation): for salt, through <s>pāka</s>, is generally sweet, while bitter and astringent become pungent through <s>pāka</s>.

children.text: prāyaḥ sarvaṃ tiktam ityādistu grantho hārītīyaḥ iha kenāpi pramādāl likhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the passage beginning "generally everything bitter" belongs to <s>Hārīta</s>; it has been written here by someone through error.
"Collection by group" means the gathering of food substances such as awned grains by class.
In the phrase beginning "taste, potency," <s>prabhāva</s> (specific effect) is read separately because its scope is limited.

children.text: rasādinirdeśaśca yathāyogyatayā jñeyaḥ tena na sarvadravye sarvarasādyabhidhānaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: And the indication of taste and the rest should be understood as applying according to suitability. Therefore every substance will not have every taste and so forth stated for it.

children.text: atra śūkadhānyam ādāv āhārapradhānatvāt śūkavanti dhānyāni śūkadhānyāni ||
children.translated_text: Here awned grain is first because it is chief among foods. Grains that have awns are awned grains.

children.text: iha ca dravyanāmāni nānādeśaprasiddhāni tena nāmajñāne sāmarthyaṃ tathābhūtaṃ nāstyevānyeṣām api ṭīkākṛtāṃ tena deśāntaribhyo nāma prāyaśo jñeyaṃ yattu pracarati gauḍe tal likhiṣyāmo 'nyadeśaprasiddhaṃ ca kiṃcit ||
children.translated_text: Here the names of substances are established in various regions; therefore even other commentators do not really possess the requisite capacity for knowing all the names. Hence names must generally be learned from people of other regions. We shall write what is current in <s>Gauḍa</s>, and also some names established in other regions.
<s>Kalama</s> is known by its own name in the <s>Vedāgrahāra</s>s.
<s>Śakunāhṛta</s> is known in <s>Śrāvastī</s> by the name <s>Vakra</s>.
<s>Raktaśāli</s> is itself well known.
<s>Mahāśāli</s> is known in <s>Magadha</s>.

children.text: atra ca śālirhaimantikaṃ dhānyaṃ ṣaṣṭikādayaśca graiṣmikāḥ vrīhayaḥ śāradā iti vyavasthā ||
children.translated_text: And here <s>śāli</s> is winter grain, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> and the others are summer grains, and <s>vrīhi</s>s are autumn grains: this is the arrangement.
Although <s>raktaśāli</s> and the others have sweet <s>pāka</s>, their property of binding the feces is due specifically to <s>prabhāva</s>.

children.text: mahāṃstasyānviti raktaśāleranu tena raktaśāliguṇā mahāśāler manāgalpāḥ evaṃ tasyānu kalama ityatrāpi vācyam ||
children.translated_text: "Great, following it" means following <s>raktaśāli</s>. Therefore the qualities of <s>mahāśāli</s> are only slightly less than those of <s>raktaśāli</s>. The same should be said in the phrase "after it, <s>kalama</s>."
"Of it" means of <s>mahāśāli</s>.

children.text: tataḥ pare iti śakunāhṛtādayaḥ uttarottaramalpaguṇā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Those after that" means <s>śakunāhṛta</s> and the rest; the meaning is that each succeeding one has fewer qualities.

children.text: guṇāguṇair iti śālīnāṃ raktaśālyādīnāṃ ye guṇās tṛṣṇāghnatvatrimalāpahatvādayaḥ teṣām aguṇais tadguṇaviparītair doṣair yavakādayo 'nukāraṃ kurvanti tataśca yavakās tṛṣṇātrimalādikarā iti ||
children.translated_text: "By qualities and non-qualities" means this: the qualities of the <s>śāli</s> rices such as <s>raktaśāli</s>, namely removal of thirst and elimination of the three wastes and the like, are imitated by <s>yavaka</s> and the others through non-qualities, that is, faults opposite to those qualities. Consequently <s>yavaka</s> and the others cause thirst, the three wastes, and so on.
And the word "quality" here is used in the sense of praise.

children.text: ṣaṣṭikaguṇe 'kārapraśleṣād agururiti boddhavyaṃ mātrāśitīye ṣaṣṭiko laghuḥ paṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the qualities of <s>ṣaṣṭika</s>, because of coalescence with the letter a, it should be understood as "not heavy"; in the <s>Mātrāśitīya</s>, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> is read as light.
"And after that" means that white <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> and the rest have qualities only slightly inferior.

children.text: varakoddālakādayaḥ ṣaṣṭikaviśeṣāḥ kecit kudhānyāni varakādīni vadanti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Varaka</s>, <s>uddālaka</s>, and the others are varieties of <s>ṣaṣṭika</s>. Some say that <s>varaka</s> and the others are inferior grains.
<s>Vrīhi</s> is the name for autumnal awned grain.
<s>Pāṭala</s> is a variety of <s>vrīhi</s>.

children.text: tantrāntare'pi paṭhyate tridoṣastveva pāṭalaḥ iti suśrute pāṭalaśabdenaitadvyatirikto dhānyaviśeṣo jñeyaḥ tena tadguṇakathanena neha virodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is also read in another treatise: "<s>Pāṭala</s> is surely tridoṣic." In <s>Suśruta</s>, by the word <s>pāṭala</s>, a grain variety different from this should be understood. Therefore there is no contradiction here with the statement of its qualities there.
<s>Koradūṣa</s> and the others are varieties of inferior grain.

children.text: koradūṣaḥ kodravaḥ koradūṣasya kevalasya śleṣmapittaghnatvaṃ tena yaduktaṃ raktapittanidāne yadā janturyavakoddālakakoradūṣaprāyāṇy annāni bhuṅkte ityādinā pittakartṛtvaṃ koradūṣasya tat tatraivoktaniṣpāvakāñjikādiyuktasya saṃyogamahimnā boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Koradūṣa</s> is <s>kodrava</s>. The destruction of <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s> belongs to <s>koradūṣa</s> by itself. Therefore, in the diagnosis of <s>raktapitta</s>, where <s>koradūṣa</s> is said to produce <s>pitta</s> in the statement beginning, "When a person eats foods consisting mostly of <s>yavaka</s>, <s>uddālaka</s>, and <s>koradūṣa</s>," that should be understood as due to the power of combination with <s>niṣpāva</s>, sour gruel, and the like, which are stated there itself.
<s>Śyāmāka</s> and the others too are particular kinds of grass grain.

children.text: hastiśyāmākaḥ śyāmākabheda eva nīvāra uḍikā gavedhuko ghuluñcaḥ sa grāmyāraṇyabhedena dvividhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hastiśyāmāka</s> is simply a variety of <s>śyāmāka</s>. <s>Nīvāra</s>, <s>uḍikā</s>, <s>gavedhuka</s>, and <s>ghuluñca</s>: it is twofold, by the distinction between cultivated and wild.

children.text: praśāntikā uḍikaiva sthalajā raktaśūkā ambhaḥśyāmākā jalajā oḍikā loke ḍe ityucyate priyaṅguḥ kāṅganī iti prasiddhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Praśāntikā</s> is just <s>uḍikā</s> grown on dry land. <s>Raktaśūkā</s> and <s>ambhaḥśyāmākā</s> are water-grown. <s>Oḍikā</s> is called <s>ḍe</s> in common speech. <s>Priyaṅgu</s> is well known as <s>kāṅganī</s>.

children.text: mukundo vākasatṛṇa iti varukaḥ śaṇabījaṃ varakaḥ śyāmabījaṃ śibiras tīrabhuktau siddhaka ityucyate jūrṇāhvo jonāra iti khyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mukunda</s> is <s>vākasatṛṇa</s>. <s>Varuka</s> is hemp seed. <s>Varaka</s> is dark seed. <s>Śibira</s> is called <s>siddhaka</s> in the region of <s>Tīrabhukti</s>. That which is named <s>jūrṇa</s> is known as <s>jonāra</s>.

children.text: yavasya gurorapi bahuvātatvaṃ rūkṣatvāt kiṃvā suśrute yavo laghuḥ paṭhitaḥ tenātrāpyagururiti mantavyaṃ balyaśca srotaḥśuddhikaratvāt prabhāvādvā ||
children.translated_text: Barley, though heavy, has abundant <s>vāta</s>-producing character because of its dryness. Or else, since barley is read as light in <s>Suśruta</s>, here too it should be regarded as not heavy. And it is strengthening because it purifies the channels, or else by its specific effect.

children.text: asya ca śītamadhurakaṣāyatvenānuktamapi pittahantṛtvaṃ labhyata eva tena suśrute kaphapittahantā ityuktamupapannam ||
children.translated_text: And since it is cold, sweet, and astringent, its unstated property of destroying <s>pitta</s> is certainly obtained. Therefore the statement in <s>Suśruta</s> that it destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> is appropriate.

children.text: godhūmasya svāduśītasnigdhādiguṇopayogāc chleṣmakartṛtvaṃ bhavatyeva ata eva suśrute śleṣmakara ityuktam ||
children.translated_text: Because wheat has qualities such as sweetness, coldness, and unctuousness, it certainly produces <s>śleṣman</s> (kapha). For this very reason <s>Suśruta</s> says that it produces <s>śleṣman</s>.

children.text: yattu vasante kaphapradhāne yavagodhūmabhojanaḥ ityuktaṃ tat purāṇagodhūmābhiprāyeṇa purāṇaśca godhūmaḥ kaphaṃ na karotītyuktam eva prāyaḥ śleṣmalaṃ madhuram ityādinā granthenātraivādhyāye ||
children.translated_text: But the statement that in spring, when <s>kapha</s> is predominant, one should eat barley and wheat is intended with reference to old wheat. And it has already been said that old wheat does not produce <s>kapha</s>, in the passage in this very chapter beginning, "as a rule, sweet things are <s>śleṣmala</s> (kapha-producing)."
<s>Nandīmukhī</s>, <s>yavikā</s>, and <s>madhūlī</s> are varieties of wheat.
This is the point here.
This is the meaning of the expression "in this manner."

children.text: samāpta iti vaktavye samāpyata iti yat karoti tena jñāpayati yat bahudravyatvān nāyaṃ samāpto gaṇaḥ kiṃtu yathā kathaṃcit prasiddhaguṇakathanena samāpyate ||
children.translated_text: When he ought to say "it is completed," he instead says "is being completed"; by doing so he indicates that, because there are many substances, this group is not fully completed, but is only somehow brought to a close by stating the qualities of well-known items.

children.text: evamanyatrāpi ṣaṣṭho vargaḥ samāpyata ityādau vyākhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: So too elsewhere, in statements such as "the sixth group is being completed," it should be explained in this way.
Although <s>mudga</s> is to be discussed in the class of leguminous grains under the heading of grain, it is defined separately because of its importance.
<s>Sūpya</s> is leguminous grain suitable for soup. Among them the best is the best of the <s>sūpya</s>s.

children.text: vṛṣya ityādimāṣaguṇe snigdhoṣṇamadhuratvādiguṇayogādeva vātaharatve labdhe punastadabhidhānaṃ viśeṣavātahantṛtvapratipādanārtham evamanyatrāpyevaṃjātīye vyākhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: In the qualities of <s>māṣa</s>, beginning with "aphrodisiac," since its property of removing <s>vāta</s> is already obtained from qualities such as unctuousness, heat, and sweetness, the repeated statement of that is for the purpose of indicating that it destroys <s>vāta</s> in a special way. The same should be explained elsewhere in cases of this kind.
"Masculinity" means semen.

children.text: śīghramiti vacanena śukrasrutikaratvalakṣaṇamapi vṛṣyatvaṃ māṣasya darśayati śukrasrutikaraṃ ca vṛṣyaśabdenocyata eva vacanaṃ hi śukrasrutikaraṃ kiṃcit kiṃcit śukravivardhanam ||
children.translated_text: By the word "quickly," he shows that the aphrodisiac property of <s>māṣa</s> also consists in causing the flow of semen. And what causes the flow of semen is indeed denoted by the word <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac). For there is the statement: "Some aphrodisiac causes the flow of semen; some increases semen."

children.text: srutivṛddhikaraṃ kiṃcittrividhaṃ vṛṣyamucyate iti tadevaṃ sampūrṇavṛṣyatvaṃ māṣe boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: "Some causes both flow and increase: thus an aphrodisiac is said to be threefold." Therefore complete aphrodisiac power should be understood in <s>māṣa</s>.

children.text: rājamāṣaguṇakathane tatsvāduriti māṣavatsvāduḥ kiṃvā rūkṣaścetyādi pāṭhāntaram ||
children.translated_text: In the statement of the qualities of <s>rājamāṣa</s>, "that is sweet" means that it is sweet like <s>māṣa</s>; or else there is another reading, "and it is dry," and so on.

children.text: uṣṇa ityādinā kulatthaguṇaḥ kulatthaśca śuklakṛṣṇacitralohitabhedena caturvidho bhavati tathā grāmyavanyabhedena ca dvividho'pi ata eva tantrāntare vanyaḥ kulatthastadvacca viśeṣān netraroganut ityuktam ||
children.translated_text: With the passage beginning "hot," the quality of <s>kulattha</s> is stated. <s>Kulattha</s> is fourfold, divided into white, black, variegated, and red; and it is also twofold by the division into cultivated and wild. For this very reason another treatise says, "Wild <s>kulattha</s> is like that; and, because of its special properties, it removes eye diseases."
<s>Makuṣṭaka</s> is known as <s>moṭha</s>.
<s>Caṇaka</s> is well known.
<s>Khaṇḍikā</s> is three-valved pea. <s>Hareṇu</s> is round pea.
<s>Kalāya</s> is <s>vātala</s> (vāta-producing); this refers to the three-valved pea.

children.text: tilaguṇo yadyapi viśeṣeṇa noktaḥ tathāpi pradhāne kṛṣṇatile jñeyaḥ uktaṃ hi suśrute tileṣu sarveṣvasitaḥ pradhāno madhyaḥ sito hīnatarās tato'nye iti ||
children.translated_text: Although the quality of sesame is not stated specifically, still it should be understood with reference to the chief sesame, namely black sesame. For <s>Suśruta</s> has said: "Among all sesames the black is foremost, the white is middling, and the others are inferior."
"Various kinds of legumes" means the varieties of <s>kuśimbī</s> that are black, yellow, red, and white.
Some read the passage beginning, "The legume is dry."
The division is: "<s>Āḍhakī</s>, <s>tuvarī</s>, is <s>vātala</s> (vāta-producing)."
"Removing <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>" is the quality of the seed of <s>avalguja</s> and <s>aiḍagaja</s>.
<s>Niṣpāva</s> is <s>valla</s>.

children.text: kākāṇḍaḥ śūkaraśimbiḥ umā atasī ūrṇāṃpāṭhapakṣe tasyaivorṇā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kākāṇḍa</s> is pig-legume. <s>Umā</s> is flax. On the reading <s>ūrṇā</s>, that very same plant is <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: śamīdhānyavarga ityatra śamī śimbiḥ tadantargataṃ dhānyam ||
children.translated_text: In the phrase "the class of leguminous grains," <s>śamī</s> means a pod, and the grain contained within it is meant.
After the <s>sūpya</s>s, because meat is important as a relish, the class of meats is discussed.

children.text: kharaḥ gardabhaḥ aśvataraḥ vegasaraḥ sa cāśvāyāṃ kharājjātaḥ dvīpī citravyāghraḥ ṛkṣaḥ bhallūkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khara</s> is the donkey. <s>Aśvatara</s> is the mule, also called <s>vegasara</s>, and it is born from a donkey and a mare. <s>Dvīpin</s> is the spotted tiger. <s>Ṛkṣa</s> is the bear.

children.text: vṛkaḥ kukkurānukārī paśuśatruḥ tarakṣuḥ vyāghrabhedaḥ taraccha iti khyātaḥ babhruḥ atilomaśaḥ kukkuraḥ parvatopakaṇṭhe bhavati kecid bṛhannakulam āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛka</s> is an enemy of cattle resembling a dog. <s>Tarakṣu</s> is a kind of tiger, known as <s>taraccha</s>. <s>Babhru</s> is a very hairy dog that lives near mountains; some say it is a large mongoose.
<s>Lopāka</s> is a small jackal with a large tail.
<s>Śyena</s> is the well-known bird.
<s>Vāntāda</s> is the dog.
<s>Cāṣa</s> is known as the golden crow.
<s>Śaśaghnī</s> is known as <s>pāñji</s>.
<s>Bhāsa</s> is an ash-colored crested bird in the class of predatory animals.
<s>Kuliṅga</s> is the black sparrow.

children.text: kākulīmṛgaḥ māluyāsarpa iti khyātaḥ tasya śveta ityādayaś catvāro bhedāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kākulīmṛga</s> is known as <s>māluyāsarpa</s>. Its four varieties are white and the others.
<s>Kūrcikā</s> is <s>saṃkuca</s>.
<s>Cillaṭa</s> is <s>ciyāra</s>.

children.text: śallako mahāśakalī śalaka iti khyātaḥ gaṇḍakaḥ godhābhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śallaka</s> is the great scaled one, known as <s>śalaka</s>. <s>Gaṇḍaka</s> is a variety of monitor lizard.
<s>Kadalī</s> is known as <s>kadalīhaṭṭa</s>.
<s>Śvāvit</s> is known as <s>sejjaka</s>.
"Sleeping on the ground" means dwelling in holes.
<s>Sṛmara</s> is the great boar.
The <s>camara</s> is the animal called <s>keśamṛtyu</s>.
The <s>khaḍga</s> is the rhinoceros.
The <s>gavaya</s> is one shaped like a cow.
The <s>nyaṅku</s> is the deer called <s>nyaṅkuśa</s>.
The <s>ruru</s> is a deer with many horns.
The <s>śiśumāra</s> is the crocodile with a cow-like snout.
The <s>timiṅgila</s> is a great sea fish.

children.text: śuktiḥ muktāprabhavo jantuḥ ūdraḥ jalabiḍālaḥ kumbhīraḥ ghaṭikāvān culukī śuśu iti khyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>śukti</s> is the creature from which pearls arise; the <s>ūdra</s> is the water-cat; the <s>kumbhīra</s> is one having a pot-like form; the <s>culukī</s> is known as <s>śuśu</s>.

children.text: śiśumārādīnāṃ matsyagrahaṇena grahaṇe prāpte viśeṣavyavahārārthaṃ punarabhidhānam ||
children.translated_text: Although <s>śiśumāra</s> and the others would be included when fish are mentioned, they are named again for the sake of a special usage.
The <s>haṃsa</s>, in all its four kinds, beginning with the <s>rājahaṃsa</s>, is to be included.
The <s>krauñca</s> is known as <s>koñca</s>.
The <s>baka</s> is a white-winged bird.
The <s>balākā</s> is white.
The <s>kāraṇḍava</s> has a crow-like beak.
The <s>plava</s> is known by its own name and has a pouch-like throat.
The <s>śarāri</s> is called <s>śarālī</s> in common speech.
The <s>madgu</s> is the water-crow.
The <s>kādamba</s> is the <s>kalahaṃsa</s>.
The <s>kākatuṇḍaka</s> is the white <s>kāraṇḍava</s>.
The <s>utkrośa</s> is known as <s>kurala</s>.
The <s>puṇḍarīkākṣa</s> is the <s>puṇḍara</s>.
The <s>megharāva</s> is the <s>meghanāda</s>.
Others say that the <s>megharāva</s> is the <s>cātaka</s>; that is not so, because the latter is not a water-going bird.
The <s>ambukukkuṭī</s> is the water-hen.
The <s>ārā</s> is known by its own name.
The <s>nandīmukhī</s> is the <s>patrāṭī</s>.
The <s>sārasa</s> is well known.
The <s>raktaśīrṣaka</s> is a variety of <s>sārasa</s>, with a red head.
The phrase "water-moving" means that they swim in water.
The <s>pṛṣata</s> is the spotted deer.

children.text: śarabhaḥ aṣṭāpada uṣṭrapramāṇo mahāśṛṅgaḥ pṛṣṭhagatacatuṣpādaḥ kāśmīre prasiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>śarabha</s> is an eight-footed animal, camel-sized, with great horns and four feet on its back, famous in Kashmir.
The <s>rāma</s> is a great wild animal in the Himalaya.
The <s>śvadaṃṣṭra</s> has four fangs and is famous in <s>Kārttikapura</s>.
The <s>mṛgamātṛkā</s> is a small, broad-bellied kind of deer.
The <s>kuraṅga</s> is a variety of deer.
The <s>gokarṇa</s> is a special cow-faced deer.
The <s>hariṇa</s> is tawny in color; the <s>eṇa</s> is the black antelope.
The <s>ṛṣya</s> is a blue-testicled deer.
The <s>cāruṣka</s> and the others too are simply varieties of deer.
But the hare is listed by <s>Suśruta</s> among the animals that live in holes; that is because the distinction is slight.
The <s>lāva</s> is well known.
The <s>vartīra</s> is a variety of <s>kapiñjala</s>.
The <s>kapiñjala</s> is the pale partridge.
The <s>vārtīka</s> is a variety of sparrow that moves in flocks.
The <s>upacakra</s> is a variety of <s>cakora</s>.

children.text: kukkubhaḥ prasiddhaḥ raktavartmaka iti kukkubhaviśeṣaṇaṃ tena sthūlakukkubho gṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: The <s>kukkubha</s> is well known. The qualifier "red-eyed" specifies the <s>kukkubha</s>, and by it the large <s>kukkubha</s> is meant.
The <s>vartaka</s> is known as <s>vaṭṭahī</s>.

children.text: vārtikā svalpapramāṇā jātyantarameva kecit tu vartakastriyaṃ vartikāṃ vadanti asyāśca grahaṇaṃ strīliṅgabhede'pi viśeṣalāghavapratiṣedhārtham anyathā strītvena vartikādvartikāyā lāghavaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: The <s>vārtikā</s> is small in size and is itself a separate species. Some, however, say that the female <s>vartaka</s> is the <s>vārtikā</s>. Its mention is meant to rule out a special lightness merely from the difference of feminine gender; otherwise, because it is female, the <s>vārtikā</s> would be lighter than the <s>vartaka</s>.
The <s>barhī</s> is the peacock.
The <s>śārapadendrābha</s> is the <s>mallakaṅka</s>.
The <s>gonarda</s> is known as <s>ghoḍākaṅka</s>.
The <s>krakara</s> is well known.
The making of two groups of scattering-feeding birds, one beginning with <s>lāva</s> and another beginning with <s>vartikā</s>, is for the sake of stating a difference in qualities.
The <s>śatapattra</s> is the wood-fowl.

children.text: bhṛṅgarājaḥ prasiddho bhramaravarṇaḥ koyaṣṭiḥ koḍā iti khyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> is well known, black like a bee; it is known as <s>koyaṣṭi</s> or <s>koḍā</s>.
The <s>jīvañjīvaka</s> dies at the sight of poison.

children.text: atyūhaḥ ḍāhukaḥ dātyūha iti vā pāṭhaḥ sa ca prasiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>atyūha</s> is the <s>ḍāhuka</s>; or the reading is <s>dātyūha</s>, and that bird is well known.
The <s>laṭṭā</s> is the <s>pheñcāka</s>, red on the lower part of the tail; the <s>laṭūṣaka</s> is also a variety of it.
The <s>ḍiṇḍimānaka</s> has a loud sound like a drum.

children.text: kuliṅga iti vanacaṭakākāraḥ pītamastakaḥ vāe iti loke ||
children.translated_text: The <s>kuliṅga</s> is shaped like a forest sparrow, with a yellow head, and is called <s>vāe</s> in common speech.
The <s>kalaviṅka</s> is the village sparrow.
But the <s>caṭaka</s> is the temple sparrow, small in size.
Those names that are not stated here and are not commonly known should be learned from experts on them and from people of other regions.
He states the defining characteristic by deriving the designation beginning with <s>prasaha</s>.
<s>Prasahya</s> means forcibly.

children.text: ānūpānūpasaṃśrayāditi pūrvatrāsiddhavidher anityatvenānūpā ityatra yalopasya siddhatvenaiva saṃhitā jñeyā ||
children.translated_text: In the expression <s>ānūpānūpasaṃśrayāt</s>, because a rule not established in the previous case is not invariable, the sandhi should be understood with the elision of <s>y</s> already established in <s>ānūpā</s>.

children.text: jalecaryāditi jalavāsinām eva haṃsādīnāṃ jale caraṇamātratvaṃ boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: In the phrase "moving in water," one should understand only that water-dwelling creatures such as <s>haṃsa</s>s move in water.

children.text: sthalajā ityukte gajādiṣvapi sthalajāteṣu prasaktiḥ syādityāha jāṅgalacāriṇa iti ||
children.translated_text: If one merely said "land-born," there would be overextension to elephants and other land-born creatures; therefore he says, "those moving in dry-country terrain."

children.text: vikīryetyatra bhakṣayanti iti śeṣaḥ evaṃ pratudyetyatrāpi pratudyeti bahudhābhihatya ||
children.translated_text: In "scattering," the remainder to be supplied is "they eat." Likewise in "pecking" too, <s>pratudya</s> means "having struck in many ways."

children.text: prasahā dvividhā māṃsādā vyāghraśyenādayaḥ tathā amāṃsādāśca gavādayaḥ tena māṃsādānāṃ viśeṣamāha prasahānām ityādi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prasaha</s> animals are of two kinds: flesh-eaters, such as tigers and hawks, and non-flesh-eaters, such as cows. Therefore he states the special feature of the flesh-eaters in the passage beginning "of the <s>prasaha</s>s."
By their chronic condition, he indicates the long persistence of piles and the other disorders.

children.text: pratudā ityatra tathā jāṅgalā ityatra cakāro luptanirdiṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the expressions <s>pratudāḥ</s> and likewise <s>jāṅgalāḥ</s>, the word <s>ca</s> is indicated though omitted.
The division is <s>kaphānuge</s>, "when <s>kapha</s> follows."
"Because of similarity to the bodily tissues" means because it is similar to human flesh.

children.text: etena śītagurusnigdhatvena yuktam apyājamāṃsaṃ śarīradhātusāmyāt kaphaṃ na karotītyuktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By this it is said that even goat meat, though possessing coldness, heaviness, and unctuousness, does not produce <s>kapha</s> because of its similarity to the bodily tissues.

children.text: āvikaṃ māṃsaṃ madhuraśītatvena pittaharamapi boddhavyam ata eva śaradvidhāv apyuktam urabhraśarabhān iti ||
children.translated_text: Mutton should also be understood as removing <s>pitta</s> because it is sweet and cold. For this very reason, even in the autumn regimen, sheep and <s>śarabha</s> are mentioned.

children.text: raktapittanidāne tu varāhamahiṣetyādinā dravyāntarasaṃyuktasyaivāvikamāṃsasya raktapittakartṛtvaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: But in the diagnosis of <s>raktapitta</s>, from the statement beginning "boar, buffalo," one should understand that mutton causes <s>raktapitta</s> only when combined with other substances.
In the phrase "in the <s>yoni</s> (class)," this refers to the eightfold class beginning with <s>prasaha</s>.

children.text: miśragocaratvāditi kadācidanūpasevanāt kadācid dhanvasevanāt kadācid ubhayasevanād ajāvyor aniścitayonitvam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Because their range is mixed" means: because they sometimes frequent marshy land, sometimes dry land, and sometimes both, goats and sheep have an uncertain <s>yoni</s> (class).

children.text: atra aniścite iti yoniviśeṣaṇaṃ kiṃvā ajā ca avī ca ete aniścite ||
children.translated_text: Here "uncertain" may qualify <s>yoni</s>; or else the goats and sheep themselves are uncertain.

children.text: nanu yadyevaṃ tadā tittirirapi dhanvānūpasevanānna viṣkiragaṇe paṭhanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If this is so, one may object, then the <s>tittiri</s> too, because it frequents both dry and marshy land, ought not to be listed in the class of scratching birds.

children.text: naivaṃ tittirijātiviśeṣasya dhanvānūpayor niyamena niṣevaṇād guṇaniyamaḥ pāryate kartum avyajayostu niyamo'yaṃ nāsti yataḥ kecidajāvī dhanvamātracare keciccānūpamātracare keciccobhayamātracare tena tayor niyamacarakṛto yonibhedaḥ kartuṃ na pāryate ||
children.translated_text: Not so. Since the particular species called <s>tittiri</s> regularly frequents both dry and marshy land, a fixed rule about its qualities can be made. But this rule does not apply to goats and sheep, because some goats and sheep range only in dry land, some only in marshy land, and some only in both; therefore a distinction of <s>yoni</s> based on their fixed range cannot be made for them.
"Of some" refers to peacocks and the others that will be mentioned.
"Because of superiority in qualities" means because they possess distinctive qualities.

children.text: mayūrasya gurutvasnigdhatvaṃ vartakādigaṇapaṭhitatvenaiva labdhaṃ sat punarucyate viśeṣārtham ||
children.translated_text: The heaviness and unctuousness of peacock, although already obtained from its being listed in the group beginning with <s>vartaka</s>, is stated again for the sake of a special point.

children.text: evamanyatrāpi gaṇoktaguṇakathanena labdhasya punaḥ kathane vyākhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: The same explanation should be applied elsewhere too when what has already been obtained from the statement of group qualities is stated again.
The "weapon-footed" bird is the cock.

children.text: dhanvānūpaniṣevaṇāditi hetukathanena ya eva dhanvānūpaniṣevī tittiriḥ sa eva yathoktaguṇa iti jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Since the reason is stated as "because of frequenting dry and marshy land," it should be understood that only that <s>tittiri</s> which frequents dry and marshy land has the qualities described.

children.text: evamanye 'pi ye gavādayo dhanvānūpaniṣeviṇas te 'pi tittirisamānaguṇā bhavanti tittiristu viśeṣeṇeti tittiriḥ sākṣāduktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, other animals such as cattle that frequent dry and marshy land also have qualities like those of the <s>tittiri</s>; but the <s>tittiri</s> is mentioned directly because it is especially so.

children.text: kiṃvā tittirereva evaṃguṇatve dhanvānūpaniṣevaṇaṃ hetuḥ nānyatra gavāder anūpadeśāder iti jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Or rather, it should be understood that frequenting dry and marshy land is the cause only of the <s>tittiri</s>'s having such qualities, not of other animals such as cattle, because there is no instruction regarding them.
<s>Kapota</s>s are household-dwelling pigeons, that is, <s>pārāvata</s>s.

children.text: caṭakā madhurā ityādi kecit paṭhantyeva ye tu na paṭhanti teṣāṃ mate caṭakasya pratudasāmānyaguṇalabdhaṃ vṛṣyatvaṃ tṛptiṃ caṭakamāṃsānāṃ gatvā yo 'nupibet payaḥ ityādivṛṣyaprayogādeva labhyate ||
children.translated_text: Some indeed read, "<s>Caṭaka</s>s are sweet," and so on. But in the view of those who do not read it, the aphrodisiac property and satisfaction of <s>caṭaka</s> are obtained from the common qualities of the pecking-bird class, and also from aphrodisiac applications such as, "one who has eaten sparrow meat and then drinks milk."

children.text: mayūrādīnāṃ tu bahavo guṇā gaṇoktaguṇādhikā iti pṛthak pāṭhaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But peacocks and the others have many qualities in addition to the qualities stated for the group, and so a separate recitation was made.

children.text: māṃsaṃ bṛṃhaṇānām ityanenaivāgryādhikāravacanena māṃsasya bṛṃhaṇatve labdhe śarīrabṛṃhaṇe nānya ityādivacanaṃ prakaraṇaprāptatvena tathā tasyaivārthasya dārḍhyārthaṃ ca jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Since the bulk-promoting property of meat has already been obtained by the authoritative statement, "meat is foremost among bulk-promoters," the statement "there is no other for building up the body" and the like should be understood as being required by the topic and as strengthening that same meaning.
Vegetables too are taught immediately afterwards because they serve as relishes.
<s>Śuṣā</s> is <s>kāsamarda</s>.
<s>Śaṭī</s> is well known by its own name.
<s>Vāstuka</s> is <s>ṭaṅkavāstuka</s>.

children.text: nātyuṣṇaśītavīryeti noṣṇatvaṃ prakarṣaprāptamasyā nāpi śītatvam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Not of excessively hot or cold potency" means that neither hotness nor coldness is present in it to an intense degree.

children.text: yattu suśrute tiktā kākamācī vātaṃ śamayati uṣṇavīryatvāt ityuktaṃ tadvīryavādimatena ata eva dravyaguṇe suśrute'pi nātyuṣṇaśītā ityevameva paṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: As for what is said in <s>Suśruta</s>, "bitter <s>kākamācī</s> pacifies <s>vāta</s> because it has hot potency," that follows the opinion of those who teach potency in that way. For this very reason, even in <s>Suśruta</s>'s section on the qualities of substances it is read simply as "not excessively hot or cold."
<s>Rājakṣavaka</s> is <s>dugdhikā</s>.

children.text: kālaśākaṃ kāliyā iti khyātaṃ kālākhyam iti kālaśākam evocyate punaḥ anye tu kālāyam iti paṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kālaśāka</s>, known as <s>kāliyā</s>, is just what is called "named <s>kāla</s>," namely <s>kālaśāka</s>. But others read <s>kālāya</s>.
<s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s> is known as <s>maṇimaṇī</s>.
<s>Kucelā</s> is a variety of <s>akarṇaviddhikā</s>.
<s>Vanatiktaka</s> is <s>pathyasundara</s>.
<s>Avalguja</s> is <s>vālgujī</s>.
<s>Śakulādanī</s> is <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>.
<s>Śārṅgeṣṭā</s> is <s>kākatiktā</s>.
<s>Kaṭhillaka</s> is <s>punarnavā</s>.
<s>Nāḍī</s> is <s>nāḍīca</s>.
<s>Kalāya</s> is the round <s>kalāya</s>.
<s>Tilaparṇikā</s> is <s>hulahulikā</s>.
<s>Gojihvā</s> is <s>dārvipattrikā</s>.

children.text: kulakaḥ kāravellakaḥ kecit tu kulakaṃ paṭolabhedam āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kulaka</s> is <s>kāravellaka</s>; but some say that <s>kulaka</s> is a variety of <s>paṭola</s>.
<s>Karkaśa</s> is a small <s>karkoṭaka</s>.
<s>Sūpyaśāka</s>s are <s>māṣaparṇī</s> and the like.
<s>Phañjī</s> is <s>brāhmaṇayaṣṭikā</s>.
<s>Cillī</s> is <s>gauḍavāstuka</s>.
<s>Kutumbaka</s> is <s>droṇapuṣpikā</s>.
<s>Āluka</s>s are <s>piṇḍāluka</s> and the like.
<s>Karbudāra</s> is <s>kāñcana</s>.
<s>Suvarcalā</s> is <s>sūryabhaktikā</s>; some say it is <s>phappuka</s>.
<s>Pattūra</s> is <s>śāliñca</s>.
<s>Cuccuparṇikā</s> is a variety of <s>nāḍīca</s>.
<s>Kumārajīva</s> is <s>jīvaśāka</s>.
<s>Loṭṭāka</s> is <s>loṭṭāmāriṣa</s>.
<s>Nālikā</s> is <s>gonāḍīca</s>.
<s>Āsurī</s> is <s>rājikā</s>, or <s>maṇḍaka</s>.
<s>Vṛkadhūmaka</s> is <s>bhūmiśirīṣa</s>.
<s>Lakṣmaṇā</s> is known by its own name.
<s>Nalinī</s> is lotus fiber. If the reading is <s>nīlinī</s>, it is <s>buhnā</s>.
<s>Yavaśāka</s> is <s>kṣetravāstuka</s>.
<s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> is <s>sarpacchattra</s>.
<s>Avalguja</s> means a variety of <s>avalguja</s>.
<s>Yātuka</s> is white <s>śālaparṇī</s>.
<s>Śālakalyāṇī</s> is a variety of <s>śāliñca</s>.
<s>Triparṇī</s> is <s>haṃsapādikā</s>.
<s>Pīluparṇī</s> is <s>moraṭaka</s>.
<s>Gaṇḍīra</s> is <s>śamaṭha</s>.
<s>Bilvaparṇī</s> is <s>bilvārjaka</s>.
<s>Bhaṇḍī</s> is known by its own name.
<s>Parvaṇī</s> is <s>parvaśāka</s>.
<s>Parvapuṣpī</s> is <s>kukkuṭī</s>.
<s>Pañcāṅgula</s> is variegated <s>eraṇḍa</s>.
<s>Ervāruka</s> is <s>rājakarkaṭī</s>.

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍakaṃ suśrute bālyādyāvasthābhedena paṭhitaṃ tad apyaviruddham eva yato bālamadhyayos tatra pittaharatvaṃ kaphakaratvaṃ coktaṃ tadapīha pittottare kaphottare saṃnipāte boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kūṣmāṇḍaka</s> is read in <s>Suśruta</s> according to the difference between its tender and other states. That too is not contradictory, because there the removal of <s>pitta</s> and production of <s>kapha</s> are stated for the tender and middle states; here too that should be understood with reference to a combined disorder in which <s>pitta</s> predominates and one in which <s>kapha</s> predominates.

children.text: kelūṭe hārītavacanaṃ kelūṭaṃ svādu viṭapaṃ tatkandaḥ svāduśītalaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Regarding <s>kelūṭa</s>, there is <s>Hārīta</s>'s statement: "<s>kelūṭa</s> is sweet and branch-like; its tuber is sweet and cooling."

children.text: kadambaṃ kadambikāṃ vadanti kecit tu svalpakadambakam āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kadamba</s> is called <s>kadambikā</s>; some, however, call it <s>svalpakadambaka</s>.
<s>Nadīmāṣaka</s> is known as <s>udīmānaka</s>.
<s>Ainduka</s> is <s>nikṣāra</s>.
<s>Tālapralamba</s> is a sprout of the palm.
By the word <s>śasya</s> here, marrow from the head is meant.
<s>Taruṭa</s> is the tuber of <s>kahlāra</s>.
<s>Krauñcādana</s> is <s>dhiñculikā</s>.
By the word <s>kaśeruka</s>, both <s>ciñcoḍakā</s> and <s>rājakaśeruka</s> are meant.
<s>Aṅkāloḍya</s> is a small lotus tuber.
<s>Muñjātaka</s> is a tuber from the northern region.
<s>Amlikā</s>, with small branches, generally occurs in <s>Kāmarūpa</s> and similar regions.
<s>Sarpacchattra</s> is a mushroom shaped like a snake's hood.
Other mushroom varieties, produced from dung, straw, and the like, should be understood to be numerous.

children.text: pattrakandaphalāśraya iti prādhānyena tena puṣpādyāśrayatvam api śākavargasya jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: The phrase 'based on leaves, bulbs, and fruits' is primary; by it one should also understand that the class of greens may be based on flowers and so forth.
Because some fruits too are used like greens, he states the class of fruits.
<s>Mṛdvīkā</s> is mentioned first because its qualities are superior.
<s>Phalgu</s> is the fruit of the <s>udumbara</s> fig.

children.text: madhūkaśabdena samānaguṇatvāt phalaṃ kusumaṃ ca jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: By the word <s>madhūka</s>, because they have the same qualities, both the fruit and the flower should be understood.
And here <s>parūṣaka</s> should be understood as sweet <s>parūṣaka</s>.

children.text: āmrātam āmaḍā iti khyātamāmraphalasadṛśam iti candrikā etacca dvividhaṃ madhuramamlaṃ ca atra madhurasyaiva guṇaḥ amlasya vakṣyamāṇatvāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āmrāta</s> is known as <s>āmaḍā</s>, resembling the mango fruit, according to the <s>Candrikā</s>. This too is of two kinds, sweet and sour; here only the qualities of the sweet one are meant, since the sour one will be stated later.

children.text: tālaśasyānīti tālaphalāni yathā harītakīnāṃ śasyāni ityatra phalameva śasyam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Tālaśasya</s>' means palm fruits, just as in the expression 'the <s>śasya</s>s of <s>harītakī</s>' the fruit itself is called <s>śasya</s>.
'<s>Siddha</s>' means ripe; therefore the ripe palm fruit is intended.
<s>Bhavya</s> is the fruit of <s>karmaraṅga</s>; some say it is a fruit merely enclosed in its rind.
<s>Āruka</s> is well known in <s>Kārttikeyapura</s>.

children.text: karkandhūḥ śṛgālabadarī karkandhūnikucayor vicchidya pāṭhena nityaṃ pittaśleṣmakartṛtvaṃ tayor darśayati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Karkandhū</s> is <s>śṛgālabadarī</s>. By reading <s>karkandhū</s> and <s>nikuca</s> separately, he shows that both of them always produce <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>.

children.text: parūṣakādīnāṃ tu madhurāmlabhedena dvirūpāṇāṃ ya eva parūṣakādayo 'mlāsta eva pittaśleṣmakarā iti ||
children.translated_text: But among <s>parūṣaka</s> and the others, which have two forms according to the distinction between sweet and sour, only those <s>parūṣaka</s>s and the rest that are sour produce <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>.
<s>Pārāvata</s> is well known in <s>Kāmarūpa</s>.

children.text: atra yo madhuraḥ sa śītaḥ yaścāmlaḥ sa uṣṇa iti jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Here, the one that is sweet should be understood as cold, and the one that is sour as hot.

children.text: evaṃ rasanirdeśenaiva vīrye labdhe'pi punarvīryākhyānamamlasyāmalakasya śītatādarśanād boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, even though potency is already obtained from the indication of taste, the repeated statement of potency should be understood because the sour <s>āmalaka</s> is observed to be cold.
<s>Ṭaṅka</s> is well known in <s>Kāśmīra</s>.
'<s>Siddha</s>' means ripened through time.
The statement of the qualities of <s>kapittha</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and mango according to their different stages is because they are useful in all stages.
<s>Badara</s> is of medium size, for that is indeed only sweet.
<s>Gāṅgeruka</s> is the fruit of <s>nāgabalā</s>.
<s>Karīra</s> is a tree of the desert region.
<s>Todana</s> is a variety of <s>dhanvana</s>.
<s>Rājādana</s> is <s>kṣīrī</s>.

children.text: avadaṃśakṣamamiti lavalīphalaṃ prāśya dravyāntare rucir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: 'Fit as a relish' means that after one eats the fruit of <s>lavalī</s>, desire for another substance arises.
<s>Nīpa</s> is <s>kadambaka</s>.
The fruit of <s>śatāhvaka</s> is known as <s>seha</s>.
<s>Pīlu</s> belongs to the northern region.
<s>Tṛṇaśūnya</s> is the fruit of <s>ketakī</s>.
<s>Prācīnāmalaka</s> is <s>pānīyāmalaka</s>.
<s>Tinduka</s> is <s>kendu</s>.

children.text: dāḍimaguṇe kaphapittāvirodhīti amladāḍimaṃ pittāvirodhi madhuraṃ tu kaphāvirodhi evaṃ ca tridoṣaharatvamasyopapannaṃ yad uktaṃ suśrute dvividhaṃ tattu vijñeyaṃ madhuraṃ cāmlameva ca ||
children.translated_text: In the qualities of <s>dāḍima</s>, 'not opposed to <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>' means that sour <s>dāḍima</s> is not opposed to <s>pitta</s>, while the sweet one is not opposed to <s>kapha</s>. Thus its property of removing all three <s>doṣa</s>s is established, as has been said in <s>Suśruta</s>: 'That should be known as twofold, sweet and also sour.'
The sweet one destroys all three <s>doṣa</s>s, while the sour one removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
<s>Vṛkṣāmla</s> is <s>mahārdraka</s>.
<s>Amlikā</s> is <s>tintiḍī</s>.

children.text: śeṣamiti tvaṅmāṃsam ato'nyatheti guru kiṃvā śūle 'rucāv ityādyuktakesaraguṇaviparītam ||
children.translated_text: 'The remainder' means the bark and flesh; 'otherwise' means heavy, or else opposite to the qualities of the filaments stated in the passage beginning 'in colic and anorexia.'
<s>Vātāma</s> and the others belong to the northern region.
This <s>priyāla</s> is well known in <s>Magadha</s>.
<s>Dantaśaṭha</s> is <s>jambīra</s>; some call it <s>amloṭa</s>.

children.text: ihāmrātakamamlaṃ grāhyaṃ pūrvaṃ tu madhuramāmrātakam uktam ||
children.translated_text: Here sour <s>āmrātaka</s> is to be understood, whereas sweet <s>āmrātaka</s> was stated before.
<s>Karamarda</s> is twofold: village-grown and forest-grown.
<s>Airāvata</s> is <s>amlātaka</s>, or else <s>nāgaraṅga</s>.

children.text: vārtākaṃ dakṣiṇāpathe phalavat khādyate yad goṣṭhavārtākasaṃjñakaṃ tasyeha guṇaḥ kiṃvā phalavadasiddhasyaiva vārtākasyopayojyasyāyaṃ guṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vārtāka</s>, which is called <s>goṣṭhavārtāka</s> and is eaten like a fruit in the southern region, has its quality stated here. Or this is the quality of usable <s>vārtāka</s> itself, when it is uncooked like a fruit.
<s>Ākṣikī</s> is a creeper; its fruit is <s>ākṣika</s>.
<s>Anupākī</s> is known as <s>anuyā</s>.
'Like fire' means because it produces blisters and the like.

children.text: haritānām apyārdrakādīnāṃ phalavadagnipākam antareṇa bhojanasya prāk paścāccopayogāt phalam anu haritakathanaṃ phalebhyastu paścādabhidhānaṃ haritasya tṛptyanādhāyakatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Even green substances such as fresh ginger are used, like fruits, before and after a meal without cooking by fire; therefore the discussion of greens follows fruits. But greens are mentioned after fruits because they do not bring about satiety.
The qualification 'fresh ginger' is for the sake of excluding dry ginger; the quality of dry ginger will occur in the class of substances combined with food.
<s>Jambīra</s> is a variety of <s>parṇāsa</s>; the <s>jambīra</s> fruit is fragrant.
'When young, it removes the <s>doṣa</s>s' means that in the tender stage, when its taste is still indistinct, it removes all three <s>doṣa</s>s.

children.text: tantrāntaravacanaṃ hi yāvaddhi cāvyaktarasānvitāni navaprarūḍhāni ca mūlakāni bhavanti tāvallaghudīpanāni pittānilaśleṣmaharāṇi caiva ||
children.translated_text: For there is a statement from another treatise: 'As long as radishes have an unmanifest taste and are newly sprouted, so long they are light, kindling digestion, and remove <s>pitta</s>, <s>anila</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s>.'

children.text: vṛddhaṃ tridoṣamiti tadevapravṛddham enāmeva mūlakāvasthām abhipretya coktaṃ mūlakaṃ kandānāmapathyatve prakṛṣṭatamam iti mārutāpahaṃ snigdhasiddhamiti sāmānyena bālaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: "The grown one is tridoṣic" means that very same <s>mūlaka</s> (radish) when fully developed. And it is with reference to this very root-state of <s>mūlaka</s> that it has been said, "Among roots, <s>mūlaka</s> is the foremost in unwholesomeness." "Removing <s>māruta</s> when cooked with fat" is stated generally, for both the young and the grown.

children.text: śuṣkāṇi kaphavātaghnānyetāni iti vakṣyamāṇagranthenaiva śuṣkakasya kaphavātahantṛtve labdhe punarvacanaṃ prakarṣaprāptyartham ||
children.translated_text: Since the forthcoming passage itself, "These, when dry, destroy <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>," establishes that dried <s>kaska</s> destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, the repetition is for the sake of conveying special intensity.

children.text: pūtigandhaheti śarīrasya tathā vyañjanārthaṃ māṃsasya ca pūtigandhatāṃ hanti ||
children.translated_text: "Removing putrid odor" means that it removes putrid odor from the body and likewise from meat when it is used for seasoning.
<s>Arjaka</s> is <s>śvetaparṇāsa</s>.

children.text: śigruḥ viṭapaśobhāñjanaḥ śāleyaś cāṇakyamūlaṃ marau prasiddhaṃ kiṃvā śāleyam iti misteyaṃ pāṭakaprasiddhaṃ vacanaṃ hi cāṇakyamūlamisteye śāleyābhikhyayā jaguḥ iti mṛṣṭakaṃ rājikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śigru</s> is <s>viṭapa</s>, <s>śobhāñjana</s>, and <s>śāleya</s>; <s>cāṇakyamūla</s> is well known in <s>Maru</s>. Or else <s>śāleya</s> is <s>misteya</s>, according to the reading known in recitation; for the statement says, "They have called <s>cāṇakyamūla</s> and <s>misteya</s> by the name <s>śāleya</s>." <s>Mṛṣṭaka</s> is <s>rājikā</s>.

children.text: gaṇḍīro dvividho raktaḥ śuklaśca tatra yo raktaḥ sa hi kaṭutvena haritavarge paṭhyate yastu śuklo jalajaḥ sa śākavarge paṭhita iti naikasya vargadvaye pāṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṇḍīra</s> is of two kinds, red and white. Of these, the red one, because it is pungent, is listed in the group of greens; but the white one, which is aquatic, is listed in the group of vegetables. Thus it is not the case that one and the same thing is taught in two groups.
<s>Jalapippalī</s> grows in water in the shape of <s>pippalī</s>.

children.text: śṛṅgaverī gojihvikā kiṃvā ārdrakākṛtiḥ śṛṅgaverī yaduktaṃ śṛṅgaveravad ākṛtyā śṛṅgaverīti bhāṣitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgaverī</s> is <s>gojihvikā</s>, or else <s>śṛṅgaverī</s> has the form of fresh ginger. As it has been said, "Because of its shape, like <s>śṛṅgavera</s>, it is called <s>śṛṅgaverī</s>."
"And they call <s>tumburu</s>s those that have the same shape as <s>kustumburu</s>."
<s>Bhūstṛṇa</s> is <s>gandhatṛṇa</s>.
<s>Kharāhvā</s> is black cumin.
<s>Ajagandhā</s> is wild <s>yavānī</s>.
<s>Sumukha</s> is a variety of <s>parṇāsa</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ ca dhānyakādīnām ārdrāṇāṃ guṇaḥ śuṣkāṇāṃ tv āhārayogigaṇe kāravī kuñcikā ityādinā guṇaṃ nirdekṣyati ||
children.translated_text: And this is the property of fresh <s>dhānyaka</s> and the others; but he will indicate the property of them when dried in the group of foods used in combination, with the passage beginning "<s>kāravī</s>, <s>kuñcikā</s>," and so on.
<s>Gṛñjanaka</s> is simply a <s>palāṇḍu</s> with a small stalk and leaf.
"These" means those stated in the group of greens.

children.text: śuṣkāṇītyādinā yadyapi śuṣkāṇām api śuṇṭhīprabhṛtīnāṃ guṇa ukto bhavati tathāpi viśeṣaguṇāntarakathanārthaṃ punastadabhidhānam āhārasaṃyogivarge bhaviṣyatīti na paunaruktyam ||
children.translated_text: Although the words beginning "when dry" already state the property of dried substances such as <s>śuṇṭhī</s>, nevertheless, because a further particular property is to be stated, the repeated mention of them in the class of substances combined with food will occur; hence there is no repetition.

children.text: pūrvādhyāye annaṃ prāṇāḥ ityuktaṃ tadyena prakāreṇānnaṃ prāṇahetur bhavati tadabhidhānārthaṃ vividhāśitapītīyo 'bhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: In the preceding chapter it was said, "Food is life." In order to explain the manner in which food becomes the cause of life, the chapter <s>Vividhāśitapītīya</s> is now stated.
This designation too is based on its meaning.
"Various," and so on.

children.text: vividhamiti anenāśitādīnāmavāntarabhedaṃ darśayati aśitādiṣu yo yaḥ prāya upayujyate sa pūrvam uktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the word "various" he shows the internal subdivisions of things eaten and the rest. Among things eaten and the like, whatever is chiefly used has been stated first.

children.text: jantor hitam iti vacanam ahitasyāśitāder balavarṇādikartṛtvābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: The statement "beneficial to the living creature" is made because things eaten and the like that are harmful do not produce strength, complexion, and so on.

children.text: antaragninā jāṭhareṇa vahninā saṃdhukṣitaṃ balaṃ yasya tenāntaragnisaṃdhukṣitabalena ||
children.translated_text: "One whose strength is kindled by the inner fire" means one whose strength has been kindled by the internal fire, the gastric fire.

children.text: yathāsvenoṣmaṇeti pṛthivyādirūpāśitādeyasya ya ūṣmā pārthivāgnyādirūpastena vacanaṃ hi bhaumāpyāgneyavāyavyāḥ pañcoṣmāṇaḥ sanābhasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "By its own heat" means by that heat of what is to be eaten and the rest, which is composed of earth and the other elements and has the form of earth, fire, and so on. For the statement says, "The five heats, terrestrial, watery, fiery, airy, together with the ethereal,

children.text: pañcāhāraguṇān svān svān pārthivādīn pacanti hi iti ||
children.translated_text: digest their own five qualities of food, the terrestrial and the others."
"Being properly digested" refers to the eaten substance and the rest.

children.text: kiṃvā yathāsvenoṣmaṇeti yasya rudhirāder ya ūṣmā dhātvagnirūpastena samyagvipacyamānamaśitādi rasatām āpannaṃ yadā raktādidhātūn pratipadyate tadā raktādyūṣmaṇaiva pacyate evaṃ vipacyamānamaśitādi śarīramupacayādinā yojayatyūrjayati vardhayatīti yojanā ||
children.translated_text: Or else, "by its own heat" means by whatever heat belongs to blood and the other tissues, in the form of the tissue-fire. When the eaten substance and the rest, properly digested and having become <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid), reach the tissues such as blood, then they are digested precisely by the heat of blood and the other tissues. The construction is: the eaten substance and the rest, while being digested in this way, joins the body with increase and the like, invigorates it, and makes it grow.
He states what kind of body it is: "like time," and so on.

children.text: yathā kālo nityagatvenānavasthitaḥ tathānavasthitaḥ aviśrāntaḥ sarvadhātūnāṃ pāko yasmin śarīre tattathā etena sarvadā svāgnipākakṣīyamāṇadhātoḥ śarīrasyāśitādinopacayādiyojanam upapannamiti darśayati yadi hi pākakṣīyamāṇaṃ śarīraṃ na syāttadā svataḥ siddhe upacayādau kimaśitādi kuryād iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as time, because it is always moving, does not remain in one state, so too that body is unceasing and without rest, because the digestion of all its tissues does not remain fixed. By this he shows that it is reasonable for the body, whose tissues are constantly being depleted by digestion through their own fires, to be joined by food and the like with increase and so forth. For if the body were not being depleted by digestion, what would food and the like do with respect to increase and the rest, since those would already be accomplished by themselves? This is the intention.

children.text: kiṃvā kālavadityaśitādiviśeṣaṇaṃ tena yathoktakālakṛtam aśitādītyarthaḥ akālabhojanasyopacayādyakārakatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Or else "like time" is a qualifier of food and the like; thus it means food and the like taken at the prescribed time, since eating at an improper time does not produce increase and the rest.

children.text: tathā anavasthitasarvadhātupākamityetadapi aśitādiviśeṣaṇaṃ tena anavasthitaḥ sarvadhātuṣu pāko yasyāśitādestattathā etena kvacidapi dhātau sthagitasyāśitāde rasarūpasya pākavigamanān nopacayādir bhavatīti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, "in which the digestion of all tissues is unsettled" is also a qualifier of food and the like. Thus it means food and the like in which digestion is not fixed in all the tissues. By this he shows that increase and the rest do not occur when the <s>rasa</s>-form of food and the like is stopped in any tissue and digestion ceases.

children.text: etacca vyākhyānaṃ nātisundaram asyārthasya anupahatetyādiśarīraviśeṣaṇenaiva labdhatvāt punaḥ śarīraviśeṣaṇam anupapannam ||
children.translated_text: And this explanation is not very good, because that meaning is already obtained from the qualifier of the body, "unimpaired," and so on; a further qualifier of the body is therefore inappropriate.

children.text: anupahatetyādi anupahatāni sarvadhātūnām ūṣmamārutasrotāṃsi yasya tattathā yadā hi eko 'pi dhātupācako'gnirupahataḥ māruto vā dhātupoṣakarasavāhī vyānarūpaḥ kvacid upahato bhavati tathā sroto vā dhātupoṣakarasavaham upahataṃ syāt tadā aśitādikaṃ dhātūnām avardhakatvānnopacayādikārakam iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Unimpaired," and so on means: that body in which the heat, <s>māruta</s>, and channels of all the tissues are unimpaired. For when even one fire that digests a tissue is impaired, or when <s>māruta</s>, in the form of <s>vyāna</s> that carries the nutrient fluid of the tissues, is impaired somewhere, or when a channel that carries the nutrient fluid of the tissues is impaired, then food and the like, because it does not increase the tissues, does not produce increase and the other effects. This is the sense.

children.text: kevalamiti kṛtsnaṃ śarīraṃ kiṃvā kevalamiti adharmarahitam adharmayukte hi śarīre viphalamaśitādi bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: "Entirely" means the whole body. Or else "entirely" means free from <s>adharma</s> (wrongdoing), for in a body joined with <s>adharma</s>, food and the like becomes fruitless.

children.text: nanu śarīradhātūnāṃ prakṛtisthitānāṃ svata evopacayādyasti tat kimaśitādinā kriyata ityāha dhātavo hītyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, one might object: since there is growth and so forth by itself in the bodily tissues when they remain in their natural condition, what is accomplished by food, drink, and the like? To answer this he says, "For the tissues," and so on.

children.text: dhāturāhāro yeṣāṃ te dhātvāhārāḥ dhātavo rasādayo nityaṃ kṣīyamāṇā aśitādijanitadhātvāhārā eva santaḥ paraṃ svāsthyamanuvartante nānyathetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those for whom the tissues are food are called "having tissue-food." The meaning is that the tissues, beginning with <s>rasa</s>, which are constantly being depleted, maintain the highest health only when they have as their food the tissue-nutriment produced from what is eaten and so forth, and not otherwise.
He states what that food of the tissues is with the passage beginning "there."
"There" means in what is eaten and so forth.
The syntactic connection is: <s>rasa</s> and <s>kiṭṭa</s> are produced.

children.text: āhāraprasāda ityākhyā yasya sa tathā prasādaḥ sāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is so called because the name "clarified essence of food" belongs to it; <s>prasāda</s> means the essence.
<s>Kiṭṭa</s> is the non-essential portion.

children.text: kiṭṭād iti kiṭṭāṃśāt tena annādyaḥ kiṭṭāṃśas tato mūtrapurīṣe bhavato vāyuśca rasāt pacyamānānmalaḥ kaphaḥ evamādi grahaṇyadhyāye vakṣyamāṇam anusartavyaṃ vakṣyati hi
children.translated_text: "From the <s>kiṭṭa</s>" means from the portion that is <s>kiṭṭa</s>. Thus the first portion of food is a waste portion; from it urine and feces arise, and wind too. From <s>rasa</s> while it is being cooked, the waste is <s>kapha</s>. One should follow what will be stated in the chapter on <s>grahaṇī</s>, and indeed he will say:
"The <s>kiṭṭa</s> of food is feces and urine; that of <s>rasa</s> is <s>kapha</s>, and that of blood

children.text: pittaṃ māṃsasya svamalo malaḥ svedastu medasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is <s>pitta</s>; the proper waste of flesh is waste, and sweat is the waste of fat.

children.text: syāt kiṭṭaṃ keśalomāsthno majjñaḥ sneho'kṣiviṭ tvacām
children.translated_text: The <s>kiṭṭa</s> of hair, body-hair, and bone is said to be so; from marrow come unctuousness of the eyes, feces, and skin."
Thus.
By the word "and so on," substances such as the unctuousness of the eyes are to be included.

children.text: yadyapi ca vāto'naśanād apyupalabhyate tathāpi rūkṣakiṭṭādibhojanamalāṃśād apyutpadyata eveti kiṭṭādvātotpattiryuktaiva na cāyaṃ niyamo yanmalādevotpadyata iti vyāyāmādavagāhāderapi ca vātādisadbhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: And although <s>vāta</s> is observed even from fasting, still it certainly also arises from the waste portion of eating dry <s>kiṭṭa</s> and the like. Therefore the origination of <s>vāta</s> from <s>kiṭṭa</s> is quite reasonable. Nor is there any rule that it arises only from waste, since <s>vāta</s> and the others also occur from exercise, bathing, and the like.
"Reproductive organ" means the sexual organ.
He states what is nourished by <s>rasa</s> with the passage beginning "but they are nourished."
"The substances of the five senses" means earth and the other elements, which are the causes of the sense faculties beginning with smell.
"Called the clarified essence of the tissues" shows that the sense faculties are produced from tissue-essence only when it is extremely pure.
Because it binds the body, it is called the "binding of the body," by sinews, vessels, and the like.
By the word "and so on," menstrual blood, breast milk, and the like are included.

children.text: atrāhārarasād raktādipoṣaṇe kecid bruvate yat raso raktarūpatayā pariṇamati raktaṃ ca māṃsarūpatayā evaṃ māṃsādayo 'pyuttarottaradhāturūpatayā pariṇamanti ||
children.translated_text: Here, regarding the nourishment of blood and the subsequent tissues from food-<s>rasa</s>, some say that <s>rasa</s> transforms into the form of blood, and blood into the form of flesh; in this way flesh and the others too transform successively into the form of the next tissue.

children.text: atrāpi ca pakṣe kecid bruvate kṣīrād yathā sarvātmanā dadhi bhavati tathā kṛtsno raso raktaṃ bhavati evaṃ raktādayo'pi māṃsādirūpā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Even within this view some say: just as curds arise from milk in its entirety, so the whole of <s>rasa</s> becomes blood; and in this same way blood and the others become flesh and the subsequent tissues.

children.text: anye tv āhuḥ kedārīkulyānyāyena rasasya dhātupoṣaṇaṃ tatrānnādutpanno raso dhāturūpaṃ rasamadhigamya kiyatāpyaṃśena taṃ rasaṃ vardhayati aparaśca rasarāśistatra gataḥ san śoṇitagandhavarṇayuktatvācchoṇitam iva bhūtvā kiyatāpi śoṇitasamānenāṃśena dhāturūpaṃ śoṇitaṃ puṣṇāti śeṣaśca bhāgo māṃsaṃ yāti tatrāpi śoṇitavadvyavasthā tathā medaḥprabhṛtiṣvapīti ||
children.translated_text: Others, however, say that the nourishment of the tissues by <s>rasa</s> occurs according to the principle of irrigation channels to fields. In that model, the <s>rasa</s> produced from food reaches the <s>rasa</s> that has the form of a bodily tissue and increases that <s>rasa</s> by some portion. Another mass of <s>rasa</s>, having gone there, becomes as it were blood because it possesses the smell and color of blood, and by some portion similar to blood it nourishes the blood that has the form of a bodily tissue. The remaining portion goes to flesh, and there too the arrangement is as in the case of blood; likewise in fat and the following tissues.

children.text: ata eva ca mukhyārtho 'yaṃ grantho bhavati yathā
children.translated_text: For this very reason this text has the primary meaning, as follows:

children.text: rasād raktaṃ tato māṃsaṃ māṃsānmedastato'sthi ca
children.translated_text: "From <s>rasa</s> comes blood, from that flesh; from flesh comes fat, and from that bone;

children.text: asthno majjā tataḥ śukraṃ śukrādgarbhaḥ prasādajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: from bone comes marrow, then semen; from semen comes the embryo, born of the clarified essence."

children.text: iti tathā hārīte'pyuktaṃ rasaḥ saptāhādarvāk parivartamānaḥ śvetakapotaharitahāridrapadmakiṃśukālaktakarasaprakhyaś cāyaṃ yathākramaṃ divasaparivartād varṇaparivartam āpadyamānaḥ pittoṣmoparāgācchoṇitatvam āpadyate iti tathā suśrute 'pyuktaṃ sa khalvāpyo rasa ekaikasmin dhātau trīṇi trīṇi kalāsahasrāṇi pañcadaśa ca kalā avatiṣṭhate evaṃ māsena rasaḥ śukrībhavati iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus. Likewise it is said also in <s>Hārīta</s>: <s>rasa</s>, transforming before seven days have passed, is successively like a white pigeon, green, turmeric-yellow, lotus-colored, <s>kiṃśuka</s>-colored, and lac-colored fluid; as it undergoes a change of color through the transformation of the days, it becomes blood because it is tinged by the heat of <s>pitta</s>. Likewise it is said also in <s>Suśruta</s>: that watery <s>rasa</s> remains in each bodily tissue for three thousand and fifteen <s>kalās</s>; thus in a month <s>rasa</s> becomes semen.

children.text: anye tv āhuḥ khalekapotanyāyenāyam annarasaḥ pṛthak pṛthag dhātumārge gataḥ san rasādīn poṣayati na tv asya dhātupoṣako rasabhāgo dhātvantareṇa samaṃ sambandham apyanubhavati rasādipoṣakāni srotāṃsyuttarottaraṃ sūkṣmamukhāni dīrghāṇi ca tenaiva rasapoṣakarasabhāgo rasamārgacāritvād rasaṃ poṣayati evaṃ rasapoṣaṇakālād uttarakālaṃ raktapoṣako rasabhāgo raktaṃ poṣayati tathā śoṇitapoṣaṇakālād uttarakālaṃ māṃsapoṣako rasabhāgo māṃsaṃ poṣayati vidūrasūkṣmamārgacāritvāt evaṃ medaḥprabhṛtipoṣaṇe'pi jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Others, however, say that, according to the principle of pigeons on a threshing-floor, this food-<s>rasa</s>, having gone separately along the paths of the tissues, nourishes <s>rasa</s> and the others. But the portion of <s>rasa</s> that nourishes a tissue does not have even a connection with another tissue. The channels that nourish <s>rasa</s> and the rest have progressively subtler mouths and are long; therefore the portion of nutritive <s>rasa</s> that nourishes <s>rasa</s>, because it travels on the path of <s>rasa</s>, nourishes <s>rasa</s>. In the same way, after the time of <s>rasa</s>-nourishment, the portion of <s>rasa</s> that nourishes blood nourishes blood. Likewise, after the time of blood-nourishment, the portion of <s>rasa</s> that nourishes flesh nourishes flesh, because it travels through a distant and subtle path. The nourishment of fat and the following tissues should be understood in the same way.

children.text: tena rasād raktaṃ tato māṃsam ityāder ayam artho yatra rasapuṣṭikālād uttarakālaṃ raktaṃ jāyate tathā raktapuṣṭikālād uttarakālaṃ māṃsaṃ prajāyate ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the meaning of "from <s>rasa</s> comes blood, from that flesh," and so on, is this: after the time when <s>rasa</s> has been nourished, blood arises; likewise, after the time when blood has been nourished, flesh comes into being, and so forth.
The statements of <s>Suśruta</s> and <s>Hārīta</s> should also be explained in this way.

children.text: yacca raktaṃ vibaddhamārgatvān māṃsādīnna prapadyate iti rājayakṣmaṇi vakṣyati taddhṛdayacāriśoṇitābhiprāyeṇa na tu poṣakaśoṇitābhiprāyeṇa ||
