children.translated_text: And what he will say in the context of <s>rājayakṣman</s>, that blood, because its path is obstructed, does not reach flesh and the other tissues, is intended with reference to blood that circulates through the heart, not with reference to nutritive blood.

children.text: kiṃca pariṇāmapakṣe vṛṣyaprayogasya raktādirūpatāpattikrameṇāticireṇa śukraṃ bhavatīti kṣīrādayaśca sadya eva vṛṣyā dṛśyante khalekapotapakṣe tu vṛṣyotpanno rasaḥ prabhāvācchīghrameva śukreṇa sambaddhaḥ san tatpuṣṭiṃ karotīti yuktaṃ tathā rasaduṣṭau satyāṃ pariṇāmapakṣe tajjanmanāṃ śoṇitādīnāṃ sarveṣāmeva duṣṭiḥ syāt duṣṭakāraṇajātatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, on the theory of transformation, the use of a <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac) would become semen only after a very long time, through the sequence of taking on the form of blood and the rest; yet milk and similar substances are seen to be <s>vṛṣya</s> immediately. But on the <s>khalekapota</s> view, it is reasonable that the rasa produced by the <s>vṛṣya</s>, by its special potency, quickly becomes connected with semen and nourishes it. Likewise, if rasa were vitiated, then on the transformation view all of blood and the other tissues born from it would be vitiated, because they would have arisen from a vitiated cause.

children.text: khalekapotapakṣe tu yaddhātupoṣako rasabhāgo duṣṭaḥ sa eva duṣyati na sarve taditareṣāmaduṣṭakāraṇatvāt tathā medovṛddhau satyāṃ bhūrikāraṇatvenāsthnāpi bhūyasā bhavitavyaṃ dṛśyate ca bhūrimedasa itaradhātuparikṣayaḥ vacanaṃ ca medasvino meda evopacīyate na tathetare dhātavaḥ iti evamādi pariṇāmavāde dūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: But on the <s>khalekapota</s> view, only that portion of rasa which nourishes a given <s>dhātu</s> is vitiated; not all are vitiated, because the causes of the others are not vitiated. Likewise, when fat increases, because the cause is abundant, bone too ought to be abundant; yet in those with much fat, wasting of the other <s>dhātu</s>s is observed. And there is the statement, 'In a fat person, only fat increases, not the other <s>dhātu</s>s in that way.' Such and similar points are objections to the doctrine of transformation.

children.text: eṣu ca pakṣeṣu sarvātmapariṇāmavādo viruddha eva yena sarvātmapariṇāme tricaturopavāsenaiva nīrasatvāccharīrasya maraṇaṃ syāt māsopavāse kevalaṃ śukramayaṃ śarīraṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: And among these positions, the doctrine of complete transformation in every respect is simply contradictory. For if there were complete transformation in every respect, then after only three or four days of fasting the body, being devoid of rasa, would die; and after a month of fasting the body would consist solely of semen.

children.text: kedārīkulyānyāyas tu tulyabala eva khalekapotanyāyena yato yad uktaṃ vṛṣyaprabhāvaṃ prati tat kedārīkulyāpakṣe'pi prabhāvādeva śīghraṃ raktādidhātūnabhigamya śukraṃ janayiṣyati vṛṣyaṃ yathā khalekapotapakṣe'pi prabhavāditi ||
children.translated_text: The <s>kedārīkulyā</s> maxim, however, has exactly the same force as the <s>khalekapota</s> maxim. For what was said with regard to the potency of a <s>vṛṣya</s> applies also on the <s>kedārīkulyā</s> view: by potency alone the <s>vṛṣya</s> will quickly reach the blood and other <s>dhātu</s>s and produce semen, just as, on the <s>khalekapota</s> view too, it does so by potency.

children.text: yattu rasaduṣṭau śoṇitadūṣaṇaṃ tanna bhavati dhātubhūtaśoṇitāṃśapoṣakasya rasabhāgasyāduṣṭatvāt iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa ||
children.translated_text: As for the vitiation of blood when rasa is vitiated, that does not occur, because the portion of rasa that nourishes the blood-component which is a <s>dhātu</s> is not vitiated. This is the same as the preceding argument.

children.text: atrāpi hi pakṣe na sarvo raso dhāturūpaśoṇitatām āpadyate kiṃ tarhi kaścideva śoṇitasamāno bhāgaḥ śeṣastu śoṇitasthānagatatvena kiṃcicchoṇitasamānavarṇāditvācca śoṇitam ucyate anena nyāyena medovṛddhau satyāmasthivṛddhir api nirastā yato na medasā asthi poṣyate api tarhi medaḥsthānagatenaiva rasena medo'nukāriṇā ||
children.translated_text: For in this view too, not all rasa comes to have the state of blood as a <s>dhātu</s>. Rather, only a certain portion is similar to blood; the remainder is called blood because it is located in the place of blood and because it has some similarity to blood in color and the like. By this reasoning, the increase of bone when fat increases is also refuted, since bone is not nourished by fat, but rather by rasa located in the place of fat and resembling fat.

children.text: evamanayoḥ pakṣayormahājanādṛtatvena tulyanyāyatvena ca naikamapi niścitaṃ buddhivibhavānna pakṣabalābalam atra na kaścit kāryavirodha ityuparamyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus, since these two positions are both accepted by learned authorities and have equivalent reasoning, neither one is determined here by my capacity of understanding, nor is the strength or weakness of the positions determined. Since there is no conflict in practical effect here, the matter is set aside.

children.text: nanvāhārarasādayaḥ puṣyantīti vadatā dhāturasādāhārarasotpādaḥ pṛthak svīkriyate tataśca tasya kiṃ sthānaṃ kiṃvā pramāṇam iti kimiti noktam ucyate na tasyāhārotkarṣāpakarṣāv evaṃvidhau utkarṣāpakarṣasya niścitapramāṇatvābhāvāt sthānaṃ tu dhamanya eva ||
children.translated_text: Objection: When one says that the food-rasa and the rest are nourished, a production of food-rasa separate from tissue-rasa is accepted. Why, then, has its location, or its measure, not been stated? The answer is: no. Its increase and decrease are just the increase and decrease of food, because there is no fixed measure for increase and decrease of that sort. Its location, however, is precisely the channels.

children.text: poṣakāhārarasasya tasya ca pṛthagrasādidhātubhyaḥ pradeśāntaragrahaṇaṃ na kriyate rasādikāraṇarūpatayā rasādigrahaṇenaiva grahaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: And no separate region is accepted for that nourishing food-rasa apart from rasa and the other <s>dhātu</s>s, because, since it has the nature of the cause of rasa and the rest, it is included simply by the mention of rasa and the rest.

children.text: atra yadyapyojaḥ saptadhātusārarūpaṃ tena dhātugrahaṇenaiva labhyate tathāpi prāṇadhāraṇakartṛtvena pṛthak paṭhitaṃ ye tu śukrajanyamoja icchanti teṣāmaṣṭamo dhāturojaḥ syāditi pakṣe cātideśaṃ kṛtvā vakṣyati rasādīnāṃ śukrāntānāṃ yat paraṃ tejaḥ tat khalvojaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Here, although <s>ojas</s>, being the essence of the seven <s>dhātu</s>s, is obtained by the mention of the <s>dhātu</s>s themselves, still it is listed separately because it sustains life. But for those who hold that <s>ojas</s> is produced from semen, <s>ojas</s> would be an eighth <s>dhātu</s>. And with reference to that position, after making an extension, he will say: 'The supreme radiance of rasa and the rest down to semen, that indeed is <s>ojas</s>.'

children.text: upapāditapoṣaṇānāṃ dhātumalānāṃ prakṛtyanuvidhānam upasaṃharati te sarva ityādi ||
children.translated_text: He concludes the natural conformity of the <s>dhātu</s>s and <s>mala</s>s whose nourishment has been explained, with the words 'all these' and so on.

children.text: malākhyā api svedamūtrādayaḥ svamānāvasthitā dehadhāraṇāddhātavo bhavantītyuktaṃ dhātavo malākhyā iti ||
children.translated_text: Even sweat, urine, and the like, though called <s>mala</s>s, become <s>dhātu</s>s when they remain in their proper measure, because they support the body. Thus it is said, '<s>dhātu</s>s called <s>mala</s>s.'

children.text: yathāvayaḥśarīram iti yasmin vayasi bālyādau yādṛśaṃ mānaṃ dhātūnāṃ tādṛśaṃ puṣyantaḥ tathā yasmin śarīre prakṛtyā dīrghe hrasve kṛśe vā sthūle vā yādṛśaṃ mānaṃ dhātūnāṃ tādṛśaṃ puṣyanta iti yojanā ||
children.translated_text: 'According to age and body' is to be construed as follows: in whatever age, such as childhood and the rest, whatever measure of the <s>dhātu</s>s exists, they are nourished to that measure; likewise, in whatever body, whether naturally tall, short, thin, or stout, whatever measure of the <s>dhātu</s>s exists, they are nourished to that measure.

children.text: evam ityādau svapramāṇāvasthitāv iti anatiriktāv anyūnau ca ||
children.translated_text: In the passage beginning 'thus,' the phrase 'remaining in their own measure' means neither excessive nor deficient.

children.text: āśrayasyeti śarīrasya yathāvatpakvau sarvāśrayaṃ paścāddhamanībhiḥ prapadyete sarvaśarīram ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Of the support' means of the body. In 'when properly digested, they later reach the whole support through the channels,' the meaning is the whole body.
'Of one whose <s>dhātu</s>s are balanced' means one whose rasa and the rest are balanced, and whose sweat, urine, and the rest are also balanced.
The phrase beginning 'on account of causes' is to be explained.
By the phrase 'on account of causes,' he rules out causeless decrease and increase in the form of fatal signs.

children.text: vṛddhikṣayābhyām āhāramūlābhyām iti yathāsaṃkhyaṃ vṛddhakṣīṇāhārakṛtābhyām etenāhāraviśeṣakṛtavṛddhikṣayo rasaḥ sāmyaṃ karotītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Through increase and decrease rooted in food' means, respectively, through increase caused by increased food and decrease caused by diminished food. By this he means that rasa, whose increase and decrease are produced by particular foods, brings about equilibrium.

children.text: dhātusāmyasyārogyatve siddhe'pi yadārogyāyeti brūte tena prākṛtadhātūnāṃ kṣayeṇa vātivṛddhyā vā sāmyaṃ nirākaroti asya sāmyasya rogakartṛtvād eva ||
children.translated_text: Although it is already established that equilibrium of the <s>dhātu</s>s is health, by saying 'for health' he rules out an equilibrium produced by depletion of the natural <s>dhātu</s>s, or by their excessive increase, since such an equilibrium itself produces disease.

children.text: kiṭṭaṃ ca malānāmevam eveti yathā rasastathā kiṭṭamapyārogyāya malānāṃ sāmyaṃ pratipāditarasakrameṇa karoti ||
children.translated_text: 'And the waste-product is likewise the same for the <s>mala</s>s': just as rasa does, so the waste-product too brings about, for the sake of health, the equilibrium of the <s>mala</s>s according to the process taught for rasa.
He states another treatment for increased <s>mala</s>s with the words beginning 'at their own measure.'

children.text: utsargo bahirniḥsaraṇaṃ saṃśodhanarūpameṣāṃ śāstroktamasti utsargaṃ vā vahantītyutsargiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Utsarga</s> is outward discharge in the form of cleansing; this is prescribed in the teaching for these. Or, because they carry out discharge, they are called <s>utsargin</s>.
He states another treatment for increased <s>mala</s>s with the words beginning 'cold and hot'.

children.text: paryayaḥ viparyayaḥ tena śītoṣṇaviparītaguṇair ityarthaḥ tena śītasamutthe male uṣṇaṃ tathoṣṇasamutthe śītamupacāro bhavati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paryaya</s> means opposite; therefore the meaning is 'by qualities opposite to cold and hot.' Thus, when a <s>mala</s> arises from cold, hot treatment is used, and when it arises from heat, cold treatment is used.

children.text: ādiśabdaś cātra luptanirdiṣṭaḥ tena snigdharūkṣādīnāmapi viparītaguṇānāṃ grahaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Here the word 'and so on' is to be supplied although not explicitly stated; therefore opposite qualities such as unctuous and dry are also included.

children.text: kiṃvā paryayaguṇā dvaṃdvaguṇāḥ snigdharūkṣamṛdutīkṣṇādayaḥ taiśca yathāyogyatayopacaryamāṇā iti jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Or else <s>paryaya</s>-qualities are paired qualities, such as unctuous and dry, soft and sharp; one should understand that the patient is treated by them according to what is appropriate.

children.text: etena vṛddhamalānāṃ trividho 'pyupakramo nidānavarjanaśodhanaśamanarūpa ukto bhavati tatra nidānavarjanaṃ vṛddhamale malavṛddhihetvāhāraparityāgād alpamalāhāropayogād vā boddhavyaṃ saṃśodhanaṃ ca utsargiṇa ityanenoktaṃ śamanaṃ ca śītoṣṇetyādi granthenoktam ||
children.translated_text: By this, all three procedures for increased <s>mala</s>s have been stated: avoidance of the cause, cleansing, and pacification. Among these, avoidance of the cause should be understood, when <s>mala</s> is increased, as abandoning foods that cause increase of <s>mala</s>, or as using foods that produce little <s>mala</s>. Cleansing is stated by the word <s>utsargin</s>, and pacification is stated by the passage beginning 'cold and hot'.

children.text: ayanāni ca tāni mukhāni cetyayanamukhāni atra āyāntyanenetyayanāni mārgāṇi mukhāni tu yaiḥ praviśanti etena malānāṃ dhātūnāṃ ca yadevāyanaṃ tadeva praveśamukhamiti nānyena praveśo nānyena ca gamanam ityuktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: They are both paths and mouths, hence 'path-mouths.' Here, 'paths' are those by which they go, and 'mouths' are those by which they enter. By this it is said that the very path of the <s>mala</s>s and <s>dhātu</s>s is also their entrance-mouth: there is no entry by one route and no movement by another.
For <s>rasa</s> and the others, the mouth of the channel is, according to each one's own name, both the entrance and the path.

children.text: kiṃvā ayanasya gamanasya mukhāni mārgāṇi tena ayanamukhāni gatimārgāṇītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or else, they are the mouths, that is, the routes, of the path or movement; therefore 'path-mouths' means the routes of motion.

children.text: tāni ca srotāṃsi malaprasādapūritāni dhātūn yathāsvamiti yadyasya poṣyaṃ tacca tat pūrayati ||
children.translated_text: And those <s>srotas</s>es, filled with <s>mala</s> and <s>prasāda</s>, fill the <s>dhātu</s>s each according to its own nature: whatever is to be nourished by a given one, that it fills.

children.text: yathāvibhāgeneti yasya dhātoryo vibhāgaḥ pramāṇaṃ tenaiva pramāṇena pūrayati tādṛkpramāṇānyeva puṣyanti nādhikanyūnānītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'According to division' means: whatever division, that is, measure, belongs to a <s>dhātu</s>, it fills it in precisely that measure. The meaning is that only things of such a measure are nourished, not more or less.

children.text: etacca prakṛtisthānāṃ karma vikṛtānāṃ tu nyūnātiriktadhātukaraṇam astyeveti boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: And this is the function of those that remain in their natural condition. But in the case of those that are impaired, one should understand that they do produce deficient or excessive <s>dhātu</s>s.

children.text: uktaṃ cānyatra srotasā ca yathāsvena dhātuḥ puṣyati dhātunā iti ||
children.translated_text: And it is said elsewhere: 'By means of its own channel, a <s>dhātu</s> nourishes the <s>dhātu</s>.'
He concludes with the words beginning 'thus'.
How can opposed results, namely the body and disease that injures it, arise from what is eaten and the like? To answer this he says, 'wholesome and unwholesome,' and so on.

children.text: hitarūpo'śitādiviśeṣaḥ śubharūpaviśeṣakārakaḥ ahitarūpastvaśitādiviśeṣo 'śubharūpaviśeṣakaro bhavati tena naikarūpāt kāraṇād viruddhakāryodaya iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A particular kind of what is eaten and the like that has the form of the wholesome produces a particular form of good, while a particular kind of what is eaten and the like that has the form of the unwholesome produces a particular form of harm. Therefore the intention is that opposed effects do not arise from a cause of one single form.

children.text: dṛśyante hi bhagavannityādau tathaivāhitasamākhyātam upayuñjānā vyādhimantaś cāgadāśceti sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the passage beginning 'For they are seen, O venerable one,' the construction is: likewise, those who use what is called harmful are seen both as diseased and as free from disease.
'Of a particular nature' means arising from particularity.
'Having that as their cause' means caused by wholesome food.
'Not merely' means 'only'.
'Disease-natures' means causes of disease.
'Those who use unwholesome food,' and so on.

children.text: kāraṇata iti nimittāntarāt pratibandhāt tacca kāraṇaṃ tadeva hy apathyam ityādivakṣyamāṇagranthaviparītaṃ boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: 'Because of a cause' means because of another cause, namely an obstruction. And that cause should be understood as the opposite of the passage to be stated, beginning 'For that very unwholesome thing'.
'Immediately' means at that very time.

children.text: anenāpathyasya rogajananaṃ prati kālāntaravikārakartṛtvaṃ prāyo bhavatīti darśayati anyathā sadya ityanarthakaṃ syāt kālāntare 'pi doṣākartṛtvāt ||
children.translated_text: By this he shows that, in general, an unwholesome thing produces disease after an interval of time. Otherwise the word 'immediately' would be pointless, since there would be no production of <s>doṣa</s> even at a later time.
'<s>Doṣa</s>-possessing' means productive of disease.

children.text: apacāra iti ahitāhāropayogaḥ ukte kāraṇamāha nahītyādi ||
children.translated_text: 'Improper conduct' means the use of unwholesome food. He gives the reason for what has been said with the words beginning 'for not'.
'Equal in <s>doṣa</s>' means producing an equal <s>doṣa</s>.
Capacity to withstand disease means opposition to the strength of disease, that is, prevention of the arising of disease.
He explains that very equality with the <s>doṣa</s> of the unwholesome thing with the words beginning 'that very'.

children.text: atra yadyapi prastutatvād apathyapratibandhakāni kāraṇāni vaktavyāni tathāpi samānanyāyatayāpathyaśaktivardhakānyucyante ||
children.translated_text: Here, although because of the present topic the causes that obstruct the unwholesome thing ought to be stated, still, because the principle is the same, the factors that strengthen the power of an unwholesome thing are stated.

children.text: tatra deśādīnāṃ yogāditi anuguṇadeśādiyogāt yathā vrīhiḥ pittakartṛtvenāpathyaḥ sa cānūpadeśayogādbhūyastaram apathyo bhavati dhanvadeśe tu hīnabalo bhavati tathā śaratkālasyānuguṇasya yogādbalavānbhavati hemante durbalaḥ saṃyogād yathā sa vrīhir dadhiphāṇitādiyukto balavān madhvādiyuktaśca durbalaḥ vīryād yathā sa evoṣṇīkṛto balavān śītastu durbalaḥ sa eva ca pramāṇātiyogād balī hīnamātrastvabalaḥ ityādyanusartavyam ||
children.translated_text: There, 'through conjunction with place and so on' means through conjunction with a favorable place and the rest. For example, rice is unwholesome because it produces <s>pitta</s>; when it is joined with marshy country it becomes still more unwholesome, but in dry country it has weak strength. Likewise, when joined with the favorable autumn season it becomes strong, but in winter it is weak. By combination, that same rice, joined with curds, treacle, and the like, is strong, but joined with honey and the like it is weak. By potency, that same rice when heated is strong, but when cold it is weak. And that very same rice, by excess in quantity, is powerful, while in a small measure it is weak. This and similar cases should be followed out.
He states equality with the strength of the <s>doṣa</s> with the words beginning 'that same <s>doṣa</s>'.

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭā militā bahavo yonayaḥ kāraṇāni yasya sa tathā kiṃvā saṃsṛṣṭayonir iti anuguṇadūṣyaḥ yathā pittasya raktaṃ dūṣyam āsādya kaṣṭatvaṃ kṣiprakāritvaṃ ca bhavati ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Saṃsṛṣṭa-yoni</s>' means one for which many sources, that is, causes, are combined. Or else <s>saṃsṛṣṭa-yoni</s> means one that has a favorable thing to be vitiated; for example, when <s>pitta</s> has reached blood as the thing to be vitiated, it becomes difficult to treat and acts quickly.

children.text: viruddhopakramo yathā pittaṃ mehārambhakaṃ vacanaṃ hi pittamehāḥ sarva eva yāpyāḥ viruddhopakramatvāt iti viruddhatā copakramasyātra yat pittaharaṃ madhurādi tanmehapradhānadūṣyamedaso viruddhaṃ medo'nuguṇaṃ tu kaṭvādi pitte viruddham iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Opposed in treatment' is illustrated by <s>pitta</s> that initiates <s>meha</s>. For the statement says: 'All <s>pitta</s>-type <s>meha</s>s are manageable but not curable, because their treatment is opposed.' The opposition of treatment here is that sweet and similar substances that remove <s>pitta</s> are opposed to fat, the principal thing vitiated in <s>meha</s>, while pungent and similar substances that are favorable to fat are opposed to <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: gambhīrānugata iti gambhīramajjādidhātugataḥ vacanaṃ hi tvaṅmāṃsāśrayamuttānaṃ gambhīraṃ tv antarāśrayam iti ||
children.translated_text: "Having gone deep" means having gone into deep tissues such as marrow; for the saying is: what is based in skin and flesh is superficial, but what is based internally is deep.

children.text: cirasthita iti dehe cirakālāvasthānena kṛtamūlatvāt kaṣṭasādhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Long-standing" means difficult to cure because, by remaining in the body for a long time, it has taken root.
"Arisen from the seats of life" means based in the ten seats of life, such as the temples, which will be stated in the following chapter.
"Injuring vital points" means causing injury to vital points such as <s>kṣipra</s>, the sole, and the heart, apart from the seats of life.

children.text: marmaghātitvenaiva marmaviśeṣaprāṇāyatanasamutthatve labdhe punastadvacanaṃ prāṇāyatanamarmāśrayiṇo viśeṣeṇa kaṣṭatvapratipādanārtham ||
children.translated_text: Since, by its very injuring of vital points, its origin from the particular vital points that are seats of life is already obtained, their repeated mention is for the purpose of showing the special difficulty of diseases based in vital points that are seats of life.
"Most difficult" means because it produces much suffering and because it is incurable.
"Most rapidly acting" means extremely quick in producing disorder.

children.text: cakārāt saṃsṛṣṭayonitvādihetūnām alpatvena kaṣṭakaṣṭatarakṣiprakārikṣiprakāritarādiviśeṣāś ca bhavantīti darśayati yathoktasarvahetumelake kaṣṭatamaḥ kṣiprakāritamaś ca bhavatīti jñeyaṃ kaṣṭatamatvādi ca yathāyogyatayā jñeyaṃ viruddhopakramo doṣaḥ kaṣṭa eva bhavati na kṣiprakārī ||
children.translated_text: And by the word "and" he shows that, when causes such as mixed origin are present only in small degree, there are distinctions such as difficult, more difficult, rapidly acting, and more rapidly acting. When all the stated causes are combined, it should be known to be most difficult and most rapidly acting. The state of being most difficult and so forth should be understood according to what is appropriate. A <s>doṣa</s> requiring an opposite treatment is difficult indeed, but not rapidly acting.
He states the bodies that are susceptible to disease, with the words "and bodies," and so on.

children.text: aniviṣṭāni ślathāni māṃsādīni yeṣāṃ śarīriṇāṃ tāni tathā kiṃvā aniviṣṭānīti viṣamāṇi ||
children.translated_text: "Not firmly settled" means those beings whose flesh and other tissues are loose; or else "not firmly settled" means uneven.

children.text: upacitānīti saṃvardhitāni asātmyapuṣṭaṃ hi śarīraṃ bhūridoṣabhāvitameva bhavatīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Built up" means increased; the sense is that a body nourished by what is unsuitable is necessarily affected by many <s>doṣas</s>.
"Opposite" means possessing qualities such as not being excessively corpulent.
"Resistant to disease" means obstructing the production of disease.

children.text: etacca śarīramadhikṛtya vaiparītyaṃ vyādhisahatve udāharaṇārtham upanyastaṃ tena yathoktāpathyabalavaiparītyaṃ doṣabalavaiparītyaṃ ca na sadyo vyādhikārakaṃ bhavatītyetad apyuktaṃ boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: This opposition, when the body is under discussion, is set forth as an example of resistance to disease. Therefore one should understand that opposition to the strength of the unwholesome regimen already described, and opposition to the strength of the <s>doṣa</s>, also do not immediately produce disease.

children.text: etad evāpathyāhāradoṣaśarīrāṇām evābalavattvabalavattvābhyāṃ lakṣaṇaviśeṣaṃ yathāyogyatayā mṛdvādivyādhikāraṇatvenopasaṃharann āha ebhyaś caivetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Summing up these very special characteristics of unwholesome foods, <s>doṣas</s>, and bodies, according to whether they are weak or strong, as causes of mild and other diseases in the proper way, he says, "And from these," and so on.

children.text: viśeṣā yathoktā uktaviparītāśca tatroktaviparītaviśeṣān mṛdavastathā cirakāriṇaśca bhavanti yathoktāpathyādiviśeṣāttu dāruṇāḥ kṣiprakāriṇaśca bhavantīti mantavyam ||
children.translated_text: The special factors are those stated above and their opposites. Among them, from the special factors opposite to those stated, diseases are mild and also slow-acting; but from the stated special factors of unwholesome regimen and the rest, they should be understood as severe and rapidly acting.

children.text: anena prasaṅgena vātādīnāṃ rasādisthānaviśeṣeṣu kupitānāṃ ye vyādhayo bhavanti tān darśayitum āha ta evetyādi ||
children.translated_text: In this connection, in order to show the diseases that arise when <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s> are aggravated in particular locations such as <s>rasa</s>, he says, "Those very," and so on.

children.text: tatra rasetyādau prakupitānāṃ doṣāṇāmiti aniyamena rase kupito vāyur vā pittaṃ vā śleṣmā vā saṃsṛṣṭā vā aśraddhādīni kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: There, in the passage beginning with "in <s>rasa</s>," the phrase "of the aggravated <s>doṣas</s>" is unrestricted: <s>vāyu</s>, or <s>pitta</s>, or <s>śleṣman</s>, or combined <s>doṣas</s>, aggravated in <s>rasa</s>, produce lack of desire for food and the rest.

children.text: satyapi doṣabhede 'trāśrayasyābhedād āśrayaprabhāveṇaivāśraddhādayo bhavanti paraṃ doṣabhede aśraddhādāv eva vātādiliṅgaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Although there is a difference among the <s>doṣas</s>, here, because the substrate is not different, lack of desire for food and the rest arise precisely through the effect of the substrate. Yet when the <s>doṣa</s> differs, the sign of <s>vāta</s> and the others is particularized within lack of desire for food and the like itself.

children.text: kiṃvā yathāyogyatayā rasāśrayiṇā vātādinā aśraddhādikaraṇaṃ boddhavyaṃ yato na gauravaṃ vātaduṣṭarase bhavitumarhati etacca nātisundaraṃ tena pūrva eva pakṣo jyāyān ||
children.translated_text: Or else, according to what is appropriate, the production of lack of desire for food and the rest should be understood as caused by <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s> lodged in <s>rasa</s>, since heaviness cannot properly occur in <s>rasa</s> vitiated by <s>vāta</s>. But this is not very good; therefore the former view is preferable.

children.text: aśraddhāyāṃ mukhapraviṣṭasyāhārasyābhyavaharaṇaṃ bhavatyeva paraṃ tv anicchā arucau tu mukhapraviṣṭaṃ nābhyavaharatīti bhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In lack of desire for food, food that has entered the mouth is indeed swallowed, but there is unwillingness; in distaste, however, what has entered the mouth is not swallowed. This is the distinction.
"Bad taste in the mouth" is the alteration of the taste of the mouth from its usual state.
"Inability to know taste" is non-apprehension of taste.
"Lassitude" is collapse or languor of the limbs.

children.text: raktapradoṣajeṣu kuṣṭhagrahaṇādeva dadrvādilābhe siddhe punastadvacanaṃ viśeṣaprādurbhāvapradarśanārtham ||
children.translated_text: Among diseases born from vitiation of blood, even though ringworm and the like are already obtained from the mention of <s>kuṣṭha</s>, the repeated mention of it is for showing the manifestation of particular forms.
"Tilakālakas" are marks shaped like sesame seeds.
"Asramaṇḍala" means a red, blood-like circle.
Here, by the word <s>kīla</s>, hemorrhoids are meant.

children.text: ninditāni pramehapūrvarūpāṇīti keśajaṭilatvādīni teṣāmeva ninditatvāt na tv āsyavairasyamadhuratvādīni ||
children.translated_text: "Blameworthy" means the preliminary signs of <s>prameha</s>, such as matting of the hair, because those alone are blameworthy, not bad taste or sweetness in the mouth and the like.

children.text: kiṃvā ninditānīti atisthūlagatāny āyurhrāsādīny aṣṭauninditīyoktāni teṣāṃ ca ninditatvaṃ ninditātisthūlasambaddhatvena ||
children.translated_text: Or else "blameworthy" means the eight blameworthy conditions, such as shortening of life, that belong to the excessively corpulent and are stated in the chapter on the eight blameworthy persons. Their blameworthiness is because they are connected with blameworthy excessive corpulence.

children.text: evaṃ pūrvasminvyākhyāne yāni ca iti cakāro niyame uttaravyākhyāne tu samuccaye ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the former explanation, the word "and" in "and those which" has a restrictive force; but in the latter explanation it has a conjunctive force.
By the expression "extra bone and teeth," both extra bone and extra teeth are included.
"Pain" should be understood as pain in the bone itself.
"Aching," and so on, should be known as arising from a <s>doṣa</s> of the marrow.
"Arūṃṣi" means wounds.
"Impotence" means non-erection of the penis.
And "lack of pleasure" is incapacity for intercourse even when erection of the penis is present.

children.text: śukraṃ hi duṣṭaṃ sāpatyaṃ sadāraṃ bādhate naramiti atrāpatyabādhā rogiklībādyapatyajanakatvena dārabādhā tu srāvigarbhādijanakatvena ||
children.translated_text: For in the statement, "Corrupted semen afflicts a man together with his offspring and wife," affliction of offspring means producing diseased, impotent, and similar children; affliction of the wife means producing miscarriage accompanied by discharge and the like.

children.text: upaghātetyādau upaghāto vināśaḥ upatāpastu kiṃcid vaikalyam ||
children.translated_text: In the passage beginning with "injury," injury is destruction, while distress is a certain impairment.
In "from the sinews," the ablative is used in the sense of the locative.
"Khallī" is contraction or twisting of the hands and feet.
"Granthi" is specifically a knot or tumor of sinew and the like.

children.text: malānityādau bhedaśoṣapradūṣaṇam iti yathāsambhavaṃ jñeyaṃ tatra bhedaḥ purīṣasya śoṣastu viśeṣeṇa sarvamaleṣu sambhavati pradūṣaṇaṃ tu praduṣṭavarṇādiyuktatvena prākṛtavarṇādyupaghātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the passage beginning with wastes and the like, "division, drying, and vitiation" should be understood according to what is possible in each case. There, division belongs to feces; drying, however, occurs especially in all wastes. Vitiation is the impairment of the natural color and so on through being accompanied by a corrupted color and the like.

children.text: saṃgotsargāv atīva ceti atīva saṅgaḥ apravṛttiḥ atyutsargastu atipravṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Excessive retention and discharge" means this: excessive retention is non-elimination, while excessive discharge is over-elimination.

children.text: sampratyahitāhārajanitān doṣān darśayan yathākartavyam upadiśati vividhādityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, showing the <s>doṣa</s>s produced by unsuitable food, he instructs what is to be done, with the passage beginning "various."
The remainder to be supplied is: "it has been said to be conquered by the physician."

children.text: pañcakarmāṇītyabhidhāyāpi vastaya iti vacanaṃ tiktopahitavaster viśeṣeṇa hitatvopadarśanārtham ||
children.translated_text: Although he has already said "the five procedures," the statement "the <s>basti</s>s" is made to show that a <s>basti</s> prepared with bitter substances is especially beneficial.
"Purification" means by emesis and the other procedures.
"Success is stated somewhere" means in conditions such as diarrhea and <s>grahaṇī</s>.

children.text: samprati rasādīnāṃ śākhārūpatvāt koṣṭhāśrayiṇo doṣā yathā śākhāṃ yānti tad āha vyāyāmetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, because <s>rasa</s> and the others have the form of branches, he explains how <s>doṣa</s>s based in the <s>koṣṭha</s> go to the branches, with the passage beginning "by exercise."

children.text: tatra vyāyāmakṣobhāt koṣṭhaṃ parityajya śākhāṃ malā yānti ūṣmaṇo vahnestīkṣṇatvād vilāyitā doṣāḥ śākhāṃ yānti hitasyānavacāraṇayāhitasevayātisevayātimātravṛddho doṣo jalāpūravad vṛddhaḥ svasthānamāplāvya sthānāntaraṃ yātīti yuktam ||
children.translated_text: There, because of agitation by exercise, the wastes leave the <s>koṣṭha</s> and go to the branches. Because of the sharpness of heat, that is, of fire, liquefied <s>doṣa</s>s go to the branches. Through failure to practice what is wholesome, through resorting to what is unwholesome, and through excessive use, a <s>doṣa</s> that has increased beyond measure, swollen like a flood of water, inundates its own place and goes to another place; this is reasonable.

children.text: drutatvānmārutasyeti calatvād vāyor vāyunā kṣipto yātītyarthaḥ vāyvantareṇa ca vāyor ākṣepaṇamupapannam eveti anyathā malā iti bahuvacanam asādhu ||
children.translated_text: "Because of the swiftness of <s>māruta</s>" means because of the mobility of <s>vāyu</s>; the sense is that, driven by <s>vāyu</s>, it goes. And the propulsion of one <s>vāyu</s> by another <s>vāyu</s> is indeed possible; otherwise the plural "wastes" would be incorrect.
Now he says what those that have gone to the branches do, with the passage beginning "and standing there."

children.text: vilambante kadācid iti kadācidvyādhikaraṇe vilambaṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: "They linger sometimes" means that, at times, they cause lingering in the locus of disease.
Why do they linger? He says: "not set in motion."

children.text: ye doṣā alpatvenābalavantaste hetvantareṇa samīritāḥ santaḥ kupyanti tathā ta eva nādeśa ityananuguṇadeśe tathā nākāla ityananuguṇakāle kupyantīti yojanā ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>doṣa</s>s which, because of their small quantity, are weak become aggravated when they are set in motion by some other cause. The construction is also that those same ones become aggravated not in a wrong place, that is, in a favorable place, and not at a wrong time, that is, at a favorable time.
He gives the reason for this here, with the passage beginning "again."

children.text: yasmād bhūyo hetupratīkṣiṇas te 'lpabalā doṣāstasmādīraṇādyapekṣante etena bhūyo ye 'hetupratīkṣiṇo bhavanti balavattvānna te īraṇādyapekṣante ata evoktaṃ kadāciditi ||
children.translated_text: Because those weak <s>doṣa</s>s wait again for a cause, therefore they depend on being set in motion and the like. By this it is implied that those which do not wait again for a cause, because of their strength, do not depend on being set in motion and the like. For just this reason the word "sometimes" was used.

children.text: samprati śākhābhyaḥ koṣṭhāgamanahetuṃ doṣāṇām āha vṛddhyetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now he states the causes for the <s>doṣa</s>s coming from the branches back to the <s>koṣṭha</s>, with the passage beginning "through increase."

children.text: viṣyandanāditi vilayanāt vilīnaśca dravatvādeva koṣṭhe nimnaṃ yāti ||
children.translated_text: "Through liquefaction" means through melting; and because it is fluid, what has melted goes downward into the <s>koṣṭha</s>.

children.text: pākāditi pakvo doṣo 'baddhatvenaiva nimnaṃ koṣṭhaṃ yāti ||
children.translated_text: "Through ripening" means that a ripened <s>doṣa</s>, precisely because it is no longer bound, goes downward to the <s>koṣṭha</s>.
"Through cleansing the mouths of the channels" means because the obstruction has been removed.

children.text: vāyornigrahāditi kṣepturvāyornigrahāt prākṛtaṃ sthānaṃ koṣṭhaṃ yāti ||
children.translated_text: "Through restraint of <s>vāyu</s>" means that, because the ejecting <s>vāyu</s> has been restrained, it goes to its natural place, the <s>koṣṭha</s>.
Now he states in aphoristic form the treatment for all diseases without exception, with the passage beginning "of those not yet arisen."
"The method that has been seen" means in the whole treatise.

children.text: nanu yadi sukhārthā sarvaprāṇināṃ pravṛttistatkathaṃ ko 'pi amārge pravartata ityāha jñānetyādi ||
children.translated_text: But if the activity of all living beings is for the sake of happiness, how does anyone proceed on a wrong path? In answer he says, with the passage beginning "knowledge."

children.text: ajñānād eva sukhasādhanamidam iti kṛtvā aparīkṣakāḥ pravartante na tu duḥkhakartṛtāsaṃdhānād iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is from ignorance alone that unexamining people act, thinking, "this is a means to happiness," and not because they recognize that it produces suffering. This is the intention.

children.text: hitameveti āyativiśuddham eva tadātve duḥkhakaram api ||
children.translated_text: "Beneficial alone" means pure with respect to the future, even if it causes suffering at the present moment.
"Pleasant alone" means producing happiness at the present moment but opposed to future welfare.
"Ordinary people" means unexamining people.
He praises the examiner, with the passage beginning "what has been heard."

children.text: parīkṣakamāśrayantīti parīkṣake bhavanti kiṃvā buddhyādidevatāḥ parīkṣakamāśrayante yad uktaṃ viviśur jñānadevatāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: "They resort to the examiner" means that they exist in the examiner. Or else the deities of intellect and the other faculties resort to the examiner, as it is said, "the deities of knowledge entered."
"Rooted in them" means rooted in <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: yathā aparīkṣake rajastamomūlā rogā bhavanti tadāha prajñāparādhād ityādi ||
children.translated_text: He explains how diseases rooted in <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> arise in an unexamining person, with the passage beginning "from an offense against wisdom."
The intention is that resorting to harmful objects and the like also produces disease.

children.text: tadātvasukheṣviti vaktavye yat sukhasaṃjñeṣu iti karoti tattadātvasukhasyāpathyasya duḥkhānubandhasukhakartṛtayā paramārthatas tadātve 'pyasukhatvaṃ darśayati yathā sukhasaṃjñakam ārogyam ityatroktam ||
children.translated_text: Where one would expect him to say "among pleasures of the present moment," he says "among things called pleasure." By this he shows that the immediate pleasure that is unwholesome is not truly happiness even at the present moment, because it produces pleasure followed by suffering, just as was stated in the expression "health is called happiness."
"One who has understood" means an examiner.
"Not from passion," and so on.

children.text: ahitatvena jānann api rāgādeva kaścid duṣṭaḥ pravartate ajñānāccāhitatvājñānād eva kaściddhitādhyavasāyena pravartate etaddvayamapi niṣidhyate ||
children.translated_text: Someone corrupt acts from passion alone, even while knowing something to be harmful; another, from ignorance, acts with the conviction that it is beneficial precisely because he does not know it to be harmful. Both of these are prohibited.
How should food be examined? He says, with the passage beginning "of food."

children.text: āhārasya vidhau vidhāne'ṣṭau viśeṣāḥ prakṛtikaraṇasaṃyogādayo rasavimāne vaktavyā hetusaṃjñakāḥ kva hetusaṃjñakā ityāha śubhetyādi ||
children.translated_text: In the rule, that is, the prescription, of food there are eight particulars, nature, processing, combination, and the rest, which are to be stated in the <s>Rasavimāna</s> and are called causes. Where are they called causes? He says, with the passage beginning "good."

children.text: śubhāśubhasamutpattau iti te ca prakṛtyādayaḥ śubhāḥ śubhakarāḥ aśubhā aśubhakarāḥ iti jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: "In the production of good and bad" means that those nature and the others are to be understood as good, that is, productive of good, or bad, that is, productive of bad.

children.text: nanu pathyasevāyāṃ kriyamāṇāyām api balavatprāktanādharmavaśādapi vyādhayo bhavanti tat kim anena pathyasevanenetyāha parihāryāṇītyādi ||
children.translated_text: But even when wholesome regimen is being practiced, diseases occur through the force of powerful prior <s>adharma</s>. What, then, is the use of this practice of wholesome regimen? To this he says, with the passage beginning "things to be avoided."

children.text: anṛṇatām iva prāpto'nṛṇatāṃ prāptaḥ etena parihāryaparihāreṇa puruṣakāre'naparādhaḥ puruṣo bhavatīti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: "As though one has attained freedom from debt" means one has become free from debt. By this he shows that, through avoidance of what should be avoided, a person is not at fault in the matter of personal effort.

children.text: yastu daivāgatastasya vyādhistatra sādhavo naivaṃ pathyasevinaṃ garhayanti etadevāha yattvityādi ||
children.translated_text: But as for a disease that has come from <s>daiva</s> (fate), in that case good men do not blame a person who follows a wholesome regimen. He states just this with the words beginning "but what."
"Impossible to avoid" means because it is produced by powerful <s>karma</s>.

children.text: na śocitavyam iti puruṣakārasya daivajanye 'vaśyambhāvini vyādhāv akiṃcitkaratvād ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "It should not be grieved over" means because human effort is ineffective with regard to a disease born from <s>daiva</s> and bound to occur.
In the summary, "substance" means the body.

children.text: sahatve cāsahatve cetyādinā śarīrāṇi cātisthūlāni ityādi viparītāni punar vyādhisahāni ityantaṃ granthaṃ jñāpayati ||
children.translated_text: With the passage beginning "with endurance and non-endurance," he indicates the text beginning "bodies that are excessively stout" and so on, down to "and the opposite ones are resistant to disease."
Now he establishes that the <s>dhamanī</s>s have a great root, with the words beginning "by that."

children.text: teneti hṛdayena mahatā yuktāḥ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "By that" means by the heart; "endowed with the great one" is to be supplied.
"They are sent out" means they spread forth.

children.text: saṃprati dhamanīnām uktaṃ mahāphalatvaṃ vyutpādayannāha yenaujasetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, explaining the previously stated great fruitfulness of the <s>dhamanī</s>s, he says, with the words beginning "by which <s>ojas</s>."
By "by which <s>ojas</s>," <s>ojas</s> of both kinds is to be understood in a general way.
"They make live" means "they live"; <s>vartayanti</s> is a causative of the <s>curādi</s> class.
"Satisfied" means nourished.

children.text: yat sāramādau garbhasyeti śukraśoṇitasaṃyoge jīvādhiṣṭhitamātre yat sārabhūtaṃ tatrāpi tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: "Whatever is the essence at the beginning of the embryo" means that the essential part also remains there when the semen and blood have united and are merely occupied by the living self.

children.text: yat tadgarbharasād rasa iti garbharasācchukraśoṇitasaṃyogapariṇāmena kalalarūpāt rasa iti sārabhūtam ||
children.translated_text: "What from that embryonic fluid is <s>rasa</s>" means the essence called <s>rasa</s> from the embryonic fluid, in the form of the <s>kalala</s>, through the transformation of the union of semen and blood.

children.text: saṃvartamānaṃ hṛdayaṃ samāviśati yat pureti yadā hṛdayaṃ niṣpadyamānaṃ tadaiva vyaktalakṣaṇaṃ saddhṛdayam adhitiṣṭhati yadityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "It enters the heart as it is forming, what was before" means: when the heart is being produced, then that same entity, possessing manifest characteristics, occupies the heart.

children.text: etena garbhāvasthātraye'pi tad ojas tiṣṭhatītyucyate paraṃ garbhādau śukraśoṇitasārarūpatayā kalalāvasthāyāṃ tu rasasārarūpatayā avayavaniṣpattau tu svalakṣaṇayuktam eva bhavatyoja ityojasaḥ sarvāvasthāvyāpakatvena mahattvam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: By this it is said that that <s>ojas</s> exists in all three embryonic stages. At the very beginning of the embryo it has the form of the essence of semen and blood; in the <s>kalala</s> stage it has the form of the essence of <s>rasa</s>; and when the limbs have been produced, <s>ojas</s> itself has its own defining characteristics. Thus the greatness of <s>ojas</s> is stated because it pervades all stages.

children.text: yasya nāśāttu nāśo'stīti dhātvantarākṣaye'pi satyojaḥkṣaye maraṇamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "From whose destruction there is destruction" means that even when the other <s>dhātu</s>s have not been exhausted, death occurs when <s>ojas</s> is exhausted.
"Bearer" is said because it is chief among the things connected with sustaining life.

children.text: śarīrarasasneha iti śarīrasārasāraṃ rasaśabdaḥ snehaśabdaśca sāravacanaḥ tena śarīrarasānāṃ dhātūnāmapi sāra ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "The unctuous essence of the body's fluids" means the essence of the essences of the body. The words <s>rasa</s> and <s>sneha</s> both express essence; therefore the meaning is that it is the essence even of the bodily fluids, the <s>dhātu</s>s.
And this is, in another manner, a statement of the single function of especially important things, in order to make known the special importance of <s>ojas</s>.
"Having that as their fruit" means having <s>ojas</s> as their fruit, that is, carrying <s>ojas</s>.

children.text: etena yathoktaguṇaśālitvenaujo mahat etadvahanena phalantīveti mahāphalā dhamanya uktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this, since <s>ojas</s> possesses the qualities just described, it is great; and because they carry it, the <s>dhamanī</s>s are said to be great-fruited, as though they bear fruit.

children.text: dvitīyāṃ niruktimāha bahudhā vā tāḥ phalantīti tā hṛdayāśritā daśadhamanyo bahudhā anekaprakāraṃ phalantīti niṣpadyante etena mūle hṛdaye daśarūpāḥ satyo mahāsaṃkhyāḥ śarīre pratānabhedādbhavantītyuktam ||
children.translated_text: He gives a second derivation: "or they bear fruit in many ways." Those ten <s>dhamanī</s>s based in the heart bear fruit, that is, come forth, in many ways and in many forms. By this he says that, although at their root in the heart they exist as ten, they become very numerous in the body through differences of branching.

children.text: hetorhetutvaṃ kārye bhavatīti hetukāryaṃ vyādhimāha atastrividhā ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Because the causal status of a cause exists in its effect, he states disease as the effect of the cause, with the words beginning "therefore threefold."

children.text: na cātra yathāsaṃkhyam ekarūpādapi hetos trividhavyādhyutpādāt ||
children.translated_text: And here there is no one-to-one correspondence in order, because threefold disease can arise even from a cause of a single kind.
Here too, the statement that diseases are threefold is made to show that, although diseases are endless, they do not go beyond being fiery and so forth.

children.text: āgneyāḥ paittikāḥ saumyāḥ kaphajāḥ vāyavyāḥ vātajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Fiery" diseases are those due to <s>pitta</s>; "watery" diseases are those due to <s>kapha</s>; "windy" diseases are those due to <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: yadyapi pradhānatvena vāyavyā eva prathamaṃ nirdeṣṭuṃ yujyante tathāpīha jvare pittasya pradhānatvād āgneyābhidhānam ||
children.translated_text: Although, because of its primacy, the windy type ought to be mentioned first, nevertheless here the fiery type is named because <s>pitta</s> is predominant in fever.

children.text: āgneyasaumyavāyavyā iti samāsenaikaikasmād apyasātmyendriyārthasaṃyogādes trividharogotpattitvaṃ darśayati asamāse hi yathāsaṃkhyamapi śaṅkyeta ||
children.translated_text: By using the compound "fiery, watery, and windy," he shows that from each single cause, such as unsuitable contact of the senses with their objects, three kinds of disease arise. For if there were no compound, a one-to-one correspondence in order might be suspected.
He also states, in another way, diseases born from causes not yet mentioned, with the words beginning "and there are two further kinds."

children.text: rājasatāmasānāṃ ca vicchidya pāṭheneha tantre śārīravyādhyadhikārapravṛtte 'nadhikāratvenāprapañcanīyatvaṃ darśayati abhidhānaṃ ca rājasatāmasayoriha vyādhikathanasya nyūnatāparihārārtham ||
children.translated_text: By reading the <s>rājasa</s> and <s>tāmasa</s> diseases separately here, in a treatise whose topic is bodily diseases, he shows that they are not to be elaborated because they are outside the present topic. The mention of <s>rājasa</s> and <s>tāmasa</s> here is meant to avoid incompleteness in the account of diseases.

children.text: āgantavaścābhighātādijā rogā āgneyādiṣvevāntarbhavanti yatastatrāpi hi doṣaprakopo 'vyapadeśyo 'styeva kiṃvā apare iti apradhānāḥ paro hi śreṣṭha ucyate apradhānatve coktaivopapattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Adventitious diseases, those born from injury and the like, are included within the fiery and other classes, since even there an aggravation of the <s>doṣa</s>s certainly exists, though it may not be explicitly designated. Or else "further" means non-principal, for <s>para</s> is said of what is superior; and if they are non-principal, the justification has already been stated.

children.text: idānīṃ vyādherjanakahetumabhidhāya tathā taddhetujanyaṃ ca vyādhim uktvā tasya vyādher jñānopāyam āha tasyetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, having stated the disease-producing cause and also the disease produced by that cause, he states the means of knowing that disease, with the words beginning "of that."

children.text: avijñāte hi vyādhau cikitsā na pravartate ataḥ sāmānyena vyādhijñānopāyanidānapañcakābhidhānaṃ yuktam ||
children.translated_text: For when the disease is not known, treatment does not proceed. Therefore it is proper to state, in general, the fivefold diagnostic means for knowing disease.
He explains <s>nidāna</s> (cause), with the words beginning "there."

children.text: agre uktamiti iha khalu ityādinā pariṇāmaśca ityantena ||
children.translated_text: "It was stated before" means in the passage beginning "here indeed" and ending with "and transformation."

children.text: kāraṇaṃ ca vyādhīnāṃ saṃnikṛṣṭaṃ vātādi viprakṛṣṭaṃ cārthānāmayogādi punarviprakṛṣṭaṃ kāraṇaṃ raktapittasya jvarasaṃtāpa ityādi punaśca vyādhīnāṃ sāmānyena viprakṛṣṭaṃ kāraṇamuktaṃ yathā prāgapi cādharmādṛte na rogotpattirabhūt ityādi tadetat sarvamapi kāraṇaśabdena grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: The cause of diseases is both proximate, such as <s>vāta</s> and the others, and remote, such as improper contact with objects; and a still more remote cause, for example of <s>raktapitta</s>, is fever-heat and the like. Again, the remote cause of diseases in general has been stated, as in "formerly too, disease did not arise apart from <s>adharma</s>," and so on. All of that is to be understood by the word "cause."

children.text: tatrādharmakāryatvena vyādhīnāṃ daivavyapāśrayaprāyaścittabalimaṅgaletyādicikitsāsādhyatvaṃ pratīyate rudrakopabhavatvena ca jvarasya mahāprabhāvatvaṃ tathāgneyatvaṃ ca pratīyate krodho hyāgneyaḥ tena tanmayo jvaro'pyāgneyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, because diseases are effects of <s>adharma</s>, it is understood that they are curable by divine-recourse treatments such as expiation, offerings, auspicious rites, and the like. And because fever is produced from the anger of <s>Rudra</s>, both the great power of fever and its fiery nature are understood. For anger is fiery; therefore fever too, being made of that, is fiery.
And likewise there is the statement:

children.text: ūṣmā pittādṛte nāsti jvaro nāstyūṣmaṇā vinā
children.translated_text: "There is no heat apart from <s>pitta</s>; there is no fever without heat.
Therefore one should avoid things incompatible with <s>pitta</s>, and especially so when <s>pitta</s> is predominant."
So it is said.

And through the knowledge that it is produced by <s>vāta</s> and the others, it is understood to be curable by medicines opposite to <s>vāta</s> and the others; and an association with some further disorder of <s>vāta</s> and the others, not yet arisen, is also inferred as future.
And by observing the use of causes such as unsuitable and dry things, a future disease produced by those is inferred.

children.text: vyādhiparīkṣāyāṃ ca saṃdehe jāte yasya vyādher hetusevā dṛśyate sa parikalpyate evamādi hetunā vyādhiparīkṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: In the examination of disease, when doubt has arisen, whichever disease is seen to have had its causal regimen followed is postulated. In this and similar ways there is examination of disease by means of cause.
He explains the particularity of strength and time with the words beginning "strength".

children.text: balasya kālo balakālaḥ tasya viśeṣo vasantapūrvāhṇādir balakālaviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The time of strength is the strength-time; its particular form, such as spring or the forenoon, is the particularity of strength-time.

children.text: ṛtavaścāhorātrāhārayoḥ kālāśca ṛtvahorātrāhārakālāḥ teṣāṃ bhedo vidhiḥ tatra viśeṣeṇa niyato balakālaviśeṣaḥ ṛtvahorātrāhārakālavidhiviniyataḥ tatra ṛtuviniyato balakālaviśeṣo yathā śleṣmajvarasya vasantaḥ ahorātraviniyato yathā śleṣmajvarasya pūrvāhṇaḥ pradoṣaśca āhāraviniyato yathā śleṣmajvarasya bhuktamātrakālaḥ evamādyunneyam ||
children.translated_text: The seasons, and the times of day and night and of food, are the times of season, day-and-night, and food. Their division is the rule. There, the particularity of strength-time is what is specifically determined by the rule of the times of season, day-and-night, and food. Among these, a particular strength-time determined by season is, for example, spring for <s>śleṣma-jvara</s>; one determined by day and night is, for example, the forenoon and evening for <s>śleṣma-jvara</s>; one determined by food is, for example, the time immediately after eating for <s>śleṣma-jvara</s>. Similar cases should be inferred.

children.text: kecit tu vidhiśabdena pūrvakṛtaṃ karma bruvate tatrāpi karmaniyato balakālaviśeṣaḥ pacyamānakarmakāla eva jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some, however, say that by the word "rule" previous <s>karman</s> is meant. In that case too, the particularity of strength-time determined by <s>karman</s> should be understood as just the time when <s>karman</s> is ripening.

children.text: eṣu ca balakāleṣu yadyapi vyādher abhūtaprādurbhāvarūpā saṃprāptirna bhavati tathāpi vyādhisaṃtāne tatkālaṃ vyādhyutpattau saṃprāptir bhinnaiva bhavatīti mantavyam ||
children.translated_text: In these strength-times, although the <s>saṃprāpti</s> consisting in the manifestation of a disease that was previously absent does not occur, still, in the continuity of a disease, when disease arises at that time, the <s>saṃprāpti</s> should be regarded as distinct.

children.text: iyaṃ ca kālaviśeṣaprāptyā balavadvyādhijanikā saṃprāptivyādher viśeṣaṃ sphuṭameva bodhayati ||
children.translated_text: And this <s>saṃprāpti</s>, producing a strong disease by the arrival of a particular time, quite clearly teaches the particular character of the disease.

children.text: yataḥ pūrvāhṇe balasaṃprāptyā jvarasya kaphajatvamunnīyate madhyāhne ca balaprāptyā pittajatvamityādi ||
children.translated_text: For in the forenoon, because of the attainment of strength in the <s>saṃprāpti</s>, fever is inferred to be born from <s>kapha</s>; and at midday, because of the attainment of strength, it is inferred to be born from <s>pitta</s>, and so on.

children.text: iha ca saṃprāptereva viśeṣāḥ saṃkhyādikṛtā uktāḥ na tu nidānādīnāṃ viśeṣāḥ yato nidānādiviśeṣāḥ prativyādhivakṣyamāṇabhedenaivopayuktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, the particularities of <s>saṃprāpti</s> alone, caused by number and the like, have been stated, but not the particularities of cause and the rest, because the particularities of cause and the rest are useful precisely according to the distinctions that will be stated for each disease.

children.text: yato yādṛg jvare nidānaṃ na tādṛg raktapitte ye ca pūrvarūpādiviśeṣā jvare na te raktapittādau kiṃtu bhinnajātīyā eva ||
children.translated_text: For the cause in fever is not of the same kind as that in <s>raktapitta</s>; and the particularities of preliminary signs and the like that occur in fever are not those in <s>raktapitta</s> and the rest, but are of a different class altogether.

children.text: sa ca bhedo nidānādīnāṃ vyādhibhedagamakatvenopayukto vyādhibhedakathana eva vaktavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that difference among cause and the rest, being useful as an indicator of difference among diseases, should be stated only when the difference among diseases is being explained.

children.text: saṃprāptestu saṃkhyādibhedaḥ sarvavyādhiṣvekajātīyatvena na viśeṣagamaka iti ihaiva sarvavyādhinidāne kathyate nidānādiviśeṣāstu prativyādhiviśiṣṭatvena neha prapañcenocyante ||
children.translated_text: But the division of <s>saṃprāpti</s> by number and the like, since it is of one type in all diseases, is not an indicator of a particular disease. Therefore it is explained here itself, in the general account of the causes of all diseases; the particularities of cause and the rest, since they are specific to each disease, are not set forth at length here.

children.text: ata eva cātraivādhyāye saṃprāpteḥ sāmānyābhidhānenaivoktatvāt saṃprāptiṃ parityajya nidānādiviśeṣaṃ pratijānīte tasya nidānapūrvarūpaliṅgopaśayaviśeṣān anuvyākhyāsyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason, since in this chapter the <s>saṃprāpti</s> has been stated only through a general designation, he leaves aside <s>saṃprāpti</s> and announces the particularities of cause and the rest: "We shall further explain its specific cause, preliminary signs, marks, and indications from relief."

children.text: nidāne jñātahetvādipañcakasya cikitsopayogitayā doṣabheṣajādiviśeṣajñānam apekṣitaṃ bhavati ato vakṣyamāṇadoṣabheṣajādiviśeṣajñāpakaṃ vimānasthānaṃ brūte ||
children.translated_text: In the section on causes, when the fivefold set beginning with the known cause has been understood, knowledge of the specific <s>doṣas</s>, medicines, and the like is required because it is useful for treatment. Therefore he sets forth <s>Vimānasthāna</s>, which makes known the specific <s>doṣas</s>, medicines, and so on that are to be discussed.

children.text: tatrāpi ca doṣabheṣajayoḥ prādhānyāt tadviśeṣajñāpakaṃ rasavimānaṃ prathamaṃ brūte ||
children.translated_text: And there too, because <s>doṣa</s> and medicine are primary, he first sets forth <s>Rasavimāna</s>, which makes known their specific character.
He himself will show this connection of the section.

children.text: viśeṣeṇa mīyate jñāyate doṣabheṣajādy aneneti vimānaṃ doṣabheṣajādīnāṃ prabhāvādiviśeṣa ityarthaḥ evaṃbhūtaṃvimānam abhidheyatayā yatra tiṣṭhati tad vimānasthānam ||
children.translated_text: A <s>vimāna</s> is that by which <s>doṣa</s>, medicine, and so forth are particularly measured or known; the meaning is a particularity such as the potency of <s>doṣas</s>, medicines, and the like. The section in which such a <s>vimāna</s> stands as the subject to be explained is <s>Vimānasthāna</s>.
The chapter composed with reference to <s>Rasavimāna</s> is <s>Rasavimāna</s>.
With the words beginning "here indeed" he states the connection of the section.

children.text: iha samprāptibhedasaṃkhyāprādhānyādigrahaṇenaiva samprāptim upadiśan saṃkhyādibhedena sarvaiva samprāptiḥ kathitā bhavatīti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: Here, by the very mention of distinctions of <s>saṃprāpti</s> such as number and predominance, while teaching <s>saṃprāpti</s>, he shows that all <s>saṃprāpti</s> has been explained through distinctions such as number.

children.text: nimittādīnāṃ tu na tādṛśo bhedo 'lpagranthavaktavyo 'sti yena bhedena te 'pīha kathyeran ataste sāmānyenaivoktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in the case of causes and the rest, there is no such distinction that can be stated in a brief text, by which distinction they too would be explained here; therefore they have been stated only in general.
"Having entered into" means "having understood."
<s>Doṣas</s> and the rest have been set forth at length in <s>Sūtrasthāna</s> itself.

children.text: mānamiti prabhāvādiviśeṣaḥ etajjñāne hetum āha doṣādītyādi ||
children.translated_text: "Measure" means a particularity such as potency. He gives the reason for knowing this with the words beginning "doṣa and so on."
"Of action" means "of treatment."
He announces that he will state the meaning of the chapter with the words beginning "there, at the beginning."

children.text: yadyapi ca doṣabheṣajetyādau doṣāpekṣatvād bheṣajasya doṣa ādau kṛtaḥ tathāpīha rasadravyarūpabheṣajasyāpekṣitarogapraśamakartṛtvena tathā doṣasyāpi ca rasadravyayoreva kāraṇatvena bheṣajaśabdasūcite rasadravye evāgre kṛte paścāttu doṣagrahaṇagṛhītau doṣavikārau ||
children.translated_text: Although in the passage beginning '<s>doṣa</s> and medicine,' because medicine depends on <s>doṣa</s>, <s>doṣa</s> was placed first, nevertheless here the medicine in the form of taste and substance is expected to act as the pacifier of disease; and <s>doṣa</s> too has taste and substance as its very causes. Therefore the taste and substance indicated by the word 'medicine' are placed first, while afterwards come <s>doṣa</s> and the disorders of <s>doṣa</s>, included by the mention of <s>doṣa</s>.

children.text: prakṛṣṭo bhāvaḥ prabhāvaḥ śaktirityarthaḥ sa cehācintyaścintyaś ca grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A heightened state is <s>prabhāva</s>, meaning power. Here it should be understood as both inconceivable and conceivable.

children.text: yena tatra khalvanekaraseṣu ityādinā dravyavikārayoḥ prabhāvaṃ rasadvārā doṣadvārā ca cintyamapi vakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: For in the passage beginning 'there, indeed, among substances of many tastes,' he will state the <s>prabhāva</s> of substances and disorders, even when it is conceivable, through taste and through <s>doṣa</s>.
'They maintain' means that they keep them established in equilibrium.
The word 'wrong' here applies to non-application, excessive application, and improper application.
'<s>Doṣas</s>' means the bodily <s>doṣas</s>.
The word 'again' excludes the mental <s>doṣa</s>.
He states the actions of tastes when they are unmixed, with the passage beginning 'there'.

children.text: anena ca rasakarmopadeśena doṣāṇāmapi tattadrasotpādyatvaṃ tathā tattadrasopaśamanīyatvam uktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And by this instruction on the actions of tastes, it is also said that <s>doṣas</s> are produced by particular tastes and likewise pacified by particular tastes.

children.text: kaṭutiktakaṣāyā vātaṃ janayantīti asati paripanthinīti jñeyaṃ tenārkāguruguḍūcyādīnāṃ tiktānāmapi vātājanakatve na doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it is said that pungent, bitter, and astringent tastes produce <s>vāta</s>, it should be understood as applying when there is no opposing factor. Thus there is no fault in the fact that bitter things such as <s>arka</s>, <s>aguru</s>, and <s>guḍūcī</s> do not produce <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: tatra hy uṣṇavīryatā paripanthinī vidyate tena na te vātaṃ janayantītyādy anusaraṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: For in those cases hot potency is present as an opposing factor. Therefore they do not produce <s>vāta</s>; the rest should be followed out in the same way.

children.text: enam iti padena yaśca kaṭvādijo vāyustameva madhurādayaḥ sarvātmavaiparītyād viśeṣeṇa śamayantīti darśayati jāgaraṇādije hi vāyau jāgaraṇādiviparītāḥ svapnādaya eva viśeṣeṇa pathyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the word 'this,' he shows that sweet and the other tastes especially pacify that very <s>vāyu</s> which is produced by pungent and the other tastes, because they are opposite in every respect. For in the case of <s>vāyu</s> produced by wakefulness and the like, sleep and the like, which are opposite to wakefulness and the rest, are especially wholesome.

children.text: evaṃ pittaśleṣmaṇorapi enadenaṃ śabdayos tātparyaṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: In the same way he indicates the purport of the words 'this' and 'this one' also in the cases of <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>.

children.text: atha kayā yuktyā rasā doṣāñjanayanti śamayanti cetyāha rasadoṣetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now he states by what reasoning tastes produce and pacify the <s>doṣas</s>, with the passage beginning 'taste and <s>doṣa</s>'.
'In combination' means in a joining together within the body.

children.text: tuśabdo viśeṣe tena viparītaguṇā eva viśeṣeṇa viparītaguṇabhūyiṣṭhāpekṣayā śamayantīti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: The word 'but' marks a distinction. By it he shows that precisely those things whose qualities are opposite pacify especially, more than things in which opposite qualities merely predominate.

children.text: rasānāṃ tu yathā upācārādguṇā bhavanti tadabhihitaṃ guṇāguṇāśrayā noktāḥ ityādinā sūtre ||
children.translated_text: But in what way qualities are figuratively attributed to tastes has been stated in the sūtra passage beginning 'qualities are not stated as the substrata of qualities'.
'Being habitually used' means not being used only once.

children.text: atha kasmādrasadoṣasaṃsargabhūyastvaṃ parityajya rasaṣaṭtvaṃ doṣatritvaṃ cocyate ityāha ityetadityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now he asks why, setting aside the predominance of combinations of taste and <s>doṣa</s>, the sixfoldness of tastes and the threefoldness of <s>doṣas</s> are stated, with the passage beginning 'this, therefore'.
'Arrangement' means the concise reduction of the elaboration of combinations of taste and <s>doṣa</s>.
The phrase 'mutually unmixed' is also to be connected with 'of the <s>doṣas</s>'.
He states the reason why the detailed elaboration of combinations of taste and <s>doṣa</s> is not taught, with the passage beginning 'combination'.

children.text: yasmāt saṃsargabhedavistaro 'parisaṃkhyeyas tasmāt ṣaṭtvaṃ tritvaṃ cocyate ||
children.translated_text: Because the extension of the distinctions of combinations is innumerable, the sixfoldness and the threefoldness are stated.

children.text: vikalpabhedāparisaṃkhyeyatvād iti saṃsargavikalpasya bhedo vijātīyaprakāraḥ tasyāparisaṃkhyeyatvāt ||
children.translated_text: 'Because the distinctions of alternatives are innumerable' means: the distinction belonging to an alternative of combination is a different kind, and because that is innumerable.

children.text: etena yathā rasānām avāntaravyaktibhede 'pi madhuratvādisāmānyayogān madhurādivyapadeśena ṣaṭtvamucyate tathā madhurāmlamadhuralavaṇādisaṃsargāṇām api satyapyavāntarabhede sāmānyopasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā triṣaṣṭitvasaṃkhyāniyamo bhaviṣyatīti nirasyate yato madhurāmlādisaṃsarge 'pi vijātīyo madhurataramadhuratamādibhedakṛto bhedo 'parisaṃkhyeyo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By this he rejects the following view: just as tastes, even though they have subordinate individual differences, are called sweet and so on because they possess the general character of sweetness and the like, and so are said to be six, in the same way combinations such as sweet-sour and sweet-salty, though they have subordinate differences, may be gathered under general classes and thereby have a fixed number of sixty-three. For even in a sweet-sour combination there is a heterogeneous distinction produced by differences such as sweeter and sweetest, and it is innumerable.

children.text: vacanaṃ hi rasās taratamābhyāṃ tāṃ saṃkhyām atipatanti hi iti ||
children.translated_text: For the statement says, 'Tastes exceed that number by degrees of greater and lesser intensity.'

children.text: atha kathaṃ tarhi saṃsṛṣṭānāṃ rasānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ ca prabhāvo jñeya ityāha tatra khalvityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, how then is the <s>prabhāva</s> of combined tastes and of combined <s>doṣas</s> to be known? He states this with the passage beginning 'there, indeed'.

children.text: tatra cānekarasadravyasyānekadoṣavikārasya ca pratyekarasadoṣaprabhāvamelakena prabhāvaṃ kathayan rasasaṃsargadoṣasaṃsargayor api tādṛśameva prabhāvaṃ kathayati yato rasadoṣasaṃsargaprabhāvāv atra dravyavikārāśrayitvād rasadoṣayor dravyavikāraprabhāvatvenocyete ||
children.translated_text: There, by explaining the <s>prabhāva</s> of a substance with many tastes and of a disorder with many <s>doṣas</s> through the conjunction of the <s>prabhāvas</s> of each individual taste and <s>doṣa</s>, he also explains just such a <s>prabhāva</s> for combinations of tastes and combinations of <s>doṣas</s>. For the <s>prabhāvas</s> of combinations of taste and <s>doṣa</s> here are based on substances and disorders; because tastes and <s>doṣas</s> reside in substances and disorders, they are spoken of as the <s>prabhāvas</s> of substances and disorders.

children.text: anena nyāyena sākṣādanukte'pi ekarasadravyaikadoṣavikārayor api prabhāvo 'saṃsṛṣṭarasadoṣaprabhāvakathanād ukta eva jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this principle, even though they are not directly mentioned, the <s>prabhāva</s> of a one-taste substance and of a one-<s>doṣa</s> disorder should also be understood as already stated, because the <s>prabhāva</s> of unmixed tastes and <s>doṣas</s> has been stated.

children.text: ekaikaśyenābhisamīkṣyeti pratyekam uktarasādiprabhāveṇānekarasaṃ dravyam anekadoṣaṃ ca vikāraṃ samuditaprabhāvam abhisamīkṣya ||
children.translated_text: 'Having examined one by one' means having examined, by means of the previously stated <s>prabhāva</s> of each taste and so forth, a many-tasted substance and a disorder involving many <s>doṣas</s> as possessing a combined <s>prabhāva</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ ca rasadoṣaprabhāvadvārā dravyavikāraprabhāvaniścayo na sarvatra dravye vikāre cetyāha na tv evaṃ khalu sarvatreti ||
children.translated_text: And this determination of the <s>prabhāva</s> of substance and disorder through the <s>prabhāva</s> of taste and <s>doṣa</s> does not apply everywhere in every substance and every disorder. He states this with 'but not in this way everywhere, indeed'.

children.text: atraiva hetum āha na hītyādinādhyavasātuṃ śakyamityantena ||
children.translated_text: He gives the reason for this very point in the passage beginning 'for it is not' and ending 'can be determined'.

children.text: vikṛtiviṣamasamavetānām iti vikṛtisamavetānāṃ tathā viṣamasamavetānāṃ ceti vikṛtiviṣamasamavetānām ||
children.translated_text: 'Conjoined in altered and irregular ways' means conjoined in altered ways and also conjoined in irregular ways; hence 'conjoined in altered and irregular ways'.
'Conjoined' means the tastes and <s>doṣas</s> that are mingled together.

children.text: tatra rasasya vikṛtisamavāyo yathā madhure taṇḍulīyake madhuro hi prakṛtyā snehavṛṣyatvādikaraḥ taṇḍulīyake tu vikṛtisamavetatvena tanna karoti ||
children.translated_text: There, the altered conjunction of a taste is as in sweet <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>. For sweetness by nature produces unctuousness, virility, and the like; but in <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>, because it is conjoined in an altered condition, it does not produce those effects.

children.text: viṣamasamavetāstu tile kaṣāyakaṭutiktamadhurāḥ yadi hīme rasāḥ samayā mātrayā samavetāḥ syustatastilo'pi pittaśleṣmaharastridoṣaharo vā syāt pittakaphakarastvayaṃ tenātra rasānāṃ kvacit kartṛtvam akartṛtvaṃ ca kvaciditi vaiṣamyam unnīyate ||
children.translated_text: But in sesame the astringent, pungent, bitter, and sweet tastes are unevenly combined. For if these tastes were combined in equal measure, then sesame too would remove <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, or would remove all three <s>doṣa</s>s. But this sesame produces <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>. Therefore here an unevenness is inferred: in some cases the tastes have causal agency, and in some cases they do not.
But the three causes beginning with "of those that are manifold in nature" are indicators only of <s>vikṛtisamavāya</s> and <s>viṣamasamavāya</s>.
Therefore, through the statements beginning "because of being manifold in nature," <s>vikṛtisamavāya</s> and <s>viṣamasamavāya</s> occur.

children.text: nānātmakānāmiti nānārūpahetujanitānāṃ tena hetubhedabalādeva rasadoṣayor vikṛto viṣamo vā melako bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Of those that are manifold in nature" means of those produced by causes of various forms. Thus, by the force of difference among causes itself, there is a distorted or uneven conjunction of <s>rasa</s> and <s>doṣa</s>; this is the meaning.
Or else "of those that are manifold in nature" means of various quantities.
And in this way, diversity of quantity is the cause in <s>viṣamasamavāya</s>.
"And injured by one another" means whose qualities have been mutually impaired.

children.text: parasparaguṇopaghātastu yadyapi doṣāṇāṃ prāyo nāstyeva tathāpyadṛṣṭavaśāt kvacid bhavatīti jñeyaṃ rasānāṃ tu prabalenānyopaghāto bhavatyeva ||
children.translated_text: Although mutual impairment of qualities generally does not exist among the <s>doṣa</s>s, still it should be understood that it occurs in some cases through the force of the unseen; among tastes, however, impairment of one by a stronger one certainly occurs.

children.text: anyaiśca vikalpanairiti anyaiśca bhedakaiḥ tatra rasasya bhedakāḥ svarasakalkādayaḥ ekasyaiva hi dravyasya kalpanāviśeṣeṇa guṇāntarāṇi bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: "And by other modifications" means by other differentiating factors. There, the differentiating factors of taste are fresh juice, paste, and the like. For in one and the same substance, other qualities arise because of a special preparation.
But for a <s>doṣa</s>, other <s>dūṣya</s>s themselves become differentiating factors through connection with different qualities.

children.text: yaduktaṃ sa eva kupito doṣaḥ samutthānaviśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: As has been said: "That very <s>doṣa</s>, when aggravated, because of the specific mode of arising,
and also when it has gone to another place, produces many disorders."

children.text: asminvyākhyāne rasānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ ca ya utkarṣāpakarṣakṛto viṣamasamavāyaḥ pṛthagucyate sa na yujyate yato viṣamasamavāye 'pyutkṛṣṭasya rasasya tathā doṣasya cotkṛṣṭā guṇā apakṛṣṭasya cāpakṛṣṭā guṇā bhavantīti kṛtvāvayavaprabhāvān anumānenaiva samudāyaprabhāvānumānaṃ śakyam ||
children.translated_text: In this explanation, the <s>viṣamasamavāya</s> produced by increase and decrease among tastes and <s>doṣa</s>s, which is stated separately, is not reasonable. For even in <s>viṣamasamavāya</s>, the qualities of an increased taste, and likewise of an increased <s>doṣa</s>, are increased, while the qualities of a decreased one are decreased; therefore the effect of the whole can be inferred by inference from the effects of the parts.

children.text: athocyate viṣamamelake rasasya doṣasya ca na ta eva guṇā utkṛṣṭā apakṛṣṭā vā bhavanti kiṃtu guṇāntarameva bhavati hanta tarhi vikṛta evāyaṃ samavāyo visadṛśakāryakāraṇatvāt ||
children.translated_text: If it is said, "In an uneven mixture of <s>rasa</s> and <s>doṣa</s>, those same qualities are not increased or decreased, but rather a different quality arises," well then, this is precisely a distorted conjunction, because the cause and the effect are dissimilar.

children.text: tadevaṃ dūṣaṇadarśanād anyathā vyākhyāyate yad dvividho melako bhavati rasānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ ca prakṛtyanuguṇaḥ prakṛtyananuguṇaśca tatra yo militānāṃ prākṛtaguṇānupamardena melako bhavati sa prakṛtisamasamavāyaśabdenocyate yastu prākṛtaguṇopamardena bhavati sa vikṛtiviṣamasamavāyo 'bhidhīyate vikṛtyā hetubhūtayā viṣamaḥ prakṛtyananuguṇaḥ samavāyo vikṛtiviṣamasamavāya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, because faults have been shown, it is explained differently: there are two kinds of mixture among tastes and <s>doṣa</s>s, one accordant with nature and one not accordant with nature. Of these, the mixture of things that have combined without suppressing their natural qualities is called by the term <s>prakṛtisamasamavāya</s>. But that which occurs through suppression of natural qualities is called <s>vikṛtiviṣamasamavāya</s>. The meaning is: an uneven conjunction, not accordant with nature, because of a distortion that is its cause, is <s>vikṛtiviṣamasamavāya</s>.
In this very <s>vikṛtiviṣamasamavāya</s>, the three causes beginning with being manifold in nature should be connected exactly as already explained.

children.text: ye tu vikṛtiviṣamasamavāyau pṛthag eva kurvanti viṣamasamavāyasya vaiṣamyatāratamyenātibahuprapañcitatvād viṣamāvayavaguṇānumānaṃ duḥśakam iti kṛtvā tadapi dravyavikāraprabhāveṇaiva vyapadiśanti ||
children.translated_text: But those who make <s>vikṛti</s> and <s>viṣamasamavāya</s> separate, because <s>viṣamasamavāya</s> has been elaborated excessively by degrees of unevenness and because inference of the qualities of uneven constituents is difficult, describe that too only through the effect of alteration in the substance.

children.text: atha kathaṃ tarhi vikṛtiviṣamasamavāyaprabhāvajñānam ityāha tathāyukte hītyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, how then is the effect of <s>vikṛtiviṣamasamavāya</s> known? He says this with the passage beginning "for in one so joined."
"In an aggregate so joined" means in <s>vikṛtiviṣamasamavāya</s>.
"The truth of the aggregate's effect" means the truth of the effect of the mixture.

children.text: samadhṛte hi madhusarpiṣi sūryāvartākhye vā doṣasamudaye na saṃyujyamānamadhughṛtaguṇakramāgataṃ mārakatvaṃ na ca vātādidoṣaprabhāvagataṃ sūryavṛddhyā vardhiṣṇutvaṃ sūryāvartasya kiṃ tu saṃyogamahimakṛtam evetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For in honey and ghee held in equal quantities, or in the collection of <s>doṣa</s>s called <s>Sūryāvarta</s>, the fatal property in the former does not come in sequence from the qualities of the honey and ghee being joined, nor in <s>Sūryāvarta</s> does the tendency to increase with the strengthening of the sun come from the effects of <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣa</s>s. Rather, it is caused solely by the power of combination; this is the meaning.

children.text: yacca gatidvayaṃ doṣarasamelakasya tena prakṛtisamasamavāyarūpaṃ saṃnipātaṃ jvaranidāne doṣaliṅgamelakenaivoktavān ||
children.translated_text: And of the two modes of mixture of <s>doṣa</s> and <s>rasa</s>, he stated the <s>saṃnipāta</s> that has the form of <s>prakṛtisamasamavāya</s> in the diagnosis of fever, simply by the combination of the signs of the <s>doṣa</s>s.

children.text: yaduktaṃ pṛthaguktalakṣaṇasaṃsargād dvāṃdvikam anyatamaṃ sāṃnipātikaṃ vā jvaraṃ vidyād iti ||
children.translated_text: As has been said: "From the conjunction of the characteristics stated separately, one should know a fever to be twofold, or involving any one of them, or <s>sāṃnipātika</s>."

children.text: yastu vikṛtiviṣamasamavetastridoṣakṛto jvaras tasya cikitsite kṣaṇe dāhaḥ kṣaṇe śītam ityādinā lakṣaṇam uktam ||
children.translated_text: But the fever produced by the three <s>doṣa</s>s that are combined in <s>vikṛtiviṣamasamavāya</s> has its characteristics stated in the treatment section with "at one moment there is burning, at one moment cold," and so on.

children.text: na hi śyāvaraktakoṭhotpattyādi tatroktaṃ vātādijvare kvacid asti ||
children.translated_text: For the arising of dark-red wheals and the like, stated there, does not occur anywhere in fevers from <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣa</s>s.

children.text: evaṃ rase'pi yatrāmrāte madhuratvaṃ prakṛtisamasamavetaṃ tatrāmrātaṃ madhuram etanmātram evoktaṃ tena madhurasāmānyaguṇāgataṃ tasya vātapittaharatvamapi labhyata eva ||
children.translated_text: So too with taste: where sweetness in <s>āmrāta</s> is combined by <s>prakṛtisamasamavāya</s>, there only this much is said, "<s>āmrāta</s> is sweet." By that, its capacity to remove <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, derived from the general qualities of sweetness, is also obtained.
