children.text: saṃprati karmasaṃprāptikṛtamapi gadaṃ kālaviśeṣavyajyamānatayā darśayannāha nirdiṣṭamityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, while showing that even a disease produced by the attainment of karma becomes manifest through a particular time, he says the words beginning 'specified.'

children.text: kāleneti pacyamānatālakṣitena kālena yuktaṃ sat karma kāraṇaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'By time' means: karma, when joined with time characterized by maturation, becomes a cause. This is the meaning.
He states the rule connecting karma with its result, with the words beginning 'for not.'

children.text: mahaditi viśeṣaṇena kiṃcid amahat karma prāyaścittabādhanīyaphalaṃ na dadātyapi phalamiti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By the qualifier 'great,' he indicates that some karma that is not great, whose result can be blocked by expiation, does not in fact give its result.
He states that diseases born of karma are incurable, with the words beginning 'destroying treatment.'

children.text: tatkṣayāditi karmakṣayāt karmakṣayaśca karmaphalopabhogādeva paraṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: 'Because of its exhaustion' means because of the exhaustion of karma; and the exhaustion of karma occurs only after the experience of the fruit of karma.
He explains the unsuitable contact of sense faculties and objects that has come down in sequence, with the words beginning 'excessively fierce.'
'And not in every way' means because there is not in every respect a hearing of a fierce sound.
'Of tangible things' means of those described in the teaching as tangible, such as anointing and rubbing.
'Beings' are things such as poisonous creatures, worms, and <s>piśācas</s>.

children.text: yo bhūtaviṣavātādīnāṃ saṃsparśaḥ tathākālenāgataḥ snehaśītoṣṇasaṃsparśaśceti yojanā ||
children.translated_text: The construction is: the contact of beings, poison, wind, and so on, and also contact with oiliness, cold, and heat, arriving at an improper time.

children.text: tatrākāle snehasaṃsparśo yathā ajīrṇe kaphavṛddhikāle abhyaṅgasparśaḥ evaṃ śīte śītasparśaḥ uṣṇe coṣṇasparśo 'kālenāgato jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, contact with oiliness at an improper time is, for example, the touch of an anointing when there is indigestion and a time of increased phlegm. In the same way, cold contact in cold conditions and hot contact in hot conditions should be known as arriving at an improper time.

children.text: sarvaśaścāpyadarśanād iti bhāsvatāṃ sūkṣmāṇāṃ ca sarvathādarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: 'And because of non-seeing in every way' means because luminous and subtle things are not seen at all.
'Too close' means near to the eye.

children.text: tāmasānāṃ ca rūpāṇāṃ darśanādvinaśyati dṛṣṭiriti saṃbandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The connection is: sight is destroyed through seeing forms that are dark.
'That is wrong application' means one consisting in seeing hateful, terrifying, and similar things.
And seeing what is excessively subtle should also be understood as wrong application.
With 'habitual suitability and the like,' the connection is: the taking in of what is unsuitable.
And, through the imbalance of habitual suitability and the like, the seven faults beginning with constitution should be understood, apart from the fault of quantity.
'Threefold' means consisting in underuse, overuse, and wrong use.
He shows what an unsuitable object is, with the words beginning 'unsuitable.'
'Together' means combined with the body.

children.text: ātmatām avikṛtarūpatāṃ na yāti etena yad upayuktaṃ prākṛtarūpopaghātakaṃ bhavati tadasātmyam iti ||
children.translated_text: 'It does not become identical with it' means that it does not reach an unaltered condition. By this he says that what, when used, damages the natural state is unsuitable.
Having thus shown that disease born from unsuitable objects is sensory because it has the sense faculties as its gateway, he says the words beginning 'wrong.'
By 'deficient application' here one should understand non-application.
'Sensory' means having the senses as its gateway.
He sums up the cause of painful sensation that has been explained at length, with the words beginning 'of sensations.'
'Unpacified' means painful.
Now, to the question 'What is the cause of pleasant sensation?', he says the words beginning 'pleasant.'
'Balanced application' means the proper conjunction of time, intellect, sense faculties, and sense objects.
'Very difficult to obtain' is said because the proper conjunction of time and the rest is very difficult to obtain, since it is free from non-application and the other faults.

children.text: prāyo hi kālādīnāṃ madhye anyatareṇāpyayogādinā puruṣaḥ sambadhyate tena ca nityāturā eva puruṣā bhavanti alpaṃ ca rogamanādṛtya svasthavyapadeśaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ kriyata iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For generally, among time and the others, a person is connected with non-application or the like through at least one of them; and because of that, persons are always in a condition of illness. The point is that people are called healthy only by disregarding a minor disease.

children.text: saṃprati samyagyogasyopādeyatām ayogādīnāṃ ca heyatāṃ darśayituṃ yogameva caturvidhaṃ kāraṇatvena darśayannāha nendriyāṇītyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, in order to show that proper conjunction is to be adopted and that non-application and the others are to be avoided, he presents conjunction itself, in four forms, as the cause, with the words beginning 'not the sense faculties.'

children.text: nanu kathamindriyārthayoḥ sukhaduḥkhakāraṇatvenopalabhyamānayor apyakāraṇatvam ityāha santītyādi ||
children.translated_text: Objection: how can the sense faculties and their objects, though observed as causes of pleasure and pain, be non-causes? He answers with the words beginning 'there are.'

children.text: yogo na ceti indriyārthayoḥ saṃbandho na ca ||
children.translated_text: 'And there is no conjunction' means that there is no relation between the sense faculties and their objects.
The division is: 'not pleasure.'

children.text: indriyārthayoryogābhāve akāraṇatvena sati tu yoge kāraṇatvena yoga evānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ kāraṇam avadhāryeta iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When there is no conjunction of sense faculties and objects, they are not causes; but when conjunction is present, they are causes. Therefore, by agreement and difference, conjunction itself is determined to be the cause. This is the purport.

children.text: ayaṃ ca yoga indriyārthāvadhikṛtya spaṣṭatvenoktaḥ tena prajñākālayorapi boddhavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And this conjunction has been stated clearly with reference to the sense faculties and objects; therefore it should also be understood with regard to intellect and time.

children.text: etaccendriyamarthaṃ cānupādeyaṃ kṛtvā caturvidhayogasya kāraṇatvaṃ yogānāmeva heyopādeyatvopadarśanārthaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: And the fact that the sense faculty and object are made not worth adopting, while causal status is assigned to the fourfold conjunction, is done in order to show that the conjunctions alone are what should be avoided or adopted.

children.text: paramārthatas tvātmendriyamanobuddhyarthādṛṣṭānyeva tathāyuktāni sukhaduḥkhakāraṇānīti darśayannāha nātmetyādi ||
children.translated_text: But in the highest sense, while showing that the self, sense faculties, mind, intellect, objects, and unseen karma, when joined in that way, are the causes of pleasure and pain, he says the words beginning 'not the self.'
'Field' means the object of a sense faculty.
'Karma' means the unseen factor.

children.text: tatra ātmānaṃ vinā na loṣṭādau sukhaduḥkhe bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, without the self, pleasure and pain do not occur in a clod of earth and the like.
And the fact that sense objects and the like are causes of pleasure and pain is entirely clear.

children.text: karmāpi ca śubhaṃ sukhakāraṇam aśubhaṃ ca duḥkhakāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Karma too: good karma is a cause of pleasure, and bad karma is a cause of pain.

children.text: yadyātmādaya eva kāraṇaṃ tarhi kimarthaṃ kālādyayogātiyogādaya ihocyanta ityāha yathetyādi ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>ātman</s> and the rest alone are the cause, then why are non-use, overuse, and the like of time and so on mentioned here? He answers this with the words beginning "as."

children.text: yad boddhavyaṃ sukhaduḥkhaṃ yathā boddhavyaṃ kāryavaśādbhavati tattathaivocyate nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: The pleasure and pain that is to be understood, in whatever way it is to be understood, occurs according to the force of the operative cause; it is stated in just that way, and not otherwise.

children.text: tena sātmyāsātmyendriyārthajanyatvena sukhaduḥkhe iha pratīyamāne cikitsāyām upayukte bhavataḥ nātmādijanyatveneha sukhaduḥkhe abhidhīyete na hyātmādayo duḥkhahetutayā pratipannā apīha heyatayā pratipādyante kiṃtvasātmyendriyārthayogādaya eva duḥkhahetavastyajyante sukhahetavaḥ sātmyendriyārthayogādayas tūpādīyanta iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, since pleasure and pain are apprehended here as arising from suitable and unsuitable contact between the senses and their objects, and since they are useful in therapy, pleasure and pain are not described here as arising from the <s>ātman</s> and the rest. For although the <s>ātman</s> and the rest are accepted as causes of pain, they are not taught here as things to be abandoned. Rather, unsuitable conjunctions of the senses and their objects and the like, as causes of pain, are abandoned; while suitable conjunctions of the senses and their objects and the like, as causes of pleasure, are adopted. This is the purport.

children.text: idānīṃ sakalakāraṇavyāpakaṃ yogaṃ vyutpādayitum aindriyakaṃ mānasaṃ ca sparśaṃ darśayitum āha sparśanetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, in order to explain the <s>yoga</s> (connection) that pervades all causes, and in order to show both sensory and mental contact, he says the words beginning "by touch."

children.text: sparśanendriyasaṃsparśa ityanenendriyāṇām arthena saṃbandhaṃ sparśanendriyakṛtaṃ darśayati cakṣurādīnyapi spṛṣṭamevārthaṃ jānanti yadi hyaspṛṣṭameva cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ghrāṇaṃ vā gṛhṇāti tadā vidūramapi gṛhṇīyāt na ca gṛhṇāti tasmāt spṛṣṭvaivendriyāṇy arthaṃ pratipadyate mānasastu sparśaścintyādinārthena samaṃ sūkṣmo 'styeva yena manaḥ kiṃcideva cintayati na sarvaṃ tena yanmanasā spṛśyate tadeva mano gṛhṇātīti sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the expression "contact with the tactile sense organ" he shows the relation of the senses with their object as effected by the organ of touch. Even the eye and the other senses know an object only when it has been touched. For if the eye, ear, or nose grasped an object without touching it, then it would grasp even a very distant object; but it does not do so. Therefore the senses apprehend an object only after touching it. But mental contact with an object, such as something thought of, certainly exists in a subtle form, by reason of which the mind thinks of one particular thing and not everything. Thus only what is touched by the mind is grasped by the mind. This is the established position.
He states the sequence in which pleasure and pain arise with the words beginning "desire."

children.text: sukhādicchārūpā tṛṣṇā duḥkhācca dveṣarūpā tṛṣṇā pravartate ||
children.translated_text: From pleasure there proceeds craving in the form of desire, and from pain craving in the form of aversion.

children.text: iyaṃ cotpannā tṛṣṇā īpsite'rthe pravartayantī dviṣṭe ca nivartayantī pravṛttinivṛttiviṣayasya sukhaduḥkhahetutāmapekṣya sukhaduḥkhe janayatīti vākyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This craving, once arisen, impels one toward a desired object and turns one away from a hated one; and, depending on the fact that the object of activity or cessation is a cause of pleasure or pain, it produces pleasure and pain. This is the meaning of the sentence.

children.text: yathoktaṃ tṛṣṇāyāḥ sukhaduḥkhahetutvaṃ darśayannāha upādatte hītyādi ||
children.translated_text: Showing the previously stated fact that craving is a cause of pleasure and pain, he says the words beginning "for one takes up."
"Known as supports of sensation" means those mentioned as causes of sensation, in the form of non-use and the like of time and so on.

children.text: atha tṛṣṇā cet sukhaduḥkhakāraṇaṃ tat kim indriyārthenāpareṇa kāraṇenetyāha spṛśyata ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, if craving is the cause of pleasure and pain, what need is there for a sense object or another cause? He answers this with the words beginning "is touched."

children.text: anupādāna iti avidyamānārtharūpe sparśakāraṇe arthaṃ vinā nārthasya sparśo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: "When there is no appropriation" means when the cause of contact, in the form of an existing object, is absent; without an object, there is no contact with an object.

children.text: atha na bhavatvarthasparśaḥ tataḥ kimityāha nāspṛṣṭo vetti vedanā iti arthasparśaśūnyaḥ san na sukhaduḥkhe anutpannatvādeva vettītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, let there be no contact with an object; what follows from that? He says, "one who has not touched does not know sensation," meaning that one who is without contact with an object does not know pleasure and pain, precisely because they have not arisen.

children.text: vedanānāṃ kim adhiṣṭhānam ityasyottaram āha vedanānām ityādi ||
children.translated_text: He gives the answer to the question, "What is the substratum of sensations?" with the words beginning "of sensations."

children.text: dehaḥ sendriya iti anena nirindriyo dehaḥ keśalomādiko nirastaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By saying "the body together with the senses," he excludes a body without senses, such as hair and body hair.
He explains that very point, whose meaning is clear, with the words beginning "hair."
Or else, to indicate their primacy, the senses too are mentioned separately by the mention of the senses as supports of sensation.
The fact that sensation belongs to the body and the senses should be understood because it is apprehended as having them as its support.
"Fluid" means urine.
"Qualities" means sound and the rest.

children.text: śarīragatā ete hi keśādayo na vedanādhārā ityanubhava eva pramāṇam ||
children.translated_text: For these, hair and the like, though located in the body, are not supports of sensation; direct experience itself is the proof.

children.text: yā tu mūtrapurīṣagatā vedanā grahaṇīmūtrakṛcchrādau vaktavyā sā mūtrapurīṣādhāraśarīrapradeśasyaiva bodhyā ||
children.translated_text: But the sensation located in urine and feces, which is to be discussed in conditions such as <s>grahaṇī</s> and dysuria, should be understood as belonging to that bodily region which is the support of urine and feces.

children.text: kva caitā vedanāḥ sarvā ityādipraśnasyottaraṃ yoga ityādi ||
children.translated_text: The answer to the question beginning "And where are all these sensations?" is given with the words beginning "in yoga."
"<s>Yoga</s>" is what will be stated in the passage beginning "because of non-undertaking."
"<s>Mokṣa</s>" is the absolute cessation of the body and the rest.
"Without remainder" means that it does not arise again.

children.text: etena yoge nivṛttā vedanā punar bhavatīti sūcayati ||
children.translated_text: By this he indicates that sensation that has ceased in <s>yoga</s> arises again.
"Leading to <s>mokṣa</s>" means being a cause of <s>mokṣa</s>.

children.text: kiṃvā sayogamokṣau nivartakau iti pāṭhaḥ tadā asmin pakṣe yadyapi yogamokṣayorvedanānivartakatvaṃ yoge mokṣe ca ityādinā ślokārdhenoktaṃ tathāpi yogamokṣayoriha kartṛtā vedanānivṛttiṃ prati dṛśyata iti na paunaruktyam ||
children.translated_text: Or else the reading is "<s>yoga</s> and <s>mokṣa</s> are the removers." In that interpretation, although the removal of sensations by <s>yoga</s> and <s>mokṣa</s> has already been stated by the half verse beginning "in yoga and in mokṣa," still, agency with respect to the cessation of sensations is seen here in <s>yoga</s> and <s>mokṣa</s>; therefore there is no repetition.

children.text: yathā yogo vedanānivartako bhavati yaśca yogastenāha ātmetyādi ||
children.translated_text: He says, with the words beginning "the self," how <s>yoga</s> becomes a remover of sensation, and what that <s>yoga</s> is.
"Because of non-undertaking" means because the mind does not undertake anything for the sake of appropriating objects.
"When the mind is fixed in the self" means when it has withdrawn from objects and is fixed in knowledge of the self alone.

children.text: sthire iti acale ātmajñānaprasakta eveti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: "Steady" means unmoving, that is, engaged solely in knowledge of the self.
"Both of those" means pleasure and pain.
In regard to <s>yoga</s>, he states the attainment of another property of <s>yoga</s> with the words beginning "mastery."
"Mastery" is the eightfold power of sovereignty that will be described.

children.text: saśarīrasyetipadena śarīreṇa sahaiva vaśitvaṃ bhavatīti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By the phrase "of one who is embodied," he shows that mastery occurs together with the body itself.
He says the words beginning "entry."
"Entry" means entering another body.
"Knowledge of the mind" means knowledge of another's thought.
"Action upon objects at will" means the making of objects according to one's desire.
"Sight" means supersensory seeing.
"Hearing" means supersensory hearing.
<s>Smṛti</s> (memory) is recollection of the true nature of all entities.
<s>Kānti</s> (radiance) is superhuman radiance.

children.text: iṣṭataścāpyadarśanamiti yadecchati tadā darśanayogya eva na dṛśyate yadā cecchati tadā dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: And "non-appearance at will" means: when he wishes, although he is fit to be seen, he is not seen; and when he wishes, he is seen.

children.text: kiṃvā āveśaścetasa iti paracetasaḥ praveśaḥ jñānamiti sarvam atītānāgatādijñānaṃ śeṣaṃ pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Or, "possession of the mind" means entrance into another's mind; "knowledge" means knowledge of everything past, future, and so on. The rest is as before.
"Divine" means produced by lordly power attained through the efficacy of yoga.
"From the concentration of pure <s>sattva</s>" means from the proper placing of the mind, free from <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, in the <s>ātman</s>.

children.text: atha kathaṃ mokṣo bhavati kaścetyāha mokṣa ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now he states how <s>mokṣa</s> occurs and what it is, with the words beginning "<s>mokṣa</s>".
"From the exhaustion of powerful karma" means from the destruction of karma whose fruit must necessarily be experienced.
"From all connections" means from all things connected with the <s>ātman</s>, such as body, intellect, ego, and the rest.
Because there is no further connection with body and the rest, it is called non-rebirth.
In connection with this topic he states the means to <s>mokṣa</s>, with the words beginning "of the good".
"Supreme firmness" means an exceptional restraint of the mind.
"Non-undertaking of actions" means not performing the instruments of future <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.

children.text: kṛtānāṃ ca parikṣaya iti janmāntaraiḥ kṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalopabhogāt parikṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "And the exhaustion of those already done" means the exhaustion, through the experience of their fruits, of actions done in former births.
<s>Naiṣkramya</s> is the wish to depart from <s>saṃsāra</s>.
"Absence of egoity" means the abandonment of notions such as "this is mine" and "I do this".
"Connection" means connection of the <s>ātman</s> with the body and the rest.
"Concentration of mind and intellect" means the concentration of mind and intellect in the <s>ātman</s>.
"All this" means what has been stated, beginning with "non-undertaking of actions".

children.text: tattvasmṛtiḥ ātmādīnāṃ yathā bhūtānusmaraṇaṃ sā ca nātmā śarīrādyupakāryaḥ śarīrādayaścāmī ātmavyatiriktāḥ ityādismaraṇarūpasmṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tattvasmṛti</s> (recollection of reality) is recollection of the <s>ātman</s> and the rest as they truly are. It is memory in the form of recollection such as: the <s>ātman</s> is not something to be served by the body and the rest, and these body and other things are distinct from the <s>ātman</s>.

children.text: atha smṛtiḥ kathaṃ duḥkhapramoṣe kāraṇamityāha smṛtvetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, how is memory a cause in the removal of suffering? He answers with the words beginning "having remembered".
"Its own nature" means the form fixed for each self.

children.text: guruvacanāddhi prathamapratipannam ātmādīnāṃ rūpaṃ parasparabhinnaṃ parasparānupakārakatvena vyavasthitaṃ smaran na kvacidapi pravartate apravartamānaśca na duḥkhena pravṛttijanyena yujyata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For, remembering the nature of the <s>ātman</s> and the rest, first learned from the teacher's word, as mutually distinct and established as not assisting one another, he does not proceed into action anywhere; and not proceeding into action, he is not joined with the suffering produced by activity. This is the meaning.
Now, in connection with the topic of memory, he states the causes of memory, with the words beginning "they will be stated".

children.text: nimittagrahaṇaṃ kāraṇajñānaṃ kāraṇaṃ hi dṛṣṭvā kāryaṃ smarati ||
children.translated_text: "Grasping the occasion" means knowledge of the cause; for, after seeing a cause, one remembers the effect.
"Grasping the form" means grasping the shape.

children.text: yathā vane gavayaṃ dṛṣṭvā gāṃ smarati ||
children.translated_text: For example, after seeing a <s>gavaya</s> in the forest, one remembers a cow.

children.text: sādṛśyād yathā pituḥ sadṛśaṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitaraṃ smarati ||
children.translated_text: "From resemblance" means, for example, after seeing a man resembling one's father, one remembers one's father.

children.text: saviparyayāditi atyarthavaisādṛśyādapi smaraṇaṃ bhavati yathā atyarthakurūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā pratiyoginamatyarthasurūpaṃ smarati ||
children.translated_text: "With its opposite" means that recollection also arises from extreme dissimilarity; for example, after seeing someone extremely ugly, one remembers the opposing case, someone extremely handsome.

children.text: sattvānubandhāditi manasaḥ praṇidhānāt smartavyasmaraṇāya praṇihitamanāḥ smartavyaṃ smarati ||
children.translated_text: "From attachment of <s>sattva</s>" means from mental attention; one whose mind is directed toward remembering what is to be remembered remembers that thing.
"From practice" means that one remembers a practiced object through the very force of practice.

children.text: jñānayogād iti tattvajñānayogāt upajātatattvajñāno hi tadbalādeva sarvaṃ smarati ||
children.translated_text: "From connection with knowledge" means from connection with knowledge of reality; for one in whom knowledge of reality has arisen remembers everything by that very power.

children.text: punaḥ śrutāditi śruto'pyartho vismṛtaḥ punar ekadeśaṃ śrutvā smaryate ||
children.translated_text: "From hearing again" means that an object once heard but forgotten is remembered after one hears a part of it again.
Having described the cause of memory, he states the form of memory with the words beginning "seen".

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ pratyakṣopalakṣaṇaṃ śrutaṃ tvāgamapratītaṃ tena sarvapūrvānubhūtāvarodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Seen" denotes what is apprehended by perception, while "heard" denotes what is known from authoritative tradition; by these, everything previously experienced is included.

children.text: kvacit smaraṇaṃ smṛtirucyate iti pāṭhaḥ tatrāpi nārthabhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In some places the reading is "recollection is called memory"; there too there is no difference in meaning.

children.text: evaṃ smṛtiṃ sāmānyena pratipādya tattvasmṛter mokṣasādhakatvaṃ darśayannāha etadityādi ||
children.translated_text: Having thus explained memory in general, he shows that recollection of reality is a means to <s>mokṣa</s>, with the words beginning "this".
"The one path" means the highest path.

children.text: muktairiti jīvanmuktairiti jñeyaṃ sarvathāmuktānāṃ śarīrābhāve nopadarśakatvābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: By "the liberated" one should understand those liberated while alive, since those liberated in every respect have no body and therefore no capacity to point it out.

children.text: tattvasmṛtibalamiti tattvasmṛtirūpaṃ balaṃ kiṃvā tattvasmṛtirbalaṃ yatra mokṣasādhanamārge tattattvasmṛtibalam ||
children.translated_text: "The strength of recollection of reality" means the strength consisting in recollection of reality; or, recollection of reality is strength wherever, on the path that is the means to <s>mokṣa</s>, there is that strength of recollection of reality.
"By which" means in whatever way.
"Gone" means gone to <s>mokṣa</s>.

children.text: na punarāgatā iti muktiṃ yātā na punarāgacchanti ||
children.translated_text: "They did not return again" means: having gone to liberation, they do not come back again.

children.text: idānīṃ saṃkṣepeṇa saṃsārahetumajñānaṃ tathā mokṣahetuṃ ca samyagjñānaṃ darśayannāha sarvamityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, briefly showing ignorance as the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> and right knowledge as the cause of <s>mokṣa</s>, he speaks with the words beginning "all".
"Everything has a cause" means everything that comes into being, such as intellect, ego, body, and the rest.
"Suffering" means precisely a cause of suffering.

children.text: asvam iti sarvaṃ kāraṇavad evātmavyatiriktaṃ paramārthataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Not one's own" means that everything that has a cause is in truth distinct from the <s>ātman</s>.

children.text: na cātmakṛtakam iti na cātmanodāsīnena kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: "And not made by the <s>ātman</s>" means not made by the <s>ātman</s>, which is indifferent.
"There" means in what has a cause, such as intellect and body.
"Ownness" means possessiveness in the form "this intellect is mine" and the like.

children.text: atha kiyantaṃ kālamiyaṃ bhrāntyā yutotpadyate ityāha yāvad ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, for how long does this arise joined with delusion? He answers with the words beginning "as long as".
"True understanding" means right knowledge.
"By which true understanding" means by that true understanding.

children.text: naitad buddhyādyahaṃ kiṃtu bhinna evāhaṃ tathā naitad buddhyādi mama kiṃtu prakṛteḥ prapañca iti vijñāya ||
children.translated_text: Having known, "this intellect and the rest are not I; rather, I am distinct. Likewise, this intellect and the rest are not mine; rather, they are an expansion of <s>prakṛti</s>,"
"The knower" means one who possesses direct realization of reality.

children.text: sarvam ativartata iti sarvaṃ buddhyādi tyajati ||
children.translated_text: "He transcends all" means he abandons everything, intellect and the rest.
"Final renunciation" means the renunciation of all action that is to occur afterward.

children.text: prathamaṃ hi mokṣopayogitvena guruvacanāt kriyāsaṃnyāsaḥ kṛta eva paraṃ svānubhavaviraktena na kṛtaḥ abhyāsād udbhūtena jñānena sākṣāddṛṣṭaṃ bhāvasvabhāvena yaḥ sarvasaṃnyāsaḥ kriyate tatra samūlāḥ sarvavedanā jñānādayaśca śarīroparamādevoparamante ||
children.translated_text: For at first, because it is useful for <s>mokṣa</s>, renunciation of acts is indeed performed on the teacher's instruction; but it is not performed by one who is dispassionate through his own experience. In that case, when, through knowledge arisen from practice, one directly sees the nature of reality, there is a renunciation of everything; then all sensations, along with knowledge and the rest, cease from the cessation of the body itself, together with their roots.

children.text: samūlā iti sakāraṇāḥ kāraṇaṃ ca buddhyādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Together with their roots" means together with their causes; and the causes are intellect and the rest.

children.text: saṃjñā ālocanaṃ nirvikalpakaṃ jñānaṃ savikalpakaṃ vijñānaṃ buddhyavasāyaḥ kiṃvā saṃjñā mānollekhena jñānaṃ vijñānaṃ śāstrajñānam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃjñā</s> is apprehension, <s>jñāna</s> is indeterminate cognition, <s>vijñāna</s> is determinate cognition, and <s>buddhi</s> is ascertainment. Or else <s>saṃjñā</s> is cognition involving the marking out of measure, and <s>vijñāna</s> is knowledge of scripture.

children.text: tattvajñānamapi hi mokṣaṃ janayitvā nivartata eva kāraṇābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: For even knowledge of reality, after producing <s>mokṣa</s>, itself ceases, because its cause is absent.
The answer to the question beginning "the knower of all" is the passage beginning "after this."
"Become <s>brahman</s>" means devoid of <s>prakṛti</s> and the rest.

children.text: cihnaṃ yasya na vidyate ityanena muktātmanaḥ prāṇāpānādyātmaliṅgābhāvād gamakaṃ cihnaṃ nāstyeveti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By the phrase "whose sign does not exist," he shows that, because signs of the self such as <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> are absent in the liberated self, there is no identifying mark at all.
Because it does not flow away, that is, does not go into another state, it is "imperishable".
That whose characteristic does not exist is "without characteristic".
He shows that this very <s>mokṣa</s> is unknowable to other persons with the words beginning "knowledge."

children.text: brahmavidāmevātra manaḥ pratyeti nājñānām ahaṅkārādivāsanāgṛhītānām ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here only the mind of those who know <s>brahman</s> reaches it, not that of ignorant people possessed by latent impressions such as egoity: this is the meaning.

children.text: pūrvādhyāye śarīrasyādisarga ādhyātmiko naiṣṭhikamokṣarūpacikitsopayukta uktaḥ saṃprati garbhādirūpaṃ sargam abhidhātum atulyagotrīyo 'bhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: In the preceding chapter, the original creation of the body, pertaining to the self and useful for treatment in the form of absolute <s>mokṣa</s>, was stated. Now, in order to state creation in the form of the embryo and so on, the section beginning "one of unlike lineage" is explained.
"Conforming to the cause" means similar to the cause.
He clarifies that very point: "imitating the object of the cause."

children.text: nimittasya yo'rthaḥ kāryajananarūpaḥ kāryabodhanarūpo vā tamanukarotīti nimittārthānukāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: It imitates the object of the cause, namely the object that has the form either of producing an effect or of indicating an effect; therefore it is "imitating the object of the cause."

children.text: riṣṭākhyā hi vikṛtirmaraṇe tasyaivāvabodhane vā nimittaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For a morbid alteration called <s>riṣṭa</s> becomes the cause either in relation to death itself or in relation to the indication of that death.
He states a further particularity of a morbid alteration that conforms to its cause with the words beginning "that."

children.text: animittāmiti tadātve'nupalabhyamānanimittāṃ na tu punaḥ sarvathaivāhetukīṃ yata āyuṣaḥ kṣayanimittām ityanantaramasya viśeṣaṇaṃ kathayiṣyati riṣṭasya hi na raukṣyādinā śarīrasaṃbandhādi nimittam upalabhyate ||
children.translated_text: "Without a cause" means one whose cause is not perceived at that time; it does not mean one that is altogether without a cause, since immediately afterward he will state its qualification as "caused by the waning of life span." For in the case of <s>riṣṭa</s>, no cause is perceived such as bodily connection through dryness and the like.

children.text: yadvā āyuḥkṣayarūpaṃ yannimittaṃ tadvidyamānamapi nānyairupalabhyate kiṃtu tadeva hi riṣṭādunnīyate tena avyaktanimittatvam ihānimittatvaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Or else, even when the cause, namely the waning of life span, exists, it is not perceived by others; rather, that very cause is inferred from the <s>riṣṭa</s>. Therefore here "causelessness" should be understood as having an unmanifest cause.
Here the condition of having one's life span gone is properly the pervasive cause of every <s>riṣṭa</s> that rests in a person.
But as for what he will say, "When the <s>doṣa</s>s have passed beyond the path of treatment and rest only in the body,"

children.text: cihnaṃ kurvanti yaddoṣās tadariṣṭaṃ pracakṣate iti taddūtādigatariṣṭāvyāpakatayā puruṣāśrayiriṣṭamātrābhiprāyeṇa jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: "the sign that they produce is called <s>ariṣṭa</s>": that should be understood as intended only with reference to <s>riṣṭa</s> resting in a person, because it does not extend to <s>riṣṭa</s> occurring in messengers and the like.
"Of the knowledge of the measure of life" means of the knowledge of the measure of remaining life span.
"Abundantly" means exceedingly.
Therefore it means a morbid alteration that is caused by extreme waning of life span, that is, produced by an immediately impending waning of life span.
"Which" means whose effect belongs to one whose life span is exhausted.

children.text: pretaliṅgānurūpām iti pretasadṛśīṃ malā danteṣu jāyante pretākṛtir udīryate ityādigranthavakṣyamāṇām ||
children.translated_text: "Conforming to the signs of a dead person" means similar to a dead person, as in the passage to be stated later, "impurities arise on the teeth; the form of a dead person appears," and so on.
For they state this morbid alteration in order to know the remaining portion of life span.

children.text: yā tvanyā pretaliṅgānanurūpā varṇāśrayā sā pratyāsannamaraṇabodhikā tena sā nātyarthaṃ nātyarthakṣīṇāyuḥkāryetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But another morbid alteration, based on complexion, which does not conform to the signs of a dead person, indicates imminent death; therefore it is not "exceedingly," that is, it is not the effect of an extremely exhausted life span: this is the meaning.

children.text: evaṃ bhūyaśca ityādinā dhīrāḥ ityantena nimittānurūpavikṛtiviśeṣasya kāryaviśeṣaṃ maraṇalakṣaṇam abhidhāya punaḥ sāmānyenānimittāyā dharmāntaramāha yām adhikṛtyetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Thus, with the passage beginning "and abundantly" and ending with "the wise," he has stated the particular effect, marked by death, of the special morbid alteration that conforms to its cause. Then, in general, he states another property of one that is without an apparent cause, with the words beginning "with reference to which."

children.text: puruṣasaṃśrayāṇīti viśeṣaṇena puruṣānāśritadūtādiriṣṭe nāvaśyam animittatāstīti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By the qualification "resting in persons," he shows that in <s>riṣṭa</s> resting in messengers and the like, which do not rest in persons, causelessness is not necessary.

children.text: yato dūtādhikārādau yāni riṣṭāni tāni dṛśyamānanimittāny apy āgamādeva riṣṭatvenāvadhāryante ||
children.translated_text: For in the section on messengers and so forth, those <s>riṣṭa</s>s, even though they have visible causes, are determined to be <s>riṣṭa</s> only from authoritative teaching.
For example: "If, with hair disheveled, or naked, weeping, or impure,
a messenger is seen approaching the physician, he should declare death,"
so it is said.

children.text: atra ca bhiṣajo muktakeśavacanād dṛśyata eva kāraṇaṃ tathā dūtāgamane cāturasya preraṇādi kāraṇamastyeva tenānimittatvam āturāśrayiriṣṭa eva ||
children.translated_text: And here, because of the statement about disheveled hair, the cause is plainly visible to the physician; likewise, in the arrival of a messenger, there certainly is a cause, such as being sent by the patient. Therefore causelessness applies only to <s>riṣṭa</s> resting in the patient.

children.text: anye tu evaṃbhūtavaidyadūtasamāgamaḥ parihartavyatvena jñātaḥ san yadā daivādbhavati tadā daivanimittaḥ san riṣṭaṃ bhavati tena sarvariṣṭavyāpikaiveyam animittatā bhūyaścetyādigranthena tu pretaliṅgānurūpāṃ vikṛtiṃ bhūya āyuṣo'ntargatasya jñānārtham upadiśanti tathā puruṣasaṃśrayāṇi bhūya upadekṣyante puruṣā nāśrayāṇi tu svalpagranthenopadekṣyante iti vyākhyānayanti ||
children.translated_text: Others, however, explain it thus: when the meeting of such a physician and messenger is known as something to be avoided, yet occurs by fate, then, being caused by fate, it becomes a <s>riṣṭa</s>. Therefore this causelessness is indeed pervasive of all <s>riṣṭa</s>s. By the passage beginning "and abundantly," they teach, for the sake of knowing the remaining part of life span, a morbid alteration conforming to the signs of a dead person; likewise, <s>riṣṭa</s>s resting in persons will be taught more extensively, while those not resting in persons will be taught in a brief text.
"Thus the summary" means the summary of the meaning of the <s>Indriyasthāna</s>.

children.text: pūrvasthānoktalakṣaṇābhāvenāvadhāritāyuṣmadbhāvena cikitsā dharmārthayaśaskarī kartavyetyanantaraṃ cikitsābhidhāyakaṃ sthānam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Since the fact that the patient possesses life has been determined by the absence of the signs described in the preceding section, treatment, which produces <s>dharma</s> (religious merit), wealth, and fame, should be undertaken. Immediately after that, the section that explains treatment is stated.

children.text: rasāyanavājīkaraṇasādhanamapi yathā cikitsocyate tathānantaram eva vakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will state immediately afterward how the means for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy) and <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> (virilification therapy) are also called treatment.
And among these, before the treatment of fever and the like, <s>rasāyana</s> and <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> are taught at the beginning because their results are very great.

children.text: tayorapi ca rasāyanameva varṣasahasrāyuṣṭvādikāraṇatayā mahāphalam iti tad abhidhīyate tatrāpi cābhayāmalakīyaś cikitsāsthānārthasūtrābhidhāyakatayāgre 'bhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Of those two also, <s>rasāyana</s> itself has the greater result, since it is the cause of a thousand-year lifespan and the like; therefore it is explained. And within that too, the <s>Abhayāmalakīya</s> is explained first, because it states the guiding meaning of the Cikitsāsthāna.

children.text: tatrādau vyavahārārthaṃ sthānābhidheyasya bheṣajasya paryāyānāha cikitsitam ityādi ||
children.translated_text: There, at the outset, for the sake of practical usage, he states the synonyms of the medicine that is the subject matter of the section, with the words beginning 'treated' (<s>cikitsitam</s>).
And thus at the beginning he states the synonyms of the principal subject, just as in the Nidāna section he stated synonyms such as cause and form.

children.text: etacca paryāyābhidhānaṃ prādhānyena catuṣpādasyaiva bheṣajasya yaduktaṃ catuṣpādaṃ ṣoḍaśakalaṃ bheṣajamiti bhiṣajo bhāṣante iti ||
children.translated_text: This statement of synonyms applies chiefly to medicine with its four supports, as it is said: 'Physicians call medicine four-footed and sixteen-part.'

children.text: evaṃbhūtabheṣajāṅgarūpatayā tu sthāvarajaṅgamadravyarūpasya bheṣajasya bheṣajatvamevāntaravyavahārakṛtaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: But the status of medicine belonging to remedies in the form of plant and animal substances should be understood as arising from secondary practical usage, since they are limbs of medicine of this kind.
'Expiation' is a designation for medicine, because, like expiation, medicine removes disease, which is the effect of unrighteousness.
He explains its twofold division with the words beginning 'for the healthy.'
'Some' means not all.

children.text: svasthatvena vyavahriyamāṇasya puṃso jarādisvābhāvikavyādhiharatvena tathāpraharṣavyayāyakṣayitvānucitaśukratvādyapraśastaśārīrabhāvaharatvena ūrjaḥ praśastaṃ bhāvam ādadhātīti svasthasyorjaskaram ||
children.translated_text: For a person who is conventionally spoken of as healthy, it removes natural diseases such as old age, and likewise removes undesirable bodily states such as lack of delight, exhaustion through sexual activity, wasting, and defective semen; because it establishes a praiseworthy condition of vigor, it is called 'promoting strength for the healthy.'
By the qualifier 'removing disease for the afflicted,' it means that it removes fever and the like for one afflicted by fever and similar diseases.

children.text: roganud iti vacanenaivārtaviśeṣitāyāṃ labdhāyāṃ yad ārtasya iti karoti tena sahajajarādikṛtāṃ pīḍām anudvejikāṃ parityajya jvarādināsvābhāvikena rogeṇa pīḍitasyeti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: Although the afflicted person is already implied by the expression 'removing disease,' he adds 'of the afflicted.' By this he shows that, setting aside the non-distressing discomfort caused by inborn old age and the like, it concerns one afflicted by an unnatural disease such as fever.
In connection with medicine, he states the twofold division of what is not medicine, with the words beginning 'non-medicine.'
'Harmful' here means harmful only for the moment, as a small amount of something unsuitable is.
'Accompanied by subsequent harm' means producing disorders such as skin disease that remain for a long time.
He divides the twofold medicine that has been stated, with the words beginning 'for the healthy.'
The division should be made as: 'that is generally <s>vṛṣya</s> (virility-promoting); that is <s>rasāyana</s>.'

children.text: yadvṛṣyaṃ prāyo bhavati tathā rasāyanaṃ yat prāyo bhavati ārtasya rogaharaṃ yadbāhulyena tat svasthorjaskaram ucyate yattu dvitīyam ārtarogaharaṃ tat prāyeṇa jvarādiśamanaṃ rasāyanaṃ vājīkaraṇaṃ ca bhavati yathākṣatakṣīṇoktaṃ sarpirguḍādi rasāyanaṃ vṛṣyaṃ ca bhavati tathā pāṇḍurogokto yogarājo rasāyanatvenoktaḥ tathā kāsādhikāre 'gastyaharītakī rasāyanatvenoktetyādy anusaraṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: That which is generally <s>vṛṣya</s>, and likewise that which is generally <s>rasāyana</s>, is called strength-promoting for the healthy when it is mostly disease-removing for the afflicted. But the second kind, which removes the diseases of the afflicted, is generally pacifying of fever and the like, and may also be <s>rasāyana</s> and <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>. For example, ghee, jaggery, and similar remedies mentioned for wasting from chest injury are both <s>rasāyana</s> and <s>vṛṣya</s>; likewise the Yogarāja recipe taught for anemia is described as <s>rasāyana</s>; and <s>Agastyaharītakī</s> in the section on cough is described as <s>rasāyana</s>. This and similar cases should be followed.

children.text: rasāyanoktānāṃ ca jvarādiharatvam atra suvyaktam eva rasāyanagrantheṣu ||
children.translated_text: And the fever-removing and similar action of the substances taught as <s>rasāyana</s> is quite explicit here in the texts on <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: anye tu bruvate yad vyādhimātraharaṃ na tad rasāyanaṃ kiṃtu śarīrasaṃyogadārḍhyād dīrghāyuḥkartṛtvasādhāraṇadharmayogād upacaritavyādhiharaṃ rasāyanam ihocyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Others, however, say that what removes only disease is not <s>rasāyana</s>. Rather, because it shares the property of producing long life through firmness of bodily conjunction, a <s>rasāyana</s> is here figuratively called disease-removing.

children.text: nanu yadi svasthorjaskaramapi vyādhiharaṃ vyādhiharaṃ ca svasthorjaskaraṃ tatkiṃ kiṃciditi padena bheṣajakarmavyavasthādarśakena kriyate brūmaḥ bāhulyena svasthorjaskaratvaṃ vyādhiharatvaṃ ca vyavasthāpyate na ceha sarvārtarogaharasya svasthorjaskaratvamiti pratijñāyate yena pāṭhāsaptaparṇādīnām api rasāyanatvaṃ sādhanīyaśaktitvād ārtarogaharatvena yaducyate tadapi rasāyanaṃ vājīkaraṇaṃ ca bhavatīti lavamātropadarśanaṃ kriyate tat svasthārtayor ubhayārthakartṛtvam ||
children.translated_text: Objection: if what promotes strength for the healthy also removes disease, and what removes disease also promotes strength for the healthy, what purpose is served by the word 'some,' which shows the distinction among the actions of medicine? We reply: strength-promotion for the healthy and disease-removal are distinguished according to predominance. It is not asserted here that every disease-remover for the afflicted promotes strength for the healthy, so that substances such as <s>pāṭhā</s> and <s>saptaparṇa</s> would also have to be proved to be <s>rasāyana</s>. When it is said that, because they possess the power to accomplish it, even disease-removing remedies for the afflicted may also be <s>rasāyana</s> and <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>, only a small indication is being made of their ability to serve both purposes, for the healthy and for the afflicted.
He explains the purport of the word 'generally' with the words beginning 'generally.'
'For the sake of distinction' means 'for the sake of predominance.'
He states the function of <s>rasāyana</s> with the words beginning 'long.'
The excellence of the three beginning with radiance is to be construed.

children.text: vāksiddhiḥ yad ucyate tad avaśyaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Fulfillment of speech' means that whatever is said necessarily comes to pass.
'Reverence' means being honored by people.

children.text: katham etad rasāyanena kriyata ityāha lābhetyādi rasādigrahaṇena smṛtyādayo 'pi gṛhyante ||
children.translated_text: To the question 'How is this produced by <s>rasāyana</s>?', he answers with the words beginning 'through obtaining.' By the mention of taste and the rest, memory and similar qualities are also included.
He states the function of <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> with the words beginning 'progeny.'

children.text: apatyasaṃtānaḥ apatyaparamparā tena putrapautrakaram ityarthaḥ vājīkaraṇajanitācchukrāj jātaḥ putraḥ putrajananasamartho bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Continuity of offspring' means a succession of offspring; thus it means producing sons and grandsons. The meaning is that a son born from semen produced by <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> is capable of begetting sons.
And the fact of being extremely dear here is due to the ability to engage in intercourse without interruption, because semen has been increased. As it is said:
Kings desire even an ugly servant as a warrior;
women likewise desire as a husband a foolish and bold man who is practiced in sexual intercourse.
Thus.
"It is nourished" means it attains increase.
"Imperishable," as it were, means imperishable.
"Fruitful" means productive of an embryo.
A <s>caitya</s> is an abode of a deity.
"Worthy of worship" means fit to be worshiped.
"Endlessness," as it were, means endlessness, that is, a long continuity of lineage.
"Treatment" means in the treatment of fever and the like.

children.text: nanu rasāyanavājīkaraṇe api jvarādicikitsite eva tat kiṃ viśiṣyocyate vakṣyate taccikitsite ityāha cikitsitārtha ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Objection: rasāyana and vājīkaraṇa also belong precisely in the treatment of fever and the like; so why is it specifically said that they will be stated in that treatment? He answers with the words beginning "the purpose of treatment."

children.text: satyaṃ rasāyanaṃ vājīkaraṇaṃ ca jvarādivyādhiharatvāc cikitsitaśabdenocyata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is true: <s>rasāyana</s> and <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>, because they remove diseases such as fever, are denoted by the word "treatment": this is the meaning.

children.text: atha vyādhiharatvāccikitsite vaktavyatvācca rasāyanavājīkaraṇe kva nu vaktavye ityāha rasāyanetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, since rasāyana and vājīkaraṇa remove disease and so ought to be stated under treatment, where, then, should they be stated? He answers with the words beginning "rasāyana."
"Rule" means procedure, that is, what is called <s>rasāyana</s>.
"Ahead" means afterward.
And <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> too will be described afterward: this is the supplied remainder.
He also explains the previously mentioned non-medicine with the words beginning "non-medicine."
"Opposite" means producing an effect characterized by the generation of disease.
What is done by entering a hut is <s>kuṭīprāveśika</s>.
What is done even by exposure to wind and sun is <s>vātātapika</s>.

children.text: trigarbhāṃ prathamamekaṃ gṛhaṃ tasyābhyantare dvitīyam evaṃ trigarbhāstrayo garbhā antarāṇi yasyāṃ sā trigarbhāmiti antas triprakoṣṭhām ||
children.translated_text: "Having three interiors" means: first one house, inside that a second, and so on; thus one in which there are three interiors, three inner spaces, is called "having three interiors," that is, having three inner chambers.
"With small openings" means having small doorways and windows.
"In the bright fortnight" means in the bright half of the month.
That in which physicians and the others are ready is so called.
"Honored by lunar day and constellation" means honored because of the conjunction of an auspicious lunar day and constellation.
"Having had shaving done" means one whose shaving has been performed.
"Mental <s>doṣa</s>s" means desire, anger, and the like.
"By purifications" means by emesis, purgation, decoction-enema, and nasal purgation.
"Happy" means free from illness.

children.text: jātabala iti saṃśodhanāpahṛtamalatayā saṃsarjanādikrameṇa punar jātabalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Having regained strength" means having again acquired strength, through the sequence beginning with restorative diet, because the impurities have been removed by purification.

children.text: yadyapīha saṃśodhanair iti bahuvacanaprayogāt sarvāṇyeva saṃśodhanāni saṃmatāni tathāpīha rasāyane viśeṣeṇa yaugikatvāddharītakyādiprayoga evoktaḥ anye tu harītakyādiprayogeṇaiva paraṃ saṃśodhanaṃ kartavyam ityāhuḥ saṃśodhanair iti bahuvacanaṃ punar yāvacchuddher harītakyādiprayogasyaiva karaṇaṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: Although here, from the use of the plural in "by purifications," all purifications are accepted, nevertheless in this rasāyana, because of its special suitability, only the use of harītakī and the like is stated. Others, however, say that the highest purification should be performed only by the use of harītakī and the like; the plural "by purifications" again indicates the repeated performance of that very use of harītakī and the like until purification is complete.
"Yāvaka" means food made of barley.
The three alternatives beginning with three nights concern inferior, middling, and superior purification.

children.text: yadyapi dravyāntarāṇi daśavarṣaśatāyuṣkararasāyanādhikṛtāni santi tathāpi harītakyāmalake eva rogaharatvāyuṣkaratvarūpobhayadharmayogād adhyāyādau guṇakarmabhyāmucyete tatrāpi yadyapi āmalakaṃ vayaḥsthāpanānām ityuktaṃ tathāpi rogaharatve harītakī prakarṣavatīti kṛtvā harītaky agre 'bhihitā ||
children.translated_text: Although there are other substances authorized as rasāyanas that produce a life span of ten hundred years, still harītakī and āmalaka alone, because they possess both properties, namely removing disease and promoting longevity, are mentioned at the beginning of the chapter by their qualities and actions. And among them, although it has been said that āmalaka is foremost among age-stabilizing substances, nevertheless, because harītakī has excellence in removing disease, harītakī is mentioned first.

children.text: harītakyādiṣu pañcarasatvādyutpādo 'dṛṣṭavaśād bhūtasaṃniveśaviśeṣaprabhāvakṛtaḥ tena nātropapattayaḥ kramante ||
children.translated_text: The production of five tastes and the like in harītakī and similar substances is due to an unseen factor, produced by the special power of a particular arrangement of the elements; therefore explanations do not apply here.
"Auspicious" means causing welfare, because it is endowed with excellent qualities.
"Pacifying all diseases" means through combination, processing, and so on.
Although the removal of all diseases has been stated, the statement that it destroys skin disease and the like is for the purpose of showing specifically its destruction of skin disease and the like.

children.text: pravartakatve 'pyatīsāragrahaṇīharatvaṃ vibaddhadoṣapravartakatayā jñeyaṃ yaduktaṃ stokaṃ stokaṃ vibaddhaṃ vā saśūlaṃ yo 'tisāryete ||
children.translated_text: Even though it has a promoting action, its removal of diarrhea and grahaṇī disorder should be understood through its promoting obstructed doṣas, as has been said: "One who passes stool little by little, or obstructed stool, with pain,"
"should be purged with pastes of abhayā and pippalī, taken comfortably warm."
Although its giving of intellect and memory has been stated, the statement that it removes confusion of memory and intellect is for the purpose of showing a special power in that regard.

children.text: vīryasya tu viparyaya ityanenāmalakasya śītavīryatvam uktam ||
children.translated_text: By the phrase "but there is a reversal of potency," the cold potency of āmalaka is stated.
"Praiseworthy" means fruits without stones.

children.text: yadyapi himavān auṣadhabhūmīnām ityuktaṃ tathāpi rasāyane himavatprabhavāṇyeva bheṣajāni grāhyāṇīti darśayitum auṣadhīnām ityāhābhidhānam ||
children.translated_text: Although it has been said, "the Himavān is among the lands of herbs," still, in order to show that in rasāyana only medicines produced in the Himavān are to be taken, he states the expression "of herbs."
"At the proper times" means at the times when the fruits ripen.

children.text: yathāvidhīti yathā bheṣajagrahaṇaṃ maṅgaladevatārcanādipūrvakaṃ syāt tathāvaśyaṃ rasāyane kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: "According to rule" means that, just as the taking of medicines should be preceded by auspicious rites, worship of deities, and the like, so it must necessarily be done in rasāyana.
By the word "free from disease," he shows that the fruit is without defect from wind, burning, and the like.

children.text: pañcānām ityādau pratidravyaṃ daśapalabhāgagrahaṇam uktaṃ hi jātūkarṇe iti pañca pañcamūlāni teṣāṃ pratidravyaṃ daśapalāni iti ||
children.translated_text: In the passage beginning "of the five," the taking of ten palas of each substance is stated. For it is said in <s>Jātūkarṇa</s>: "The five sets of five roots; of these, ten palas of each substance."
"A thousand harītakīs" means a thousand fruits of harītakī.
"The two śūrpaparṇīs" are mudgaparṇī and māṣaparṇī.
"Vīrā" is the vegetable called jālaṃdhara.
"Kūrcana" is an implement for crushing, such as a small stone mortar and pestle.
"Having put in" means having thrown in.
"Plava" is kaivartamustaka.
"Kanaka" is nāgakeśara.
"Tvak" is the bark of jaggery.
"In an audumbara vessel" means in one made of copper.
"Half of the fat" means half ghee and oil.
"One" means a meal not taken in the afternoon.

children.text: piṣṭasvedanavidhineti yathā piṣṭakaṃ toyaparipūritapātroparidattatṛṇādisaṃsthitaṃ svedyate tathā tat svedanīyam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "By the method of <s>piṣṭa-svedana</s>" means: just as a cake of paste, placed on grass and the like set over a vessel filled with water, is steamed, so that is to be steamed.
"Soaked through with fresh juice" means impregnated with fresh juice.
The medicines beginning with <s>brahmasuvarcalā</s> are those that will be stated in the section on the arising of Ayurveda.
"Young woman" means <s>navamālikā</s>.
An eighth part is an <s>aṣṭabhāga</s>.
"Having the form of small jaggery" means having the form of <s>phāṇita</s>.
"With increase by half a <s>karṣa</s>" means that one should increase it beginning from half a <s>karṣa</s>.
"By the prescribed method" means by the <s>kuṭīprāveśika</s> method.
"The stated qualities" means those read in the earlier statement of the result of the procedure.

children.text: dharaṇīdharasāra iti uṣṭramukhavat tena dharaṇīdharāḥ parvatās teṣāṃ sāro lauhaṃ tadvatsāra ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Essence of the mountain-supporters" is like the expression "camel-mouthed": by it, the mountain-supporters are mountains, their essence is iron, and the meaning is "an essence like that."
"Non-poison" means poison that is unaltering.

children.text: parṇyaś catasra iti śālaparṇī pṛśniparṇī mudgaparṇī māṣaparṇī ca ||
children.translated_text: "The four <s>parṇī</s> plants" means <s>śālaparṇī</s>, <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>mudgaparṇī</s>, and <s>māṣaparṇī</s>.
<s>Tāmalakī</s> is <s>bhūmyāmalakī</s>.
<s>Kākanāsā</s> is <s>nāsāphalā</s>; others say it is <s>kākatuṇḍaka</s>.
Here the loss of taste of the substances occurs when the water has been reduced to one quarter.
"Without shell" means without a stone.

children.text: tailasarpiṣoriti samāsanirdeśād ubhābhyāmeva dvādaśapalāni na pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: "Of oil and ghee": because of the compound expression, the twelve <s>palas</s> belong to both together, not to each separately.
<s>Matsyaṇḍikā</s> is a compact mass of sugar crystals.
Here, although honey and ghee are equal, since they are six <s>palas</s> and are joined with other substances, there is no contradiction.
<s>Kukūlaka</s> is a fire of dung-cakes.
"Of those without kernels" means of those without stones.

children.text: dravyādīnāmatra mānaṃ noktaṃ tena pradhānasya cūrṇasya dadhyādibhir militaiḥ samānamānatvaṃ kiṃvā pratyekameva dadhyādīnāṃ cūrṇasamatvam ||
children.translated_text: Here the measure of the substances and so on is not stated. Therefore the principal powder may be equal in measure to the curd and the rest when combined, or each of the curd and the rest may separately be equal to the powder.
<s>Palala</s> is sesame flour.
The injunction "one should eat" is appropriate even for a linctus, because it has only the sense of taking a small amount.
"Eating no food" means eating absolutely no other food.
"At its end" means at the time of abandoning this procedure.

children.text: pratyavasthāpanamiti yavāgvādikramaviśeṣaṇaṃ tena prayogānte yadā annasaṃsarjanaṃ kartavyaṃ tadā yavāgvādikrameṇety uktasyārthasya pratyavasthāpanaṃ kriyata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Restoration" is a qualification of the sequence beginning with gruel. Thus, when, at the end of the procedure, reintroduction of food is to be done, restoration of the meaning expressed by "in the sequence beginning with gruel" is made.
"With soup or with milk" is an option dependent on the strength of the digestive fire.
Here, in the group beginning with <s>harītakī</s>, <s>kṣīraśuklā</s> is <s>kṣīravidārikā</s>.

children.text: atra harītakyādikvāthasya tv eko bhāgaḥ kṣīrasyāṣṭau bhāgāḥ sarpiṣa eko bhāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the decoction beginning with <s>harītakī</s> has one part, milk has eight parts, and ghee has one part.
A <s>kumbha</s> is two <s>droṇas</s>.

children.text: vacanaṃ hi droṇastu dviguṇaḥ śūrpo vijñeyaḥ kumbha eva ca iti ||
children.translated_text: For the statement is: "A <s>droṇa</s> is known to be double a <s>śūrpa</s>, and so too is a <s>kumbha</s>."
<s>Amṛtavallī</s> is <s>guḍūcī</s>.
<s>Somavalka</s> is <s>viṭkhadira</s>.
<s>Kṣīrasarpis</s> is ghee produced from milk.

children.text: ayaścūrṇasya caturtho bhāgaḥ yata etadayaścūrṇaṃ caturthabhāgamata ekasmin prayoge jātūkarṇena ayaścūrṇapādayuktam iti kṛtam
children.translated_text: The fourth part of the iron powder is meant; because this iron powder amounts to a fourth part, in one procedure <s>Jātūkarṇa</s> framed the expression "joined with a quarter of iron powder."

children.text: amarāṇāmamṛtaṃ jarādiharaṃ nāgānāṃ ca sudhā jarāmaraṇaharī ityubhayopādānaṃ dṛṣṭānte
children.translated_text: The ambrosia of the immortals removes old age and the like, and the nectar of the serpents removes old age and death; thus both are mentioned in the comparison.
<s>Brahman</s> means <s>mokṣa</s>.
Here the status of rasāyana as a means to <s>mokṣa</s> is stated because it is performed by one whose mind is purified.
With the passage beginning "<s>abhayā</s>," he shows the number of the stated procedures in order to remove doubt.
In the same way, elsewhere too, the setting forth of the number should be understood at the end.

children.text: pūrvapāde hy āmalakarasāyanānyuktāni ihāpyāmalakarasāyanāni santīti prāṇakāmīyam anantaram ucyate ||
children.translated_text: For in the previous quarter, <s>āmalaka</s> rasāyanas were stated; here too there are <s>āmalaka</s> rasāyanas, and so the section called <s>Prāṇakāmīya</s> is stated next.
Because it is made with reference to the word <s>prāṇakāma</s>, it is called <s>Prāṇakāmīya</s>.

children.text: nidrāharatvaṃ rasāyanasya vaikārikanidrāharatvena kiṃvā devavatsarvadā prabuddho nidrārahito bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The sleep-removing quality of rasāyana may be because it removes pathological sleep, or because one becomes like the gods, always awake and free from sleep.
The characteristic of torpor is stated in another tantra:
"Lack of awareness with respect to the objects of the senses, heaviness, yawning, and fatigue:

children.text: nidrārtasyeva yasyaite tasya tandrāṃ vinirdiśet iti ||
children.translated_text: when these belong to someone as if afflicted by sleep, one should identify that as torpor."
"Loose-fleshed" means having flesh that is not firm.
"Making the best radiance, complexion, and voice" means that it makes radiance and the rest excellent.

children.text: evaṃjātīyaś ca pūrvanipātāniyamo 'pratibandhena carake'sti sa mayūravyaṃsakādipāṭhād draṣṭavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This kind of non-fixed rule about what stands first in a compound exists freely in <s>Caraka</s>; it should be seen from the reading beginning with <s>mayūravyaṃsaka</s>.

children.text: anena hītyādinā purāvṛttakathanena rasāyanāni vakṣyamāṇāni pravṛttyarthaṃ stauti ||
children.translated_text: With the passage beginning "for by this," by telling an ancient event, he praises the rasāyanas that are going to be stated, so that people will undertake them.

children.text: rasāyanaprayoge varjanīyaṃ grāmyāhārādi dūṣaṇatvena nirdiśannāha sarve ityādi ||
children.translated_text: When indicating village food and the like, which must be avoided during rasāyana practice because they are corrupting, he says "all" and so on.
<s>Tila</s> is unground sesame; <s>palala</s> is sesame flour.
"Due to that cause" means caused by village food and the like.

children.text: śukraṃ na pravartata iti notpadyate śukramityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Semen does not proceed" means that semen is not produced.
"Each one a hundred cookings" is the meaning.

children.text: ekaikapākasādhanaṃ pṛthak kartavyaṃ tena triśatadhā pāko bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The preparation of each individual cooking should be done separately; thus there are three hundred cookings.

children.text: atra ca kalkopalepādi nopakṣīṇamapi yadavaśiṣṭaṃ bhavati tadeva grāhyaṃ vacanabalāt ||
children.translated_text: And here, with regard to the paste-smearing and the like, even what has not been used up, whatever remains, is to be taken, because of the force of the statement.

children.text: sauvarṇādipātreṣu yathāpūrvaṃ varaguṇatvam anyathā samānaguṇatve sarveṣāṃ mṛtpātrasya sulabhatvenātidurlabhataraṃ sauvarṇapātraṃ nopadeśam arhati ||
children.translated_text: In vessels made of gold and so on, superiority of quality follows the previous order. Otherwise, if all had equal quality, the golden vessel, being much harder to obtain than an earthen vessel, would not deserve to be prescribed.
"By the method stated" means by the <s>kuṭīprāveśika</s> method.
"Essence of the mountain" means iron.
"Young <s>palāśa</s>" means a <s>palāśa</s> tree that is young. By this, the exclusion of both immature and old <s>palāśa</s> is stated.

children.text: kṣārodakottaramiti yathā kṣārodakaṃ bhāvyādupari bhavati tathā kartavyamiti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: "With alkaline water above" indicates that it should be arranged so that the alkaline water with which it is to be impregnated remains above.
A fourth part is a quarter.
"The same as the preceding" means that this also is connected with the statement of the result of the preceding formula.

children.text: yāvad āśīr iti āśīḥ phalaśrutiḥ tena tadvarṣānte ityādi granthoktavidhividhānaṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: "As far as the benediction": the benediction is the statement of the result. Therefore it indicates the prescribed procedure stated in the text beginning "at the end of that year" and so on.
"With the preceding" means that this is the same as the preceding formula up to the statement of its result.
"In a dhanvan" means in arid, open country.
"Ploughing" means with a plough and the like.
"Not overgrown" means not encroached upon by a large tree standing nearby.
"In tapas" means in the month of <s>Māgha</s>.
"In tapasya" means in <s>Phālguna</s>.
"In a moving auspicious moment" means in the <s>Indra</s> muhūrta.
"Of the measure of an āmrā" means the measure of a pala.

children.text: punarnavāntā daśa ṣaḍvirecanaśatāśritīye amṛtābhayā dhātrī yuktā śreyasī śvetātirasā maṇḍūkaparṇī sthirā punarnavā iti sarvā vayaḥsthāpanoktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ten ending with <s>punarnavā</s> are those mentioned in the section <s>Ṣaḍvirecanaśatāśritīya</s>: <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>dhātrī</s>, <s>yuktā</s>, <s>śreyasī</s>, <s>śvetā</s>, <s>atirasā</s>, <s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>sthirā</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>; all are said to stabilize age.
"Explained with <s>nāgabalā</s>" means that their use too is like that of <s>nāgabalā</s>.
For <s>balā</s> and the others, the prescription is with their own fresh juice.
Food and the rest should be understood as in the case of <s>nāgabalā</s>.
When fresh juice is unavailable, he gives a substitute with the words beginning "of the fresh juices."

children.text: śuciḥ jyeṣṭhaḥ śukrastu āṣāḍhaḥ saha āgrahāyaṇaḥ sahasyaḥ pauṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śuci</s> is <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>; <s>Śukra</s> is <s>Āṣāḍha</s>; <s>Saha</s> is <s>Āgrahāyaṇa</s>; and <s>Sahasya</s> is <s>Pauṣa</s>.

children.text: etacca bhallātakaṃ māsacatuṣṭayasthitaṃ yavapallādau uddhṛtamātraṃ na prayojyaṃ kiṃtu yathokta eva kāle śītaguṇayukte ||
children.translated_text: And this <s>bhallātaka</s>, after remaining for four months in barley chaff and the like, is not to be used immediately upon being taken out; rather, it is to be used only at the stated time, when it possesses a cooling quality.
"Having anointed the inside of the mouth with ghee" is for the sake of avoiding burning in the mouth.

children.text: nātaḥ paramiti triṃśataḥ pareṇa prayogo na bhallātakasya ||
children.translated_text: "Not beyond this" means that <s>bhallātaka</s> is not to be used after thirty.

children.text: sahasraparo bhallātakaprayoga iti upayuktabhallātakasaṃpiṇḍanayā yadā sahasraṃ pūryate tadaivoparamaḥ kartavyaḥ sahasrādarvāgapi ca prayogaparityāgaḥ prakṛtyādyapekṣayā bhavatyeva ||
children.translated_text: "The use of <s>bhallātaka</s> extends to one thousand" means that, when one thousand is completed by adding together the <s>bhallātaka</s>s used, cessation should occur. Abandonment of the use even before one thousand may indeed occur, depending on constitution and the like.

children.text: sahasrasaṃkhyāpūraṇaṃ cehaikena vardhanahrāsakrameṇa na bhavati tena punar āvṛttyā ca triṃśatparyantaṃ prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ yathā hi bhallātakaprayogābhyāsena sahasrasaṃkhyāpūraṇaṃ bhavati tathā kṛtvā parityāgaḥ kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The completion of the number one thousand here does not occur by a single course of increase and decrease. Therefore the use up to thirty should be performed again and again; when the number one thousand has been completed by repeated practice of <s>bhallātaka</s> use, it should then be abandoned.

children.text: anye tv atra suśrute arśaścikitsitoktaśataparyantaṃ bhallātakaprayogeṇa samaṃ virodhaṃ paśyantaḥ suśrutaprayogasyāpyanyathā vyākhyānena triṃśatkamātraṃ prayogamicchanti tacca vyākhyānaṃ nātisaṃgatam ||
children.translated_text: Others, seeing here a contradiction with the <s>bhallātaka</s> use up to one hundred taught in <s>Suśruta</s>'s treatment of piles, interpret even the <s>Suśruta</s> procedure differently and want the use to be only up to thirty. But that interpretation is not very coherent.

children.text: kiṃca sahasradvayasya tatropayogo vihitaḥ atra sahasraparyantaḥ prayogaḥ tena vyādhiviṣayo'nya eva sa prayogaḥ ayaṃ tu rasāyanaviṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, there the use of two thousand is prescribed, while here the use extends only to one thousand. Therefore that procedure has disease as its subject, whereas this one has <s>rasāyana</s> as its subject.

children.text: piṣṭasvedanaṃ tat yatrasthaṃ piṣṭakam upasvedyate tadupari yat pidhānapātraṃ tacceha sacchidraṃ grāhyam anyathoparisthabhallātakatāpāc cyutaḥ sneho nādho yāti ||
children.translated_text: "Steaming of the paste" is the process in which the paste-cake placed in a vessel is steamed. The covering vessel above it should here be taken as perforated; otherwise, because of the heat of the <s>bhallātaka</s> above, the oil that drips down would not go downward.
"<s>Bhallātaka</s> oil" means the oily substance of <s>bhallātaka</s> obtained by the procedure just stated.
<s>Bhallātaka</s> ghee and the others are the ten applications.

children.text: atra ca yathāyogyatayā bhallātakena sarpirādīnāṃ saṃskāraḥ saṃyogaśca jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And here, according to what is suitable, the processing of ghee and the other substances with <s>bhallātaka</s>, and their combination with it, should be understood.
As has been said in <s>Jatūkarṇa</s>: "ghee, milk, honey, jaggery, soup, oil, meat paste, flour, salt, and tarpaṇa, processed or combined with <s>bhallātaka</s>."

children.text: evaṃ ca sarpiḥkṣīrayūṣatailānāṃ saṃskāro yathānyāyaṃ bhallātakena kṣaudrapalalasaktutarpaṇānāṃ bhallātakena yogaḥ guḍalavaṇayostu saṃskāraḥ saṃyogo vā ||
children.translated_text: Thus, ghee, milk, soup, and oil are processed with <s>bhallātaka</s> in the proper way; honey, meat paste, flour, and tarpaṇa are combined with <s>bhallātaka</s>; but in the case of jaggery and salt, either processing or combination may apply.

children.text: lavaṇe saṃskārapakṣe hi lavaṇasamaṃ bhallātakam antardhūmadagdhaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: For in the interpretation that salt is processed, <s>bhallātaka</s> equal to the salt, burned in a covered-fire process, should be taken.

children.text: anye tu sarpirādīnāṃ sarveṣāmeva bhallātakena saṃskāraṃ vyākhyānayanti ||
children.translated_text: Others, however, explain that all the substances beginning with ghee are processed with <s>bhallātaka</s>.
Here the use of flour, because it is not predominantly liquid, is to be distinguished by a non-specific procedure.
"Like fire" means because they cause burning and blisters.
"Having prepared" means having accomplished it.

children.text: pādānusaṃgrahe saptatriṃśatprayogā uktāḥ tatra balādibhiraṣṭābhiḥ punarnavāntaiśca daśabhiraṣṭādaśaprayogāḥ apare tu vyāhṛtā vyaktā eva ||
children.translated_text: In the collection of sections, thirty-seven applications are stated. Among them, with the eight beginning with <s>balā</s> and the ten ending with <s>punarnavā</s>, there are eighteen applications; the others that have been mentioned are quite explicit.

children.text: visarpe prāyeṇa tṛṣṇā upadravarūpā bhavatīti visarpānantaraṃ tṛṣṇācikitsitam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: In <s>visarpa</s>, thirst generally occurs as a complication; therefore, after <s>visarpa</s>, the treatment of thirst is stated.

children.text: jñānetyādau jñānaṃ tattvajñānaṃ praśamaḥ śāntiḥ tapaḥ cāndrāyaṇādi ||
children.translated_text: In the passage beginning "knowledge," knowledge is knowledge of reality; pacification is tranquility; and austerity is the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> and the like.

children.text: cikitsitaṃ cikitsāvidhāyako granthaḥ nidānādyabhidhānaṃ ca cikitsārthameva nidānādijñānapūrvakatvāc cikitsāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Treatment" means a text that prescribes the method of treatment. The statement of diagnosis and the rest also exists precisely for the sake of treatment, because treatment depends on prior knowledge of diagnosis and the like.

children.text: pañcānāmiti vacanena pañcānāmapi cikitsāviṣayatvaṃ darśayati nahi kāsaśvāsavadasyāsādhyatvaṃ kasyāścid atretyarthaḥ tathā suśrutoktātiriktatṛṣṇādvayāntarbhāvaṃ pañcasveva sūcayati ||
children.translated_text: By the expression "of the five," he shows that all five are subjects of treatment. For, unlike cough and dyspnea, none of them is incurable here; this is the meaning. He also indicates that the two additional kinds of thirst taught by <s>Suśruta</s> are included within these five alone.

children.text: uktaṃ hi suśrute tisraḥ smṛtāstāḥ kṣatajā caturthī kṣayāttathā hy āmasamudbhavā ca ||
children.translated_text: For it is said in <s>Suśruta</s>: "Those three are remembered, and the fourth is born from injury; and likewise one from wasting, and one arising from <s>āma</s> (undigested morbid matter)."
"A seventh would be caused by food"; thus.

children.text: kṣobhād ityādyuktanidānasya yathāyogyatayā vātakartṛtvaṃ vātapittakartṛtvaṃ conneyam ||
children.translated_text: For the causation stated in the passage beginning "from agitation," agency by <s>vāta</s>, and agency by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, should be inferred as appropriate.
The passage beginning "<s>pitta</s> and <s>anila</s>" is the text on the pathogenesis of all forms of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (morbid thirst).
"The mild bodily elements" means <s>kapha</s>, <s>rasa</s>, and water, which are characterized especially by lunar qualities.
"They vitiate" means they vitiate by drying up.
"Klomna" is a form ending in the second case plural.

children.text: dehe ityanena etāsāṃ tṛṣṇānāṃ śarīratvaṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By saying "in the body," he shows that these forms of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> are bodily.

children.text: yā hi mānasī tṛṣṇā sā śarīre icchādveṣātmikā tṛṣṇā sukhaduḥkhāt pravartate ityādāv uktā iyaṃ tu dehāśrayadoṣakāraṇā satī dehajaiveti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For mental <s>tṛṣṇā</s> is the thirst in the body whose nature is desire and aversion, stated in passages such as "it proceeds from pleasure and pain." But this one, having bodily <s>doṣa</s>s as its cause while resting in the body, is indeed bodily-born: this is the idea.

children.text: svābhāvikatṛṣṇāyām api vātapitte ārambhake eva tat kiṃ sāpyatra na gṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: Even in natural thirst, <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> are initiating factors. Why, then, is that not also included here?

children.text: maivaṃ tasyā ucitadravapānenaivābhipretena praśamād iha asvābhāvikavyādhiprakaraṇe nādhikāra iti hṛdi kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: Not so. Since that is calmed merely by drinking the suitable fluid desired, it has no scope here in the section on unnatural disease. This is what he has in mind.

children.text: svābhāvikatṛṣṇākaravātapittābhyāṃ vakṣyamāṇatṛṣṇārambhakavātapittayor viśeṣamāha pītaṃ pītam ityādi ||
children.translated_text: He states the difference between the <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> that cause natural thirst and the <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> that initiate the thirst to be described, with the words beginning "drunk, drunk."

children.text: prakṛtatṛṣṇārambhakau pittavātau pītaṃ pītaṃ jalaṃ śoṣayataḥ ato jalaśoṣaṇatvāddhetor na śamaṃ yāti puruṣaḥ svābhāvikyāṃ jalaṃ pītvā śāntimadhigacchatīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s> that initiate the thirst under discussion dry up the water each time it is drunk. Therefore, because they dry up water, the person does not attain relief; in natural thirst, however, he obtains relief after drinking water: this is the meaning.
He states the arising of thirst in the form of a complication, with the words beginning "terrible."
"Being secondary afflictions" means being in the form of complications.
He states the prodromal sign of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, with the words beginning "the prodrome."

children.text: prāgrūpakathane eva madhye tṛṣṇānāmavyabhicārilakṣaṇam āha svalakṣaṇam ityādi ||
children.translated_text: In the very statement of the prodrome, he states in between the unfailing characteristic sign of the thirsts, with the words beginning "the own-characteristic."

children.text: svalakṣaṇam iti avyabhicārilakṣaṇaṃ yathā jvarasya saṃtāpaḥ śvayathor utsedhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Own-characteristic" means an unfailing characteristic, as heat is of fever, and swelling is of edema.

children.text: punaḥ prakṛtaṃ prāgrūpam āha liṅgānāṃ lāghavamapāya iti ||
children.translated_text: Again he states the relevant prodrome: "the lightness of the signs is disappearance."

children.text: liṅgānāṃ vakṣyamāṇavātādijatṛṣṇāliṅgānāṃ lāghavam alpatvaṃ keṣāṃcic cābhāvaḥ pūrvarūpaṃ tṛṣṇānām ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Lightness of the signs" means the slightness, and in some cases the absence, of the signs of thirst born from <s>vāta</s> and the other causes to be described; this is the prodromal form of the thirsts.

children.text: tena pūrvarūpāvasthāyāṃ vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇāni kānicin na bhavantyeva yāni ca bhavanti tānyalpatayāsphuṭāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, at the prodromal stage, some of the signs to be described simply do not occur, and those that do occur are indistinct because they are slight.

children.text: uktaṃ ca avyaktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tasya pūrvarūpam iti smṛtam iti ||
children.translated_text: And it has been said: "The indistinct sign of it is remembered as the prodrome."

children.text: kiṃvā yadetat prāgrūpaṃ mukhaśoṣaḥ svalakṣaṇaṃ sarvadāmbukāmitvam etat prāgrūpaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ ca tṛṣṇānāṃ tena mukhaśoṣāmbukāmitve svalakṣaṇe tathā pūrvarūpe ca bhavataḥ pūrvarūpāvasthāyāṃ tv aprabale mukhaśoṣāmbukāmitve jñeye ||
children.translated_text: Or else, this prodrome is dryness of the mouth, and the own-characteristic is the constant desire for water. This is both the prodrome and the own-characteristic of the thirsts. Therefore dryness of the mouth and desire for water are both own-characteristics and prodromes; but at the prodromal stage they should be understood as weak dryness of the mouth and weak desire for water.

children.text: ye tu prāgrūpaṃ mukhaśoṣaḥ svarakṣayaḥ sarvadāmbukāmitvam iti paṭhanti teṣāṃ mate tṛṣṇāyāḥ svalakṣaṇaṃ noktaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: But according to those who read, "the prodrome is dryness of the mouth, loss of voice, and constant desire for water," the own-characteristic of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> would not have been stated.

children.text: uktaṃ ca hārīte'pi tṛṣṇāsvalakṣaṇaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ tu tṛṣṇānāṃ sarvadāmbupipāsitā iti ||
children.translated_text: And in <s>Hārīta</s> too the own-characteristic of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> is stated: "The own-characteristic of the thirsts is constant thirst for water."

children.text: kiṃvā mukhaśoṣasvarakṣaye eva pūrvarūpaṃ sarvadāmbukāmitvaṃ ca svalakṣaṇaṃ liṅgānāṃ ca lāghavaṃ rogarūpāyās tṛṣṇāyā apāyo gamanamityarthaḥ ayameva tṛṣṇāvyuparamo yad vakṣyamāṇaliṅgānām alpatvaṃ sarvathocchedo hi tṛṣṇālakṣaṇānāṃ na bhavatyeva sahajatṛṣṇāgrastatvenaitallakṣaṇānām alpamātratayāvasthānāt ||
children.translated_text: Or else, dryness of the mouth and loss of voice alone are the prodrome, and constant desire for water is the own-characteristic. The lightness of the signs is the disappearance, that is, the passing away, of thirst in the form of disease. This cessation of thirst itself is the slightness of the signs to be described; for there is never a complete eradication of the signs of thirst, since these signs remain in a very small measure because one is affected by innate thirst.

children.text: kaiścit tu liṅgānāṃ lāghavam āśūtpādaḥ sa ca apāyo maraṇam iti kṛtvā tṛṣṇānāmasādhyatālakṣaṇamidamucyate tannātimanoharam ||
children.translated_text: But some take "lightness of the signs" as rapid onset, and "disappearance" as death; on that basis, this is said to be a sign of the incurability of the thirsts. That is not very attractive.
