He states the complications of all forms of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, with the words beginning "dryness of the mouth."
"Arisen" means increased.

children.text: ye tu mukhaśoṣādīni lakṣaṇānyāhustanmate tṛṣṇopadravānām abhidhānaṃ na syāt upadravāścādhyāyasaṃgrahe saṃgṛhītāḥ tenātiśayavṛddhā mukhaśoṣādaya upadravāḥ vṛddhāstu liṅgam iti vyavasthā ||
children.translated_text: Those who say that dryness of the mouth and the rest are symptoms would, on their view, leave the complications of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> unstated; and the complications are included in the chapter summary. Therefore dryness of the mouth and the like, when excessively increased, are complications; when merely increased, they are symptoms. This is the arrangement.
With the words beginning "the water element," he states the pathogenesis and so on of the five kinds.
"Situated in the body" means situated in the body in the various forms of <s>rasa</s> and the like.
It should be construed as: "when the water element is dried up, it dries up."
"Obstruction of the channels" means severe impairment.
With the words beginning "<s>pitta</s>," he states the <s>pitta</s>-born form.

children.text: śarīrasaṃkhyāśarīre pittamāpyam uktaṃ yad dravasarasnigdhamandamṛdupicchilaṃ rasarudhiravasākaphapittasvedādi tad āpyaṃ raso rasanaṃ ca ityanena tathā tatraiva yat pittasya yo yā ca śarīre bhāḥ tat sarvam āgneyam ityanena dvayātmakatvaṃ pittasya yadyapyuktaṃ tathāpyāgneyākāratvād bāhulyāt pittam āgneyam eveti darśayannāha pittaṃ matam āgneyam iti dvayātmakatve 'pi ca pittasyāgneyāṃśaprādhānyād anyatrāpi saumyāgneyavāyavyavikārabhede paittikavikārā āgneyatvena gṛhītā eva ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Śarīra</s> section, in the chapter on the enumeration of the body, <s>pitta</s> was said to be watery by the statement, "whatever is fluid, flowing, unctuous, slow, soft, and slimy, such as <s>rasa</s>, blood, fat, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, sweat, and so on, is watery; also <s>rasa</s> and the organ of taste." And there too, by the statement, "whatever brilliance belongs to <s>pitta</s>, and whatever brightness there is in the body, all that is fiery," the twofold nature of <s>pitta</s> has indeed been taught. Nevertheless, because its fiery form is predominant, <s>pitta</s> is simply fiery. Showing this, he says, "<s>pitta</s> is considered fiery." And although <s>pitta</s> has a twofold nature, because its fiery portion predominates, elsewhere too, in the division of disorders as lunar, fiery, and airy, <s>pitta</s> disorders are taken precisely as fiery.
"For that, being heated" means: the water element, being heated.

children.text: saṃtaptaṃ hi iti pāṭhapakṣe pittameva janayediti yojyam ||
children.translated_text: In the reading "indeed heated," it should be construed that it produces <s>pitta</s> alone.

children.text: yadābdhātur janayati tadā pittasaṃtapta eva janayatīti pittasyaiva kartṛtvam ||
children.translated_text: When the water-element produces it, it produces it only when heated by <s>pitta</s>; therefore the agency belongs to <s>pitta</s> alone.
With the words beginning "thirst," he states the type born from <s>āma</s>.

children.text: āmaśabdena ceha lakṣaṇayā āmasamānacikitsita āmasamānalakṣaṇaś ca kapho 'pi gṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: And here, by implication, the word <s>āma</s> also includes <s>kapha</s>, since it has treatment like that of <s>āma</s> and symptoms like those of <s>āma</s>.

children.text: tenāmaprabhavāyā vyutpādanena kaphajāpi suśrutoktā gṛhītaiveha sāpyāgneyetyanena pūrvaparijñātaṃ sarvāsāṃ vātapittajanyatvaṃ samunnayati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by deriving the type produced from <s>āma</s>, the <s>kapha</s>-born thirst stated by <s>Suśruta</s> is also included here; and by the statement that it too is fiery, he infers the previously established fact that all forms of thirst are produced by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: vātaśca tṛṣṇākāraṇatvenokto'pyatrāpradhānaṃ pittameva ye pradhānam itīha vātākathanād unnīyate ||
children.translated_text: Although <s>vāta</s> too is stated as a cause of thirst, here it is secondary and <s>pitta</s> alone is principal; this is inferred from the absence of any mention of <s>vāta</s> here.
Elsewhere too it has been said: vision, digestion, heat, hunger, thirst, and softness of the body,
lustre, clarity, and intelligence are functions of <s>pitta</s>, arising when it is not disordered.
"Because it is produced by <s>āma</s>-<s>pitta</s>" means because it is produced by <s>pitta</s> increased through obstruction by <s>āma</s>.
With the words beginning "the body is born from <s>rasa</s>," he states the type born from depletion.

children.text: āhārarasāt sarvadhātupoṣako dhāturasa utpadyate sa ca raso dehapoṣako 'mbubhava iti āpya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From the nutritive essence of food there arises the fluid essence of the tissues, which nourishes all the bodily tissues; and that <s>rasa</s>, since it nourishes the body and is produced from water, is watery.

children.text: tasya kṣayāditi rasakṣayāt tṛṣyate rasakṣayād ambukṣayo bhavati tena cāmbukṣayeṇa puruṣaḥ pānīyaprārthanārūpatṛṣṇayā yukto bhavatīti yuktam iti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: "Because of its depletion" means because of the depletion of <s>rasa</s>. From depletion of <s>rasa</s> there is depletion of water, and by that depletion of water a person becomes affected by thirst in the form of a desire for drinking water; this is reasonable, he shows.

children.text: uktaṃ hi suśrute doṣadhātumalakṣīṇo balakṣīṇo'pi mānavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For it has been said in <s>Suśruta</s>: "A human being whose <s>doṣa</s>s, tissues, and waste-products are depleted, and whose strength too is depleted,

children.text: svayonivardhanaṃ yat tad annapānaṃ prakāṅkṣati iti ihāpi coktaṃ tasya kṣayācca tṛṣyeddhi iti ||
children.translated_text: desires that food and drink which increase its own source." And here too it has been said, "And because of its depletion, he indeed thirsts."
With the words beginning "there is," he states the type born from an accompanying complication.
"From an accompanying complication" means from a secondary disorder such as fever, that is, in the form of such a complication as fever.
"Difficult" means difficult to cure.

children.text: evaṃ prāksūtritavātapittāmāmbukṣayopasargātmikāḥ pañca tṛṣṇā vyāhṛtāḥ atraiva suśrutoktā kaphajā āmajāyām avaruddhā kṣatajā upasargātmikāyām avaruddhā annajā cāmajāyām evāntarbhāvanīyā ||
children.translated_text: Thus the five forms of thirst, previously outlined as having the nature of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>āma</s>, depletion of water, and accompanying complication, have been explained. In this very context, the <s>kapha</s>-born type stated by <s>Suśruta</s> is included under the <s>āma</s>-born type, the wound-born type under the type with accompanying complication, and the food-born type under the <s>āma</s>-born type itself.
Now he states the signs of incurability among forms of thirst, with the words beginning "all, however."
"Joined with terrible complications" means possessing distressing secondary disorders.

children.text: etacchāstrasaṃskāropapattyupadarśanapūrvakaṃ śāstrasya saṃskārakau carakadṛḍhabalau darśayannāha dṛḍhabalaḥ vistārayatītyādi ||
children.translated_text: Having first shown the propriety of redacting this treatise, and then showing <s>Caraka</s> and <s>Dṛḍhabala</s> as the redactors of the treatise, he says, "<s>Dṛḍhabala</s> expands," and so on.

children.text: yasmācchāstre prathamamativistāratayā kvacilleśoktyā ca pratipāditeṣu na samyagarthāvagamaḥ tena tadativistaraleśoktadoṣanirāsārthaṃ saṃskartā yujyate ataḥ tantrottamam idaṃ carakeṇa saṃskṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Since correct understanding of the meaning does not arise when topics are first taught in a treatise sometimes with excessive diffuseness and sometimes with only brief mention, a redactor is appropriate in order to remove the faults of excessive detail and bare mention. Therefore this excellent <s>tantra</s> was redacted by <s>Caraka</s>.

children.text: pūrvagranthasya cātīva vistaratvādinā tantrābhidhānaṃ pūrvaśrotṛjanābhiprāyādeva boddhavyam idānīṃtanaśrotṛpuruṣābhiprāyeṇa tu saṃskartuḥ saṃskāro jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The designation <s>tantra</s> for the earlier work, because of its very great extent and so on, should be understood according to the intention of the earlier hearers; but according to the intention of present-day hearers, the redaction belongs to the redactor.

children.text: uktaṃ ca saṃkṣepoktam atihanti vistaroktaṃ na gṛhyate
children.translated_text: And it has been said: what is stated too briefly is passed over; what is stated at length is not grasped.
Leaving aside both brevity and elaboration, one should redact the treatise from the beginning.
Thus.

children.text: purāṇaṃ ca punarnavam iti vistārasaṃkṣepādinā punarnavaṃ kurute ||
children.translated_text: And the statement "old, yet new again" means that he makes it new again by elaboration, abbreviation, and the like.
Showing the incompleteness of <s>Caraka</s>'s redaction, <s>Dṛḍhabala</s> says the words beginning "that."
A third part is one part among three.

children.text: tribhāgāsaṃpūrṇatā ceyam adūrāntaratayoktā tena dṛḍhabalapratipāditaikacatvāriṃśadadhyāyānāṃ na saviṃśādhyāyaśatatribhāgatā yujyate iti nodbhāvanīyam ||
children.translated_text: And this incompleteness by a third is stated as an approximation. Therefore it should not be objected that the forty-one chapters expounded by <s>Dṛḍhabala</s> do not amount to one third of the one hundred and twenty chapters.
He shows that he himself was from an excellent region by saying that he was born in <s>Pañcanadapura</s>.

children.text: ātmanaḥ saṃskāre tantrāntarānītārthena saṃskāraṃ darśayannāha kṛtvā bahubhya ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Showing that, in his own redaction, the redaction was made with material brought from other <s>tantra</s>s, he says the words beginning "having made from many."
"From <s>tantra</s>s" means from <s>tantra</s>s such as those of <s>Suśruta</s> and <s>Videha</s>.

children.text: viśeṣasya carakoktārthād atiriktarūpasya uñchaśilarūpa uccayo viśeṣoñchaśiloccayaḥ tamanyatantrebhyaḥ kṛtvā saptadaśauṣadhādhyāyasiddhikalpair idam anyūnaśabdārthaṃ tantradoṣavivarjitaṃ ṣaḍviṃśattantrayuktibhir bhūṣitam apūrayad dṛḍhabala iti yojanā ||
children.translated_text: The collection, in the form of gleaning and picking, of a special item additional to the meaning stated by <s>Caraka</s> is the "collection of special gleanings and pickings." The construction is: having made that from other <s>tantra</s>s, <s>Dṛḍhabala</s> completed this work with seventeen chapters on medicines, the Siddhi section, and the Kalpa section, deficient neither in wording nor in meaning, free from faults of a <s>tantra</s>, and adorned with twenty-six <s>tantrayukti</s>s.

children.text: tatra bhūmipatitānām aṇūnāṃ dhānyādibījānāṃ śodhanyā saṃharaṇam uñchaḥ praviralasya tu kaṇiśādirūpatayā patitasya cayanaṃ śilaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, <s>uñcha</s> is gathering with a winnowing implement the tiny grains and other seeds fallen on the ground, while <s>śila</s> is picking up what has fallen sparsely, in the form of ears of grain and the like.

children.text: etena tantreṣu yatsārabhūtaṃ taccarakācāryaiḥ saṃgṛhītaṃ mayā tu urvaritaṃ pariśiṣṭaṃ kṛtvā pūritam iti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By this he shows: what was essential in the <s>tantra</s>s was gathered by Ācārya <s>Caraka</s>; but I have completed it by taking what was left over and remaining.
"Deficient neither in word nor in meaning" means deficient neither in wording nor in meaning.

children.text: tantradoṣāścaturdaśa punaruktaṃ duṣpraṇītasūtrasaṃgraham akramaṃ ityādinā rogabhiṣagjitīyoktās tair varjitam ||
children.translated_text: The faults of a <s>tantra</s> are fourteen, stated in the Rogabhiṣagjitīya with "repetition, badly composed collection of aphorisms, disorder," and so on; it is free from those.
"By <s>tantrayukti</s>s" means by the <s>tantrayukti</s>s that will be stated below.
"Varied" means by <s>tantrayukti</s>s joined with varied meanings and lines of reasoning.
Because of the similarity in being an <s>āmalaka</s> <s>rasāyana</s>, the Karapracitīya is stated immediately afterward.
The phrase "of those gathered by hand" excludes the taking of fruits that have fallen by themselves.

children.text: māghe phālgune vetigrahaṇavacanāt tathaiva gṛhītānāmadhikāra ityāgamādunnīyate ||
children.translated_text: Because of the statement that it is to be gathered in <s>Māgha</s> or <s>Phālguna</s>, it is inferred from tradition that eligibility belongs to things gathered in just that way.
Here the fresh juice is of <s>āmalaka</s> alone, because that is the topic under consideration.
<s>Śāka</s> is a large-leaved tree.
"Cut" means severed.

children.text: iha gomayāgnyādyupakaraṇaniyamenaiva śaktyutkarṣo bhavatīti ṛṣivacanād unnīyate ||
children.translated_text: Here, from the rule about implements such as a fire of cow dung, the superiority of potency is inferred from the statement of the sages.

children.text: yaduktam ṛṣayas tv eva jānanti yogasaṃyogajaṃ phalam iti ||
children.translated_text: For it has been said: only the seers know the result produced by yogic and material combination.
In the same way, elsewhere too, a rule about the required procedure should be explained.
"Of a black hide" means of the hide of a black antelope.

children.text: samprati rasāyanasya tapobrahmacaryadhyānādiyuktasyaiva mahāphalatvaṃ bhavatīti darśayannāha tapasetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, showing that rasāyana has great fruit only when joined with austerity, celibacy, meditation, and the like, he says "through austerity" and so on.

children.text: kālayuktena cāyuṣeti aniyatakālayuktena cāyuṣetyarthaḥ niyatakālāyuṣaṃ prati tu na rasāyanaṃ phalavadityuktam eva ||
children.translated_text: "And with a life joined with time" means "with a life joined with an indeterminate time." But with regard to a lifespan whose time is fixed, it has already been said that rasāyana is not fruitful.
"Remaining" means living for a long time.

children.text: viparyayeṇa tapaḥprabhṛtivirahe rasāyanasyāphalatām āha na hītyādi ||
children.translated_text: In the opposite case, when austerity and the like are absent, he states the fruitlessness of rasāyana with "for not" and so on.

Although restraint of the senses is obtained through the state of a <s>brahmacārin</s>, the connection with the word "controlled in the senses" is meant to show an exceptional degree of sense-restraint.
In the months beginning with <s>Pauṣa</s>, the year-ending should be understood as the completion of a year counted from the prescribed day.
At the end of the expression "<s>Phālgunī</s>," the word "having reached" is to be supplied.

children.text: na drumamārohet ityasyeha āruhya drumamiti vacanenāpavādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rule "one should not climb a tree" has an exception here in the statement "having climbed a tree."
"Reciting <s>brahman</s>" means reciting the syllable <s>oṃ</s>.
"From the coming of immortality" means up to the coming of immortality.
"Their satisfaction" is a genitive used in the instrumental sense.
"Having the form of speech" means the deity presiding over it.
"In alkali" means in filtered alkaline water.
"Saline in alkali" means in the alkali of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>.
"One should prepare" means one should quench it.

children.text: lauhānāmityanenaiva lohāntarniviṣṭayoḥ suvarṇarajatayor grahaṇe siddhe punas tayor vacanaṃ tayor viśeṣeṇādaropadarśanārtham ||
children.translated_text: By the word "metals" the inclusion of gold and silver, which are comprised among metals, is already established; their being mentioned again is for showing special regard for them.
It should be understood that great wealth comes from the power of rasāyana itself.

children.text: matsyākhyako macchu iti loke khyātaḥ anye tu aindrībhedaṃ matsyākhyakam āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which is called <s>matsyākhya</s> is known in common usage as <s>macchu</s>; others, however, say that <s>matsyākhya</s> is a variety of <s>aindrī</s>.
"Three-barley-grain pieces" means pieces measuring three barley grains.
"Rich in ghee" is a qualifier of the food.
<s>Kṛtyā</s> means sorcery, <s>abhicāra</s>.
The four formulations are those beginning with <s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>.

children.text: pañcetyādau saṃkhyāvyatikrameṇānuktasaṃkhyānām api pippalīnām upayogaṃ sūcayati ||
children.translated_text: In the passage beginning "five," by a departure in number he indicates the use even of <s>pippalī</s> fruits whose number has not been stated.

children.text: yadāpi trīṇi dravyāṇi nātyupayuñjīta pippalīṃ kṣāraṃ lavaṇam ityuktaṃ tathāpīha dravyāntarasaṃyuktānāṃ pippalīnām abhyāso na viruddhaḥ kiṃvā uktapippalīrasāyanavyatirekeṇotsargāpavādanyāyāt sa niṣedho jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Although it has been said, "One should not overuse the three substances <s>pippalī</s>, alkali, and salt," nevertheless here the repeated use of <s>pippalī</s> fruits combined with other substances is not contradictory. Or else, by the principle of general rule and exception, that prohibition should be understood as applying apart from the stated <s>pippalī</s> rasāyana.
<s>Kiṃśuka</s> is <s>palāśa</s>.

children.text: śilājaturasāyanaṃ darśayituṃ śilājatuno 'bhyarhitasya guṇāneva tāvadāha anamlam ityādi ||
children.translated_text: In order to show the <s>śilājatu</s> rasāyana, he first states the qualities of <s>śilājatu</s>, which is especially worthy of honor, with "not sour" and so on.
"From the best" means from the excellent one.

children.text: suśrute yadyapi trapusīsambhavaṃ prakṣipya ṣaḍvidhaśilājatu sāmānyena roge rasāyanādhikāre coktaṃ tathāpīha rasāyanādhikāre tadadhikṛtacaturvidham evoktam ||
children.translated_text: Although in <s>Suśruta</s>, after adding the kind originating from tin, sixfold <s>śilājatu</s> is stated generally in the context of diseases and in the rasāyana section, nevertheless here, in the rasāyana section, only the fourfold kind relevant to that topic is stated.
He states the method of impregnating <s>śilājatu</s> with the passage beginning "having been placed."
What is removed immediately after being placed is called "placed-and-removed."
"Together with metals": when there is no rule about the proportions, the <s>śilājatu</s> has a portion equal to the metal.

children.text: prayogaḥ saptasaptāhā iti saptasaptāhavyāpakaprayoga ityarthaḥ evaṃ trayaś caikaśca saptaka ityatrāpi boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: "The use is seven weeks" means a use extending over seven weeks. The same should be understood also in the expression "three and one septad."
"With the method" means together with the prescribed procedure.

children.text: śilājatuvidhānaṃ ca yathākramaṃ vātapitte ityādigranthena vaktavyam ||
children.translated_text: The regimen for <s>śilājatu</s> is to be stated in due order by the passage beginning "in vāta and pitta."

children.text: hemādiśabdeneha hemādisambhavasthānabhūtaśilocyate yato na sākṣāt suvarṇādibhya eva śilājatu sravati ||
children.translated_text: By the word beginning with "gold" here is meant the mountain rock that is the place where gold and the other metals originate, since <s>śilājatu</s> does not flow directly from gold and the rest themselves.
<s>Mṛtsna</s> means smooth; <s>accha</s> means clear.

children.text: yastu rūpyabhave kaṭurase viruddhaḥ svāduḥ pāka uktaḥ sa utsargāpavādanyāyena jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the sweet post-digestive effect which, in the silver-origin kind, conflicts with the pungent taste is to be understood by the principle of general rule and exception.

children.text: vīryaṃ tu tāmrabhavasyoṣṇasya tathā trayāṇāṃ ca śītatvayuktānām atyuṣṇaśītavīryatāyā avakāśo nāsti ataḥ sāmānyaguṇakathane nātyuṣṇaśītam itipadena uṣṇasya śītasya ca vīryasya prakarṣo niṣidhyate tenānuṣṇāśītatvaṃ vidhīyate tataśca śilājatuni vīryaṃ śītam uṣṇaṃ vābhihitamapi na balavadbhavatīti labhyate ||
children.translated_text: As for potency, in the case of the copper-origin kind, which is hot, and of the three kinds characterized by coldness, there is no scope for an excessively hot or cold potency. Therefore, in the statement of common qualities, the phrase "not very hot or cold" denies an extreme of hot and cold potency; thereby a neither-hot-nor-cold condition is prescribed. Hence, even when a cold or hot potency is stated for <s>śilājatu</s>, it is understood not to be strong.
The plural "in the uses of <s>śilājatu</s>" should be understood with the different applications, such as stirring, kept in mind.
Although heavy substances are prohibited in the <s>śilājatu</s> procedure, the use of milk and the like is allowed because of a specific statement.
"At all times" means as long as the qualities brought about by rasāyana remain.

children.text: kecit tu yāvajjīvaṃ kulatthavarjanam āhuḥ yaduktaṃ suśrute tadbhāvitaḥ kapotāṃśca kulatthāṃśca vivarjayet iti ||
children.translated_text: Some, however, say that horse gram should be avoided for life, as it is said in <s>Suśruta</s>: after being treated with that, one should avoid pigeons and horse gram.
He praises the <s>śilājatu</s> procedure with the passage beginning "there is no one."

children.text: āyurvedasamutthānīyo nāma rasāyanapādaḥ pāriśeṣyād ucyate āyurvedasamutthānam asminn astīti matvarthīyacchapratyayeṇāyurvedasamutthānīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The section on <s>rasāyana</s> called "The Arising of <s>Āyurveda</s>" is so called by implication from what remains. Since the arising of <s>Āyurveda</s> is in this section, it is called <s>Āyurvedasamutthānīya</s>, with the possessive suffix <s>ccha</s>.
The settled life and wandering life of the seers are due to their adopting particular kinds of practice.
They are called <s>sāmpannikāḥ</s> because they are used after something has been prepared.
"Not excessively well" means not completely free from disease.
<s>Itikartavyatā</s> means procedure or activity.
The statement of synonyms of <s>Indra</s> is for the sake of praise; and this praise is because <s>Indra</s> revealed <s>Āyurveda</s>.
"Connected with discomfort" means that discomfort in the form of disease follows after it; therefore it is connected with discomfort.
"Root" means cause.

children.text: kṛtaḥ prajānāmanugraha iti grāme sthitvā āyurvedoktārogyasādhanadharmādiprakāśanena prajānugrahaḥ kṛta evetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Benefit has been done for creatures" means that, by staying in a village and revealing the means of health, <s>dharma</s>, and the like taught in <s>Āyurveda</s>, benefit for creatures has indeed been done.
This word is to be construed with both words denoting time.
The division of the sentence is: "To <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>."
The construction is: "having regarded the life span of creatures as short and so on."
"Because of the shortness of life" is to be supplied.

children.text: alpastapaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ saṃcayo'smin alpe āyuṣi tat tathā ||
children.translated_text: The accumulation of austerity and the like is small in this short life; thus it is described in that way.
The word <s>prati</s> is connected separately with friendliness and the other qualities.
The word <s>atha</s> marks the topic.

children.text: tena maitrīkāruṇyādīnyadhikṛtya yaṃ brahmā prajāpataye'dāt tamanuśrotum arhateti yojanā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the construction is: "With respect to friendliness, compassion, and the rest, you deserve to hear the teaching that <s>Brahmā</s> gave to <s>Prajāpati</s>."

children.text: yadyapi ca ṛṣayo bharadvājadvārā indrādadhigatāyurvedāḥ tathāpi grāmyavāsakṛtamanoglānyā na tathā sphuṭārtho vartata iti śaṅkayā punarindras tānupadiśati ||
children.translated_text: Although the seers had learned <s>Āyurveda</s> from <s>Indra</s> through <s>Bharadvāja</s>, still, because of the mental weariness produced by living in villages, it is suspected that the meaning is not so clear to them; therefore <s>Indra</s> teaches them again.
<s>Mahāśrāvaṇī</s> is <s>alambuṣā</s>.
<s>Aticchatrā</s> is <s>madhurikā</s>.
The divine herbs beginning with <s>brahmasuvarcalā</s>, having the characteristics already stated, are not very well known.
Some describe <s>ādityaparṇī</s> as simply <s>sūryāvarta</s> born in a particular region.

children.text: aśvabaleti jñāyata iti ṛṣibhirevānena nāmnā jñāyate nalaukikaiḥ lokāprasiddhatvāt ||
children.translated_text: "It is known as <s>aśvabalā</s>" means that it is known by this name only among the seers, not among ordinary people, because it is not widely known in the world.

children.text: soma iva vardhate hīyata iti yathāsomavṛddhikṣayau tathā tatkālameva tasya vṛddhikṣayau bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "It grows and diminishes like <s>soma</s>" means that, just as <s>soma</s> has increase and decrease, so its increase and decrease occur at that very time.

children.text: pralīyata iti druto bhavati anye tu mūrchatīti varṇayanti ||
children.translated_text: "It dissolves" means it becomes liquid. Others, however, explain it as "it becomes faint."
"Restoration" means that it is to be connected with the taking of food.
"Belonging to all speech" means all particular sentences.

children.text: etaddivyaṃ rasāyanamṛṣibhistadvidhair vā sevyam iti darśayann āha divyānām ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Showing that this divine <s>rasāyana</s> is to be used by the seers or by those who know it, he says, "of the divine," and so on.

children.text: viṣayābhijā iti svocitapuṇyadeśe jātā ityarthaḥ apuṇye tu deśe divyauṣadhijanmaiva na bhavati bhavantyo 'pi nirvāryā bhavantīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Born in their proper regions" means born in a meritorious land suited to them. But in an unmeritorious land divine herbs do not arise at all; even if they do arise, they are to be rejected. This is the idea.

children.text: samprati brahmasuvarcalādīnāṃ yathā mṛduvīryatvaṃ bhavati tadāha yās tv ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now he states how <s>brahmasuvarcalā</s> and the others become mild in potency, with the words beginning "but those which."
"By the qualities of the field" means by the properties of lands other than excellent regions such as the <s>Himālaya</s>.
"Of them" means of people other than the seers, such as forest-dwellers.

children.text: madhyamena ca karmaṇeti asamyakprayogeṇa kiṃvā anatimahatādṛṣṭena ||
children.translated_text: "And by middling action" means by improper application, or else by a not very great unseen merit.
In the passage beginning "of the strengthening substances," <s>joṅgaka</s> is <s>aguru</s>.
<s>Dvāradā</s> is the <s>śākataru</s>, or else <s>kapikacchu</s>.
<s>Śrīparṇī</s> is <s>gambhārī</s>.
<s>Palāśakṣāra</s> means water containing <s>palāśa</s> alkali.
"Very clean" means very thoroughly purified.
"Equal to the fire" means corresponding to the digestive fire.

children.text: ṣoḍaśīṃ mātrāmiti āmalakādicūrṇayuktaghṛtāpekṣayā ṣoḍaśabhāgo hemādicūrṇād grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "A sixteenth measure" means that, in relation to ghee mixed with powders such as <s>āmalaka</s>, one should take a sixteenth part of the powders such as gold.

children.text: kuṭīprāveśikarasāyanaviṣayān vātātapikarasāyanaviṣayāṃśca puruṣān āha samarthānām ityādi ||
children.translated_text: With the words beginning "of those who are capable," he describes persons who are suitable for <s>kuṭīprāveśika rasāyana</s> and those who are suitable for <s>vātātapika rasāyana</s>.
"Those who have time" means those who have made an opportunity.
It is called <s>sauryamārutika</s> because it is performed even through exposure to sun and wind.
In general he states the qualities of persons who are candidates for <s>rasāyana</s>, with the words beginning "truth-speaking."
One who sees beings with compassion is <s>karuṇavedī</s>.
"Unmixed" means one who does not eat mixed food.
One for whom the practice of <s>rasāyana</s> is constant is a perpetual practitioner of <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: manaḥśuddhyaiva prayatātmatāyāṃ labdhāyāṃ punas tadabhidhānam itaramānasaguṇeṣu prayatātmatāyā abhyarhitatopadarśanārtham ||
children.translated_text: Although self-purification is already obtained simply through purity of mind, the mention of it again is for the purpose of showing the superior importance of self-purification among the other mental qualities.

children.text: arujebhyo 'dvijātibhyo yeṣu ca puruṣeṣu śuśrūṣā nāsti teṣu caitan na vācyamiti yojanā ||
children.translated_text: The construction is: "This should not be spoken to people who are not healthy, who are not twice-born, and in whom there is no desire to listen and serve."

children.text: samprati rasāyanādisiddhir vaidyādhīnā tena vaidyastutim ārabhate ya ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now the success of <s>rasāyana</s> and the rest depends on the physician; therefore he begins the praise of the physician with the words beginning "he who."

children.text: prāṇācāryamityatra prāṇivaryam iti vā pāṭhaḥ tatra prāṇināṃ varyaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prāṇivaryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the word <s>prāṇācārya</s>, there is also the reading <s>prāṇivarya</s>. In that case, <s>prāṇivarya</s> means the best, the foremost, among living beings.
Because they carry the sacrifice, they are called <s>yajñavāhau</s>, "bearers of the sacrifice."
He shows this very status as bearers of the sacrifice with the words beginning "for of <s>Dakṣa</s>."
<s>Pūṣan</s> is the sun; <s>Bhaga</s> too is a particular form of the sun.

children.text: somābhipatita iti somābhipatanayogena pīḍita ityarthaḥ somātipacita iti vā pāṭhaḥ tatrāpyatipacanena somapānātiyogaṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: "Struck by <s>Soma</s>" means afflicted through the contact of <s>Soma</s>'s falling upon him. Or the reading is "overcooked by <s>Soma</s>"; there too, by the overcooking, he indicates an excessive use of soma-drinking.
"Cups" means vessels for drinking <s>soma</s>.

children.text: stotrāṇi stavāḥ stāvakavācaḥ śastrāṇīti kecit saṃśasyate 'neneti kṛtvā sāmaṛgvyatiriktaṃ stotramāhuḥ śastrāṇi astrāṇyeva vaṣaḍyuktāni śastrāṇi ca yajñe kalpyanta eva ||
children.translated_text: "Stotrāṇi" means praises, laudatory utterances. Some say that, because one is praised by means of it, a stotra is something other than a <s>sāman</s> and an <s>ṛg</s>. "Śastrāṇi" are weapons themselves; and śastras furnished with the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> are indeed prescribed in the sacrifice.

children.text: dhūmrāś ca paśava iti dhūmravarṇapaśavaḥ evaṃvarṇāś ca paśavaḥ śreṣṭhā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: "And smoky animals" means animals of smoky color; animals of this color are excellent.
"Savana" means a sacrificial place.
<s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> is a particular kind of sacrifice.
"Beyond one's capacity" means in excess even of one's own power.
He states the grounds for the use of the words "physician" and "twice-born" in the passage beginning "knowledge."

children.text: tena vidyāyogād vaidyatvaṃ tathā vidyāsamāptilakṣaṇajanmanā dvijatvaṃ bhavatītyuktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus it is said that one becomes a physician through the possession of knowledge, and likewise becomes twice-born through the birth characterized by the completion of learning.

children.text: brāhmaṃ vā ārṣaṃ vā iti vikalpo vaidyaviśeṣābhiprāyād bhavati tayor yo naiṣṭhikacikitsārthastasya brāhmam itarasya tu lokānugrāhiṇa ārṣamiti vyavasthā ||
children.translated_text: "Either <s>brāhma</s> or <s>ārṣa</s>" is an alternative with reference to a distinction among physicians: for the one whose aim is steadfast treatment, it is <s>brāhma</s>; but for the other, who benefits the world, it is <s>ārṣa</s>. This is the arrangement.
"Having promised" means having made a vow.
If treatment itself is merchandise to be sold, that is "treatment as merchandise."

children.text: te hitvetyādau dharmārthaṃ kriyamāṇacikitsā mahāphalatvena kāñcanarāśitulyā itarā tv asārakalpā pāṃśurāśitulyā ||
children.translated_text: In the passage beginning "having abandoned those," treatment undertaken for the sake of <s>dharma</s> is, because of its great fruit, like a heap of gold; the other kind, however, is as worthless as a heap of dust.
"The destruction belonging to <s>Vaivasvata</s>" means the house of <s>Yama</s>.
In the summary, "jewel elixir" means a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) combined with gold and other jewels.

children.text: āyurvedasamutthāne prakāśitatayā divyauṣadhividhyādi yaduvāca brahmacāribhyo'mareśvaraḥ tat saṃprakāśitam iti yojanā ||
children.translated_text: The construction is: what the lord of the immortals, having made it known in the origin of <s>āyurveda</s>, said to the celibate students concerning the procedure for divine medicines and the like, that has been fully explained.

children.text: svasthorjaskaratvasāmānyāt rasāyanamanu vājīkaraṇaṃ vācyaṃ tatrāpi vājīkaraṇe pravṛttyupadarśakaprakaraṇayuktatvād ādau saṃyogaśaramūlīya ucyate
children.translated_text: Because it shares with <s>rasāyana</s> the general property of strengthening the vital vigor of a healthy person, <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> (virility therapy) should be stated after <s>rasāyana</s>. And even there, in <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>, because it has a section that shows the inducement to undertake virility therapy, the section called <s>Saṃyogaśaramūlīya</s> is stated first.
Because the combination of the roots of <s>śara</s> is present in it, it is called <s>Saṃyogaśaramūlīya</s>.

children.text: avājī vājīvātyarthaṃ maithune śaktaḥ kriyate yena tad vājīkaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: That by which one who is not a stallion is made extremely capable, like a stallion, in sexual intercourse is <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>.

children.text: uktaṃ hi vājīvātibalo yena yātyapratihataḥ striyam ityādi ||
children.translated_text: For it has been said: "By means of which, being exceedingly strong like a stallion, he goes to a woman unhindered," and so on.

children.text: anvicchediti rasāyanānmahāphalāt tadapekṣayālpaphalaṃ vājīkaraṇaṃ paścād icchet ||
children.translated_text: "One should seek" means that, after <s>rasāyana</s>, which has great fruit, one should later desire <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>, whose fruit is smaller in comparison with it.

children.text: puruṣa iti padena taruṇapuruṣagrāhiṇā bālavṛddhau niṣiddhavyavāyau nirākaroti ||
children.translated_text: By the word "man," which denotes a young man, he excludes boys and old men, for whom sexual intercourse is forbidden.
For it has been said:
A very young boy, whose bodily elements are not all complete, when going to women,
would suddenly become afflicted, like collyrium in a pond.

children.text: śuṣkaṃ rūkṣaṃ yathā kāṣṭhaṃ jantujagdhaṃ vijarjaram
children.translated_text: As dry, rough wood, eaten by insects and worn out,

children.text: spṛṣṭamāśu viśīryeta tathā vṛddhaḥ striyo vrajan iti ||
children.translated_text: would quickly fall apart when touched, so too an old man when going to women.

children.text: nityam ityanena na rasāyanavat saṃprayogo vṛṣyasya kiṃtv āhāravat sarvadoṣayoga iti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By the word "always," he shows that the application of an aphrodisiac is not like that of <s>rasāyana</s>, but rather, like food, is suitable in every condition of the <s>doṣa</s>s.

children.text: ātmavānityanena durātmano vṛṣyakaraṇaṃ niṣedhati sa hi vṛṣyopayogādupacitadhātuḥ sann agamyāgamanamapi kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: By the word "self-controlled," he forbids giving aphrodisiacs to a bad-natured man. For, when his bodily elements have been increased through the use of aphrodisiacs, he might even approach women who should not be approached.

children.text: dharmādayo vṛṣyāyattā eva yathā bhavanti tadāha putrasyetyādi ||
children.translated_text: He explains how <s>dharma</s> and the other aims depend precisely on aphrodisiacs, with the passage beginning "of a son."
"Seat" means cause.

children.text: ete guṇā iti dharmādayaḥ vṛṣyaprayogajanitaḥ putro dharmādīn pituḥ sampādayatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "These qualities" means <s>dharma</s> and the rest. The meaning is that a son produced by the use of aphrodisiacs accomplishes <s>dharma</s> and the other aims for his father.

children.text: vājīkaraṇasevayā ceha yuktayaiva ṛtukāle ca maithunaṃ prādhānyenābhipretaṃ tena tisraiṣaṇīye traya upastambhāḥ ityādigranthena brahmacaryaṃ yaduktaṃ tad ṛtukāle yathāvidhikṛtamaithunāpratiṣedhakam iti na virodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the use of <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>, what is primarily intended here is only proper use and sexual intercourse in the fertile season. Therefore there is no contradiction with the statement in the chapter on the three desires that there are three supporting pillars, where celibacy is taught, because that statement does not forbid intercourse performed properly and according to rule in the fertile season.
He states the chief form of <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> among all aphrodisiacs, with the passage beginning "a stallion."
It is like a field, because the seed in the form of semen sprouts there.

children.text: arthā iti śabdādayaḥ te ca strīgatādhararasakalaviṅkarutarūpādayaḥ prasiddhā eva ||
children.translated_text: "Objects" means sound and the rest. These, such as the taste of a woman's lips, a sweet bird-like voice, and beauty, are well known.

children.text: dharmārthau strīṣviti sahaiva patnyā dharmaścarya ityādyupadeśād dharmaḥ tathānuraktā gṛhiṇī artharakṣaṇādi karotītyartha ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Dharma</s> and wealth are in women": <s>dharma</s> is there because of the teaching that one should practice <s>dharma</s> together with one's wife, and wealth is there because an affectionate housewife protects wealth and so forth. This is the meaning.

children.text: striyā lakṣmyāḥ saṃyoge dhanasampad bhavatīti strīṣu lakṣmīḥ pratiṣṭhitetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When a woman is joined with <s>Lakṣmī</s>, prosperity in wealth arises; therefore the meaning is that <s>Lakṣmī</s> is established in women.
"Compliant" means dependent.
"Educated" means trained in the sixty-four arts taught in the <s>Kāmaśāstra</s>, such as singing, instrumental music, and dance.

children.text: rūpādivyatirekeṇāpi kācit kasyacit karmavaśādvṛṣyā strī bhavatīti darśayannāha nānetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Showing that, even apart from beauty and the other qualities, some woman becomes aphrodisiac for some man because of the force of karma, he says the passage beginning "not variously."
"Through divine connection" means by the force of former karma.
"They increase" means that they produce aphrodisiac power.
"Hāva" is a particular amorous gesture of women directed toward a man.

children.text: uktaṃ ca bharatena prakāśarūpakaṃ sattvaṃ sattvotplavāḥ samudgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Bharata</s> has said: "Sattva, whose form is manifestation, and the upsurges of sattva arise."
"From them, the supreme seers say, comes the production of hāva and the rest."
"By fate" means from former karma.
"From action" means from an action in this life, such as rites of subjugation.
"Mental disposition" means desire.
"Having become a noose" means because it is the cause of bondage for the mind and senses.

children.text: nānābhāvā hi mānavāḥ ityanena rūpādiguṇayogena sarvapuruṣān prati strīṇāṃ priyatvamiti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By the statement "for human beings have various dispositions," he shows that, through the presence of beauty and other qualities, women are dear to all men.

children.text: samprati vṛṣyaprayogasādhyasya putrasyopādeyetāṃ darśayannāha acchāya ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, showing the desirability of the son who is to be attained through the use of aphrodisiacs, he speaks the passage beginning "without shade."
"Having one branch" means having one form.
A lamp drawn in a picture is a "picture-lamp."

children.text: adhātur dhātusaṃnibha iti asuvarṇādirūpaḥ suvarṇādivad ābhāsate yo jātuṣakaṅkaṇādiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "A non-metal resembling a metal" means something of a form other than gold and the like, such as a lac bracelet, which appears like gold and the like.
<s>Pūlī</s> is used because it has neuter gender.
By the expression "a straw <s>pūlī</s> in human shape," he shows that it lacks the activity proper to a human being.

children.text: kāmasukhāni cetyanena putrotpādātiriktaṃ nātiślāghyaṃ phalaṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: And by the phrase "pleasures of desire" he indicates a result other than the production of a son, one that is not especially praiseworthy.

children.text: kāmasukhāni hi aihikānyeva paraṃ na putravad ubhayalokopakārakāṇi ||
children.translated_text: For pleasures of desire are only of this world, and are not beneficial in both worlds as a son is.

children.text: upabhoge maithune sukhaṃ kurvantītyupabhogasukhāḥ kiṃvā upabhoktuṃ sukhā upabhogasukhāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Upabhogasukhāḥ</s> means that they produce pleasure in enjoyment, that is, in sexual intercourse; or else <s>upabhogasukhāḥ</s> means "easy to enjoy."
<s>Vīrya</s> means <s>śukra</s>, semen.
<s>Kāṇḍekṣu</s> means large sugarcane.
<s>Ikṣubālikā</s> means <s>khaggālikā</s>.
<s>Payasyā</s> means <s>kṣīravidārī</s>.
<s>Vīrā</s> means <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>.
<s>Phalgu</s> means <s>kāṣṭhodumbarikā</s>.
The division of the paste extends up to <s>śatāvarī</s>.

children.text: vaṃśarocanā tugākṣīrī anye vaṃśarocanānukāri pārthivadravyaṃ tāladhīti vadanti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaṃśarocanā</s> is <s>tugākṣīrī</s>. Others say that it is an earthy substance resembling <s>vaṃśarocanā</s>, called <s>tāladhī</s>.
"Congealed" means dense.
In the second preparation, "in the <s>rasa</s>" means in the decoction.
<s>Utkārikā</s> means a preparation shaped like a heap raised by mice.
With the lump-extracts of peacock, partridge, and goose, separately and together, there are four <s>piṇḍarasa</s> extracts.
By the word "at night" he indicates even intercourse throughout the whole night.

children.text: haṃsetyādi haṃsabarhidakṣāṇām aṇḍaprayogā yadyapi bhinnāḥ tathāpi prayogāpekṣayā eka evāyaṃ prayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The passage beginning with "goose" teaches the uses of the eggs of goose, peacock, and cock. Although they are distinct, from the standpoint of the procedure this is a single procedure.

children.text: evaṃ saṃgrahoktāḥ haṃsabarhidakṣāṇām ekaprayogeṇa pañcadaśaprayogāḥ pūryante ||
children.translated_text: Thus the fifteen procedures stated in the summary are completed by one procedure for goose, peacock, and cock.

children.text: vṛṣyayogāśca śuddhadehaireva kartavyā iti darśayannāha srotaḥsvityādi ||
children.translated_text: Showing that aphrodisiac formulations should be undertaken only by people whose bodies have been purified, he says the passage beginning "in the channels."
"Measured" means having the proper measure.
"Afflicted" means withered.

children.text: saṃgrahe yasya caiva yeti yasya yā vṛṣyetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the summary, "whose, and indeed which" means "whatever is aphrodisiac for whomever."
Because the naming of a vṛṣya section is under discussion, <s>āsiktakṣīrika</s> is stated as a component specifically connected with the final word.

children.text: āsiktakṣīramiti padam asty asminn iti āsiktakṣīrī tatra svārthikaḥ kapratyayaḥ kiṃvā ḍhakpratyayena vaiśeṣikaśabdavat āsiktakṣīrika iti sādhanīyam ||
children.translated_text: Since the word <s>āsiktakṣīra</s> exists in it, it is <s>āsiktakṣīrī</s>; there the affix <s>ka</s> has its own sense. Or else, like the word <s>vaiśeṣika</s>, <s>āsiktakṣīrika</s> should be derived with the affix <s>ḍhak</s>.
<s>Āsiktakṣīra</s> means grown by sprinkling with milk.
As has been said in <s>Jatūkarṇa</s>:
"Ripe <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice grown by sprinkling with milk," and so on.
"Pure <s>ṣaṣṭika</s>" means white <s>ṣaṣṭika</s>.

children.text: atra balādirasānāṃ tulyamānatāḥ kiṃvā mātrāśabdasyālpavacanatvād balādirasānām alpamātratvam ||
children.translated_text: Here the decoctions beginning with <s>balā</s> may have equal measures; or, because the word "measure" can denote a small amount, the decoctions beginning with <s>balā</s> may be in small quantities.

children.text: prakṣepyacūrṇapramāṇam āha yaiḥ sa sāndrībhaved rasa iti yāvanmānena cūrṇena rasasya sāndratā bhavati tāvanmātraṃ cūrṇaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: He states the amount of powder to be added with the phrase "by which that liquid becomes thick": as much powder as makes the liquid dense should be taken.
The abundance of honey and sugar should be understood as enough to make it extremely sweet.

children.text: atra ca prayogamahimnaiva madhuyuktasyāpi prayogasya bharjanakriyāyām agnisaṃyogo na virodham āvahati tathā hi suśrute 'pi triphalāyaskṛtau madhuno 'gnisambandho bhavatyeva ||
children.translated_text: Here, by the power of the procedure itself, even though the preparation contains honey, contact with fire in the act of frying does not create a contradiction. Thus, in <s>Suśruta</s> too, in the <s>triphalāyaskṛt</s> preparation, honey does indeed come into contact with fire.
"Self-born" means semen, the bodily product arising from exhilaration.
<s>Dakṣa</s> means a cock.

children.text: śukrāṇīti yadyapyuktaṃ tathāpi caṭakādiśukragrahaṇasyāśakyatvāt samānaguṇāni tadaṇḍānyapīha gṛhyante ||
children.translated_text: Although "semen" is stated, since collecting the semen of sparrows and the like is impossible, their eggs too, having similar qualities, are included here.
<s>Vartikā</s> means edible preparations shaped like wicks.
<s>Dhānā</s> means edible preparations shaped like grains.
Because the substances are the same, this is one formulation, even though it has the form of various edible preparations.
<s>Ajaḍā</s> means <s>śūkaśimbī</s>.

children.text: jīvaketyādau vidāryantaiḥ kalkaiḥ kṣīrajalābhyāṃ ghṛtaṃ sādhanīyam ||
children.translated_text: In the passage beginning with <s>jīvaka</s>, ghee should be prepared with milk and water, together with the pastes ending with <s>vidārī</s>.

children.text: yuktyeti yathā kaṭutvādyadhikaṃ na bhavati tathā maricādiyogaḥ kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "With proper reasoning" means that the addition of black pepper and the like should be made so that pungency and the other tastes do not become excessive.
"Rubbed" means well rubbed.
The definition of <s>rasālā</s> is: with <s>cāturjātaka</s>, <s>ajājī</s>, jaggery, fresh ginger, and dry ginger.

children.text: rasālā syācchikhariṇī sughṛṣṭaṃ sasaraṃ dadhi iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasālā</s> is <s>śikhariṇī</s>, well-rubbed curd together with its cream.
"Like moonbeams" means exceedingly white.
"Suitable here" means capable of use in an aphrodisiac procedure.
"By those seeking manhood" means by those seeking semen.
The connection with being nourished on <s>māṣaparṇī</s> too is as before.
<s>Gṛṣṭi</s> means a cow that has calved once.
By "four-teated" he indicates one fully possessing four teats.
"Red" means red in color.
From the statement it should be understood that upward-pointing horns belong only to a cow that is very pure and rich in milk.
<s>Ikṣvādā</s> means one that eats sugarcane stalks.
<s>Arjunādā</s> means one that eats leaves of the <s>arjuna</s> tree.

children.text: ikṣvādā vā arjunādā vā māṣaparṇabhṛtā veti vikalpatrayam ||
children.translated_text: Either one that eats sugarcane, or one that eats <s>arjuna</s>, or one nourished on <s>māṣaparṇī</s>: these are the three alternatives.
Milk either boiled or unboiled: these are two formulations.
That same milk mixed with sugar, honey, and ghee is the third.

children.text: etatprayogo'pi jatūkarṇe tasyāḥ kṣīraṃ śarkarākṣaudrayuktaṃ vā kevalaṃ śṛtamaśṛtaṃ veti ||
children.translated_text: This procedure too is found in <s>Jatūkarṇa</s>: her milk, either with sugar and honey, or plain, boiled or unboiled.

children.text: paryāyeṇeti pṛthak pṛthak prayoktavyaṃ tena pañcabhirgaṇaiḥ pañca yogā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: "In turn" means that they are to be applied separately; therefore, from the five groups there are five formulations.
"One should avoid" means that one should avoid the paste of <s>medā</s> and the rest.
An "old man" should be understood as one short of seventy years.

children.text: saptatikasya tu yadyapi śukranivṛttiruktā tathāpi vṛṣyaprabhāvād bhavatīti vijñeyam ||
children.translated_text: But although cessation of semen has been stated for a man in his seventies, still it should be understood that, through the efficacy of aphrodisiac treatment, it does occur.

children.text: jātarūpasyeti suvarṇasya maṇḍalarūpākṛtir iha suvarṇasya prabhāvādvṛṣyaprayogopakāriṇī bhavatīti vacanājjñeyam ||
children.translated_text: "Of <s>jātarūpa</s>" means of gold. The disk-shaped form of gold here becomes useful for the aphrodisiac application through the special efficacy of gold; this should be understood from the statement.
"Of that very one" means of the cow fed with <s>māṣaparṇā</s>.
A <s>prakuñca</s> is a <s>pala</s>.

children.text: kṣīradhārāvadohitā iti pippalīkalkād upari kṣīradhārāvadohaḥ kartavyaḥ kṣīraṃ ca tāvaddohyaṃ yāvatā pānayogyāḥ pippalyo bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: "Milked in a stream of milk" means that a stream of milk should be milked over the paste of <s>pippalī</s>; and only so much milk should be milked as makes the <s>pippalī</s>s fit for drinking.
The passage beginning "of the fruits" is meant.

children.text: phalānāmiti jīvanīyānām ityādibhis tribhiḥ pratyekam abhisaṃbadhyate ||
children.translated_text: "Of the fruits" is connected separately with each of the three expressions, "life-promoting" and so on.
"Of the life-promoting ones" means of the ten, beginning with <s>jīvaka</s> and <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, stated in the group of six decoction-classes.
"Of the unctuous ones" means of the ten substances, beginning with <s>mṛdvīkā</s>, that assist oleation and are stated in the group of seven decoction-classes.

children.text: tathā rucikāriṇām iti catuṣkakaṣāyavargoktānām āmrādīnāṃ hṛdyānāṃ daśānām iti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, "of those that produce relish" means of the ten heart-pleasing substances, beginning with mango, stated in the group of four decoction-classes.

children.text: eṣāṃ jīvanīyaprabhṛtīnāṃ phalānāṃ cūrṇitānāṃ militvā kuḍavo grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of these fruits beginning with the life-promoting group, powdered and combined, one <s>kuḍava</s> should be taken.
The rest has a very obvious meaning.

children.text: tathā hy ayaṃ prayogo jatūkarṇe ca paṭhyate drākṣākharjūramāṣājaḍāgodhūmaśālighṛtānāṃ kuḍavaḥ tilamudgau dvikauḍavikau cūrṇayitvā ityādi ||
children.translated_text: For this formulation is also recited in <s>Jatūkarṇa</s>: "a <s>kuḍava</s> of grapes, dates, <s>māṣa</s>, <s>ajaḍā</s>, wheat, <s>śāli</s> rice, and ghee, and two <s>kuḍava</s>s each of sesame and <s>mudga</s>; having powdered them," and so on.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ śatāvarītyādau śarkarādīnāṃ prakṣepyāṇām anyatodṛṣṭanyāyād ghṛtāt pādikatvaṃ ghṛtasya prāsthikatvam ||
children.translated_text: In the passage beginning "ghee, <s>śatāvarī</s>," by the rule seen elsewhere for ingredients to be added, sugar and the rest are one quarter of the ghee, and the ghee is one <s>prastha</s>.
There are fifteen formulations ending with the passage beginning "a <s>karṣa</s>."
But with the passage beginning "eating ghee and milk," diet and conduct are stated for one who desires aphrodisiac potency.

children.text: nityam ityanena vyavāyanityatayā śukramārgānavarodhena vyavāyaśaktiṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By the word "constantly," it indicates sexual capacity through the regularity of intercourse and through there being no obstruction in the channels of semen.

children.text: kṛtam ekaṃ kṛtyaṃ yaiste tathā etacca anyonyārtharāgakāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Those by whom the one required act has been done are so called; and this is the cause of mutual desire for one another.

children.text: siddhārthā iti siddhasādhyāḥ akṛtārthā hi vyākulamanaso na kāmakṣamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Having achieved their aim" means having an accomplished objective; for those whose aim is not accomplished, being disturbed in mind, are not capable of sexual pleasure.
"He becomes virile" means that he becomes one whose accumulated semen is inclined toward activity.

children.text: mattadvirephācaritāḥ ityādi gṛhāṇi ca ityantaṃ yogyatayā ṛtuvibhāgenānuktam api grīṣma eva jñeyaṃ meghānāṃ ityantaṃ prāvṛṣi tathā gandhina ityantaṃ śaradi vallabhā ityantaṃ ca vidhānaṃ hemantaśiśirayor jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: The passage beginning "frequented by intoxicated bees" and ending with "and houses," though not stated according to a division of the seasons, should, by suitability, be understood as applying in summer; the section ending with "of clouds" applies in the rainy season; that ending with "fragrant" applies in autumn; and the prescription ending with "beloved" should be understood as applying in winter and the cold season.

children.text: saṃkocaṃ kuṅkumaṃ saṃkocāguruṇoḥ samālabhanārthaṃ vallabhā yāsu niśāsu tās tathā ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Saṃkoca</s>" is saffron. The nights in which beloved women are present are nights for anointing with <s>saṃkoca</s> and <s>aguru</s>.
The prescription in the passage beginning "pleasant" is made with spring in mind, but it is not incompatible elsewhere also.
"Born from oneself" means <s>Manmatha</s>.
"The time in which passion has arisen" means a season such as spring.
By elimination, the expression "man and one whose strength has arisen, and so on" refers to a man whose strength and the like have arisen.

children.text: pumāñjātabalādayaḥ śabdā asmin vidyanta iti pumāñjātabalādikaḥ āsiktakṣīrikavacchabdasiddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The words "man," "one whose strength has arisen," and the like occur in this passage; hence the expression "man-whose-strength-has-arisen-and-so-on," just as the word <s>āsiktakṣīrika</s> is formed.

children.text: jātabalatve saty api nāvaśyam apatyabhāgitvaṃ bhavatīti vā yathā jātabalaḥ ityukte'pi yathā cāpatyavān bhavet yuktam ||
children.translated_text: Or, even when strength has arisen, it does not necessarily follow that there is a share in offspring; therefore, just as the statement "one whose strength has arisen" is possible, so too the statement "one possessing offspring" is proper.
He makes that very diversity of semen clear with the passage beginning "for not."

children.text: na hi jātabalāḥ sarve ityekaḥ pakṣaḥ tathā narā nāpatyabhāginaḥ sarva iti dvitīyaḥ pakṣo jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "For not all whose strength has arisen" is one position; likewise, "not all men have a share in offspring" should be understood as the second position.

children.text: etacchukrabalabhedaprasaṅgād aparānapi śukrabalaviśeṣān āha bṛhaccharīrā ityādi ||
children.translated_text: In connection with this distinction in the strength of semen, he states still other particular distinctions of seminal strength with the passage beginning "large-bodied."

children.text: alpāśrayā alpaśarīrāḥ ete ca śukrasāratvena narīṣu balavanto bahuprajāśca bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: "Of small support" means small-bodied. These, because their semen is excellent, are strong with women and have many offspring.
"They sprinkle like an elephant" means that they emit much semen.

children.text: kālayogena hemantādikālasambandhena vyavāye balavanto bhavantīti kālayogabalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through conjunction with time, that is, through association with seasons such as winter, they become strong in intercourse; therefore they are "strong through conjunction with time."
"Established through practice" means that they become capable of intercourse only through practice of intercourse.

children.text: evaṃ prayatnair vyajyanta iti vṛṣyaprayogaiḥ strīṣu pravartante ||
children.translated_text: "Thus they are made manifest by efforts" means that through aphrodisiac applications they become active toward women.
"Pleasurable enjoyments" means practices that are pleasant to perform.
Evacuative and unctuous enemas are mentioned because aphrodisiac applications bear fruit for those who have been purified by evacuative and unctuous enemas.
"Stiffened by rolling" means hardened by rolling.
That which is prepared with curd and pomegranate juice is called <s>dadhidāḍimasārika</s>.
And <s>dāḍimasāra</s> is pomegranate juice.
The passage beginning "of meats" is the second formulation by extension.
"Of the fattening ones" means of the fatty ones.
<s>Ajaḍā</s> is <s>śūkaśimbī</s>.

children.text: bhuktaḥ pītaśceti pūrvayogavad dhanabhāgasya bhojanaṃ dravasya ca pānaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: "Eaten and drunk" should be understood as in the previous formulation: the solid portion is to be eaten and the liquid is to be drunk.
By the word "fish," taking the principal case, they say that <s>rohita</s> is meant.
"Prepared with fruit juice" means prepared with the juice of fruits such as pomegranate and <s>āmalaka</s>.
"Pounded" means made into small pieces by pounding.
<s>Ikṣuraka</s> is <s>kokilākṣa</s>.
In the phrase "combined with sugar and honey," by the rule for added ingredients, the sugar and honey are each one quarter.
"In quarter-parts" means in measures of one quarter in relation to the ghee.
"Having scattered" means having spread out.

children.text: utkārikāḥ kāryā ityatra punaḥ pāke naivotkārikākaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: In the statement "<s>utkārikā</s>s are to be made," when there is further cooking, there is not actually a making of <s>utkārikā</s>s.
Gathering together aphrodisiac treatment that has not been explicitly stated, he says the passage beginning "whatever."

children.text: bhāvita iti vacanāt prayogeṇa śarīrabhāvanāyāṃ satyāṃ strīsevā sambhavatīti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: Because of the wording "conditioned," he shows that intercourse with women is possible when the conditioning of the body has taken place through application.
"By one's own impulse" means by one's own impulse born from resolve.

children.text: bālasya taḍāgadṛṣṭāntena punarapi śukrasadbhāvaṃ kaphaprādhānyaṃ ca darśayati vṛddhasya tu jantujagdhatvādidṛṣṭāntena vinaṣṭasyāpunarbhāvaṃ śukrasya tathābhūyiṣṭhatāṃ ca darśayati ||
children.translated_text: By the analogy of a pond for a child, he again shows the presence of <s>śukra</s> (semen) and the predominance of <s>kapha</s>; but by the analogy of an old man, such as one eaten by creatures, he shows the non-return of semen once it has been destroyed and the predominance of that state in him.

children.text: nanu tṛptasya śarīrabalaṃ bhavatyeva tat kiṃ tṛptasya striyo gantumasāmarthyam ityāha dehetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Objection: a satisfied man certainly has bodily strength; so why is there incapacity in a satisfied man to go to women? To this he says the passage beginning "of the body."

children.text: etena satyapi tṛptijanite bale kṣayādinā dehamanasor upahatatvāddharṣo na bhavati harṣābhāvād vyavāyaśaktir na bhavatītyuktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By this it is said that, although there is strength produced by satisfaction, because the body and mind are impaired by wasting and the like, excitement does not arise; and because excitement is absent, the capacity for intercourse does not exist.

children.text: samprati sambhavati śukraṃ yathā dehe sthitaṃ yathā ca pravartate tadāha rasa ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now he states how <s>śukra</s>, being present in the body, is possible, and how it comes into motion, with the passage beginning "rasa."
By the three analogies beginning with sugarcane, he shows in order men whose semen is carried outward with very little effort, with little effort, and with great effort.

children.text: saṃsparśana iti saṃsparśanavati tena keśādau saṃsparśanāvyāpteḥ śukramapi nāstīti darśayati ||
children.translated_text: "In contact" means possessing contact; by that he shows that, since contact does not pervade such things as hair, semen also is not present there.
The union of woman and man is their mingling together.

children.text: ceṣṭā vyavāyaceṣṭā saṃkalpo yoṣidanurāgaḥ pīḍanaṃ nārīpuruṣayoḥ parasparasammūrchanam atra ca nārīpuruṣasaṃyogaḥ pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ tatsahakārīṇi ceṣṭādīni ||
children.translated_text: "Activity" is the activity of intercourse; "resolve" is desire for a woman; "pressing" is the mutual embracing of woman and man. Here the union of woman and man is the principal cause, and activity and the others are its auxiliaries.
By the analogy of a wet cloth, he shows the flow of <s>śukra</s> without injury to its support.
He states yet another cause for the movement of <s>śukra</s> with the passage beginning "from excitement."
"Excitement" is a desire, preceded by resolve, that produces overflow of <s>śukra</s>, erection of the penis, and the like.
"Thirst" is longing for a woman.
"Fluidity" is instability.
"The state of tending toward minuteness" is, when there is subtlety, the natural disposition to go outward.

children.text: drutatvān mārutasya ceti śukraprerakasya vāyor abhidravaṇaśīlatvād ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "And because of the speed of the wind" means because the <s>vāyu</s> (wind) that impels <s>śukra</s> has the character of rushing forward.

children.text: ete ca yadyapi hetavastathāpi prādhānyāt prathamapratipāditastrīpuruṣasaṃyogādirūpahetūnāṃ samaṣṭau naivāmī gaṇitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Although these too are causes, nevertheless, because of the predominance of the causes first explained, whose form is the union of woman and man and so forth, these have not been counted in the aggregate.
"Moving" means wandering among various species, such as human beings and animals.
"Having every form" means the self.

children.text: tathā hy ātmaparyāyeṣūktaṃ viśvakarmā sa ca viśvarūpaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: For among the synonyms of <s>ātman</s> it has been said: "<s>Viśvakarmā</s>, and he is also <s>viśvarūpa</s>."
"The substance of form" means the antecedent cause of form.

children.text: etena avyaktasyātmano vyaktaśarīranirvṛttau śukraṃ hetur ityuktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By this it is said that, in the production of the manifest body of the unmanifest self, <s>śukra</s> is the cause.

children.text: śukraṃ ceha prakaraṇāgatatvenoktaṃ tena ārtavamapyātmano rūpadravyaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Here <s>śukra</s> has been mentioned because it belongs to the present topic; therefore <s>ārtava</s> (menstrual blood) too should be understood as the substance of the self's form.
He states the qualities of excellent <s>śukra</s> with the passage beginning "thick."
He states the etymology of the word <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> with the passage beginning "by which."

children.text: vrajeccābhyadhikam iti punaḥ punargacchet vyajyate iti vā pāṭhaḥ tatrāpi bhūyo gamanena nārīṣu puṃstvena vyajyate ||
children.translated_text: "And he would go excessively" means he would go again and again. Or the reading is "he is manifested"; there too, through going repeatedly, his masculinity is manifested among women.

children.text: vyajyāt iti pāṭhe'pi sa evārtho vidvadbhiḥ sucintanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even with the reading "he should manifest," that same meaning is to be carefully considered by the learned.

children.text: anena niruktena trividhamapi vṛṣyamavarudhyate yathā śukravṛddhikaraṃ ca māṣādi tathā srutikaraṃ saṃkalpādi śukrasrutivṛddhikaraṃ kṣīrādi ||
children.translated_text: By this etymology all three kinds of <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac) are included: that which increases <s>śukra</s>, such as black gram and the like; that which causes flow, such as resolve and the like; and that which causes both flow and increase of <s>śukra</s>, such as milk and the like.
As has been said elsewhere: some substance causes the flow of <s>śukra</s>, and some increases <s>śukra</s>.
Some substance causes both flow and increase; <s>vṛṣya</s> is said to be threefold.

children.text: trividhamapi hīdaṃ vyavāye balavattvaṃ punaḥ punarvyavāyaśaktiṃ ca karoti ||
children.translated_text: For all three of these produce strength in intercourse and the capacity for intercourse again and again.
The passage beginning "cause" and so on.
The summary is clear.
